<p align="center" style="text-align:center"><b>Fig. 26.</b> SRAM-PUF cell bit-error rate against temperature (schematic, recorded run; enrolment: one power-up at 25 °C). Circles: SKY130 Monte Carlo (bars: 95 % bootstrap intervals over cells). Lines: the cell model s(T) = s<sub>25</sub>(1 + a·|T − 25 °C|) with maximum-likelihood (solid), BER-matched (dashed) and the parameters assumed before the SKY130 simulations (dash-dotted). Shaded: outside the specified 0–85 °C range.</p>

**Result (model fit).** The BER-matched fit gives s<sub>25</sub> = 0.0205 ± 0.0045, a = 0.0228 per °C and P(1) = 0.496 for the schematic cell. With this s<sub>25</sub>, the relation BER ≈ 0.45·s<sub>25</sub> predicts 0.92 % at 25 °C, against the 0.91 % simulated. The temperature coefficient is about 14 times the 0.0016 per °C that the kT dependence of the noise alone would give. Together with the rise of the BER below 25 °C (1.9 standard errors), this is consistent with both conditions of the prediction: the temperature behaviour appears to be governed by the change of the mismatch weights, not by kT. The simulated noise-to-mismatch ratio is **2.9 times smaller** than the illustrative s<sub>25</sub> = 0.06 assumed before the SKY130 simulations (Fig. 26). In Fig. 26, the BER-matched model reproduces the simulation at 25 °C (0.92 % against 0.91 %), but lies above it at −40 °C (1.74 % against 1.34 %) and below it at 85 °C (1.68 % against 2.31 %); both model values lie inside the 95 % intervals of the simulation (0.81–1.98 % and 1.57–3.11 %), but at opposite ends. The maximum-likelihood model, which fits the counts of ones rather than the error rates, shows the same pattern (1.57 % at −40 °C and 1.53 % at 85 °C), and the prior illustrative model lies well above the simulation at every temperature (2.70 % at 25 °C).

**Interpretation.** The law s(T) = s<sub>25</sub>(1 + a·|T − 25 °C|) is symmetric in |T − 25 °C|: it predicts nearly the same error rate 65 °C below and 60 °C above the enrolment, whereas the simulated cell flips less often at −40 °C than at 85 °C. A noise-only law with one temperature coefficient therefore **cannot follow both −40 and 85 °C**: a fit to all three temperatures overestimates the error rate at −40 °C and underestimates it at 85 °C, the end of the specified range that sizes the code. The excess at 85 °C is mainly *reproducible flips*, cells whose mismatch changes sign with temperature and which therefore power up to the opposite value every time, an effect that Section VII-F counts directly in the recorded simulations and that a noise-only law cannot represent. For the extracted cell of Section VII-D, the underestimate is larger: its law gives 1.75 % at 85 °C against 3.14 % simulated, outside the 95 % interval of the simulation (2.20–4.11 %). This is why Section VII-E sizes the BCH code from the simulated error rates at each temperature, not from the law, and keeps the law only for comparison. A noise-to-mismatch ratio of about 0.02 means that only about 2 % of the cells lie close enough to their decision boundary to be affected by noise; for the 600-cell fingerprint this gives about 5 flipped bits per power-up at 25 °C, and about 14 at 85 °C (2.31 % of 600), which a BCH code with t of a few tens can correct. The statistical uncertainty is not negligible (the standard error of s<sub>25</sub> is 22 % of its value), and the simulated noise is thermal only, so Section VII-E checks the code against the illustrative s<sub>25</sub> = 0.06 as well, about three times the simulated value. These are schematic values; the model's parameters are fitted to the extracted cell, whose Monte Carlo follows in Section VII-D.

**Limitations: ageing and data remanence (not simulated).** Two effects that silicon studies of SRAM PUFs report are outside this transistor-level model, and the notebook makes no quantitative claim about them. *Ageing:* negative-bias temperature instability (NBTI) shifts the threshold voltage of a pMOS transistor while it is on; in an SRAM cell that holds its power-up value, the stressed pMOS is the one that pulls up the preferred node, so the shift weakens the cell's own mismatch, and silicon studies report that the power-up error rate grows over the lifetime of the chip (R. Maes and V. van der Leest, "Countering the effects of silicon aging on SRAM PUFs," *IEEE HOST*, 2014, who also propose writing the inverted power-up value into the array to reverse the stress). The PDK used here has no ageing model, so the drift term of the behavioural model (`puf_age_drift` = 0.03 per √year in Section V) is an assumption that no simulation in this notebook determines; the key-failure probabilities of Sections VII-E and XI hold for a fresh chip only. *Data remanence:* an SRAM cell keeps its content for a while after the supply is removed, longer at low temperature, so a power-up after a short off-time reproduces the last written data rather than the fingerprint [13]. Every simulated power-up starts with all nodes at 0 V, which assumes a fully discharged array; a product must enforce a minimum off-time or actively discharge the supply before the key is reconstructed. Neither the remanence time of this cell nor the ageing drift has been characterised here.

### D. Post-layout extraction

**Goal.** Draw both cells in SKY130, verify them, extract their parasitics and simulate them again, to find out whether the layout changes any of the values simulated in Sections VII-B and C, and to obtain the values to which the model's parameters are fitted.

**Theory: why extraction matters.** A schematic simulation knows the transistors but not the wires. The layout adds wiring capacitance to every node, coupling capacitance between nodes, and, wherever the two halves of a differential circuit are not drawn identically, an asymmetry that acts in the same direction on every chip. Each of these touches a quantity measured above:

* **Comparator noise and offset.** Both are set during the integration phase, through the capacitance C<sub>P</sub> of d<sub>p</sub> and d<sub>n</sub> (σ<sub>n</sub><sup>2</sup> ∝ kT/C<sub>P</sub>, and T<sub>int</sub> ∝ C<sub>P</sub>). If the extracted C<sub>P</sub> matches the 1 fF of wiring the schematic assumed, σ<sub>n</sub> and σ<sub>os</sub> should not change beyond their statistical errors.
* **Systematic offset.** A capacitance difference ΔC between the two sides of the latch makes one side regenerate faster, which shifts the switching point of every chip by the same amount. In a mirror-symmetric layout the only asymmetry left is where the cross-coupling wires must cross the axis, so a small systematic offset, far below σ<sub>os</sub>, is expected.
* **Energy.** Every added wiring capacitance C<sub>w</sub> that switches each cycle costs C<sub>w</sub>V<sub>DD</sub><sup>2</sup> = 3.2 fJ per fF at 1.8 V. The schematic contained no clock wiring at all, so the clock energy should rise.
* **SRAM-PUF bias.** If q and q̄ carry different capacitances, the lighter node rises faster during the power-up and every cell leans towards the same value: P(1) ≠ 0.5, fewer secret bits per cell (the min-entropy −log<sub>2</sub> max(P(1), 1 − P(1)) decreases) and fingerprints of different chips that are more alike. A point-symmetric cell, whose two halves are the same shapes rotated by 180°, should give equal capacitances and P(1) = 0.5 within the sampling error.
* **SRAM-PUF noise and mismatch.** The extra node capacitance changes the noise and the race slightly; s<sub>25</sub> should stay within its statistical interval, while the few cells whose mismatch is smaller than the change may take a different noiseless value.

**Setup.** The flow has five steps for each cell.

1. **Drawing.** Both cells are drawn as code with the KLayout Python API, rectangle by rectangle on the SKY130 layers (diffusion, poly, contacts, the local interconnect li1 and the first metal met1, implants and n-well), with the design rule that each coordinate respects noted in the source, from the same device sizes as the schematics, and written to GDS. The SRAM cell is point-symmetric: half A (inverter A, pass gate A, node q) is drawn and rotated by 180° to form half B, and each inverter's gate poly runs out to a contact under the opposite storage node, so that the cross-couple needs no crossing wires. It follows the logic design rules, not the foundry's denser SRAM rules. The comparator core (M1–M11) is mirror-symmetric about its vertical axis, with the tail M7 on the axis and the clock routed up both sides; only the cross-couple cannot be mirrored, so its two li1 routes cross the axis at different heights, between the nMOS and pMOS rows.
2. **Design-rule check (DRC).** Magic checks each layout against the PDK's full SKY130 rule deck and counts the violations.
3. **Extraction.** Magic extracts the devices with their drawn source and drain areas and perimeters, and every parasitic capacitance (area, fringe and coupling, with no lower threshold). Wire resistance is not extracted. The longest internal route, the comparator's li1 cross-couple, is about 10 squares long; at li1's sheet resistance of about 12.8 Ω/□ that is about 130 Ω, plus a few contacts of the order of 100 Ω each. Against the about 1.3 fF the route drives, this gives an RC time constant below 1 ps, far below the regeneration time constant τ = 36 ps and the kilo-ohm resistance of the transistors; the met1 runs have a far lower sheet resistance.
4. **Layout versus schematic (LVS).** netgen compares the extracted devices and nets with a reference netlist of the schematic, using the PDK's setup file.
5. **Mapping onto the schematic.** The extracted devices and capacitors are renamed onto the schematic's transistors and nets: labelled nets are taken from the pins, and unlabelled internal nets (such as the comparator's tail) are inferred from the terminals of transistors whose gate net is already known. The extracted netlists thus keep the transistor names and order of the schematics, so the PDK draws the same mismatch for every device and the testbenches inject the same noise: the comparison is paired, cell by cell and instance by instance, and every difference is caused by the layout. The comparator's buffers and SR latch remain at schematic level.

The post-layout simulations use the settings and seeds of Sections VII-B and C. Because a full post-layout Monte Carlo requires about 40 minutes on two cores, the results are shown by default from recorded runs of the same code and seeds: the SRAM cell's Monte Carlo of 1,024 cells × 8 power-ups × 3 temperatures (`dev/spice_puf/demo_postlayout.py`), whose fit sets the model's parameters, and the comparator's noise, offset (the same 96 instances) and energy. Setting `PEX_LIVE = True` in the waveform cell of Section VII-C re-runs both checks live: the SRAM cell's first 128 cells × 5 power-ups (about 105 s), which are then compared bit for bit with the record, and the comparator's three measurements (about 50 s); `PUF_MODE = "full"` re-runs the complete SRAM Monte Carlo. The layout drawing, DRC, extraction and LVS of both cells, and the waveform comparison of Fig. 31, always run live.

> **Next cell.** 1. Writes the layout flow shared by both circuits to `sky130_layout.py`; no tool is run. The flow covers GDS out of KLayout, DRC and extraction with Magic, LVS with netgen, and the mapping of an extraction back onto the schematic's transistors and nets, which finds unlabelled internal nets (such as the comparator's tail) from the transistors' terminals.


```python
%%writefile sky130_layout.py
"""SKY130 layout flow shared by the SRAM-PUF cell (puf_layout.py) and the StrongARM comparator (comparator_layout.py).

  write_gds      boxes and pin labels -> GDS, with the KLayout Python API (pip package `klayout`, headless in Colab)
  render         the same boxes plotted with matplotlib, coloured like KLayout's SKY130 layer set
  drc            Magic with the PDK's full SKY130 rule deck
  extract        Magic extraction: devices with drawn source/drain areas and perimeters, and every parasitic
                 capacitance (area, fringe and coupling; cthresh 0).  Wire resistance is not extracted: the li1 and
                 met1 runs here are a few squares, ohms against transistors of kilo-ohms and more.
  lvs            netgen with the PDK's setup file
  map_extraction extracted devices and capacitors renamed onto a schematic's transistors and nets, found from the
                 labelled nets and the transistors' terminals (internal nets such as a tail node are inferred)

Shapes are (layer, x0, y0, x1, y1) in nm; pins are (pin layer, text, (x0, y0, x1, y1)).  Text on a pin layer
(li1 67/16, met1 68/16) becomes a subcircuit port in Magic.
"""
import os
import re
import subprocess

# GDS (layer, datatype) of the SKY130 layers used here
GDS = dict(nwell=(64, 20), diff=(65, 20), tap=(65, 44), poly=(66, 20), licon=(66, 44), npc=(95, 20),
           li=(67, 20), li_pin=(67, 16), mcon=(67, 44), met1=(68, 20), met1_pin=(68, 16),
           nsdm=(93, 44), psdm=(94, 20))

# Display colours for `render` (close to the KLayout SKY130 layer properties), drawn bottom to top
STYLE = [("nwell", "#7f7f7f", 0.12), ("psdm", "#d9a400", 0.10), ("nsdm", "#2a9d8f", 0.10), ("npc", "#9b5de5", 0.10),
         ("diff", "#2e8b57", 0.55), ("tap", "#1f6f43", 0.55), ("poly", "#d62828", 0.55), ("licon", "#111111", 0.9),
         ("li", "#457b9d", 0.40), ("mcon", "#6a4c93", 0.9), ("met1", "#1d3557", 0.25)]


def write_gds(shapes, pins, path, name):
    """Write boxes and pins to GDS with KLayout (database unit 1 nm).  Returns dict(path, name, bbox_um)."""
    import klayout.db as kdb
    ly = kdb.Layout()
    ly.dbu = 0.001
    top = ly.create_cell(name)
    idx = {k: ly.layer(*v) for k, v in GDS.items()}
    for layer, x0, y0, x1, y1 in shapes:
        top.shapes(idx[layer]).insert(kdb.Box(x0, y0, x1, y1))
    for layer, text, (x0, y0, x1, y1) in pins:
        top.shapes(idx[layer]).insert(kdb.Box(x0, y0, x1, y1))
        top.shapes(idx[layer]).insert(kdb.Text(text, kdb.Trans((x0 + x1) // 2, (y0 + y1) // 2)))
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), exist_ok=True)
    ly.write(path)
    bb = top.bbox()
    return dict(path=path, name=name, bbox_um=(bb.left / 1000, bb.bottom / 1000, bb.right / 1000, bb.top / 1000))


def extent(shapes, layers=("diff", "tap", "poly", "li", "met1")):
    """Width, height and area (um) of the drawn shapes on the given layers (implant and well margins excluded)."""
    core = [s for s in shapes if s[0] in layers]
    w = (max(s[3] for s in core) - min(s[1] for s in core)) / 1000
    h = (max(s[4] for s in core) - min(s[2] for s in core)) / 1000
    return dict(width_um=w, height_um=h, area_um2=w * h)


def render(shapes, pins, ax=None, path=None, title=None, figsize=(3.3, 6.2), legend=True, pin_size=7.5):
    """Plot the layout with matplotlib, one patch per drawn box."""
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle, Patch
    own = ax is None
    if own:
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    for layer, color, alpha in STYLE:
        for s in shapes:
            if s[0] == layer:
                x0, y0, x1, y1 = (v / 1000 for v in s[1:])
                ax.add_patch(Rectangle((x0, y0), x1 - x0, y1 - y0, fc=color, ec=color, lw=0.4, alpha=alpha))
    for _, text, (x0, y0, x1, y1) in pins:
        ax.text((x0 + x1) / 2000, (y0 + y1) / 2000, text, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=pin_size,
                color="white", fontweight="bold", bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.15", fc="#131c28", ec="none", alpha=0.75))
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.autoscale_view()
    ax.set_xlabel("x (µm)")
    ax.set_ylabel("y (µm)")
    ax.grid(False)
    if title:
        ax.set_title(title)
    if legend:
        handles = [Patch(fc=c, ec=c, alpha=min(1, a + 0.25), label=n) for n, c, a in STYLE]
        ax.legend(handles=handles, loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1.0), fontsize=7.5, frameon=False)
    if own and path:
        fig.savefig(path, dpi=200, bbox_inches="tight")
    return ax


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Magic and netgen
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def tool_config(pdk_root, magic="magic", netgen="netgen", workdir="layout_work"):
    tech = os.path.join(pdk_root, "sky130A", "libs.tech")
    return dict(pdk_root=os.path.abspath(pdk_root), magic=magic, netgen=netgen, workdir=os.path.abspath(workdir),
                magicrc=os.path.join(tech, "magic", "sky130A.magicrc"),
                netgen_setup=os.path.join(tech, "netgen", "sky130A_setup.tcl"))


def _run_magic(tcfg, script, name):
    wd = tcfg["workdir"]
    os.makedirs(wd, exist_ok=True)
    tcl = os.path.join(wd, name + ".tcl")
    with open(tcl, "w") as f:
        f.write(script + "\nquit -noprompt\n")
    env = dict(os.environ, PDK_ROOT=tcfg["pdk_root"])
    p = subprocess.run([tcfg["magic"], "-dnull", "-noconsole", "-rcfile", tcfg["magicrc"], tcl],
                       cwd=wd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900, env=env)
    log = p.stdout + p.stderr
    with open(os.path.join(wd, name + ".log"), "w") as f:
        f.write(log)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"magic failed ({name}, rc={p.returncode}); see {os.path.join(wd, name + '.log')}")
    return log


def _load(gds, name):
    return f"gds read {os.path.abspath(gds)}\nload {name}\nselect top cell\n"


def drc(tcfg, gds, name):
    """Magic DRC with the full SKY130 deck.  Returns dict(count, errors=[(rule, n_boxes)])."""
    log = _run_magic(tcfg, _load(gds, name) + "drc style drc(full)\ndrc check\ndrc catchup\n"
                     "set n [drc list count total]\nputs \"DRCCOUNT $n\"\n"
                     "foreach {why boxes} [drc listall why] { puts \"DRCERR [llength $boxes] $why\" }\n", f"drc_{name}")
    m = re.search(r"DRCCOUNT (\d+)", log)
    if not m:
        raise RuntimeError(f"magic DRC gave no count; see drc_{name}.log")
    errors = [(l.split(" ", 2)[2], int(l.split(" ", 2)[1])) for l in log.splitlines() if l.startswith("DRCERR ")]
    return dict(count=int(m.group(1)), errors=errors)


def extract(tcfg, gds, name):
    """Magic extraction.  Writes <name>_lvs.spice (devices only, for LVS) and <name>_pex.spice (devices and all
    parasitic capacitances) in the work directory and returns their paths."""
    wd = tcfg["workdir"]
    base = _load(gds, name) + "extract do local\nextract do capacitance\nextract do coupling\nextract all\n"
    _run_magic(tcfg, base + f"ext2spice lvs\next2spice -o {name}_lvs.spice\n", f"extract_lvs_{name}")
    _run_magic(tcfg, base + "ext2spice format ngspice\next2spice cthresh 0\next2spice rthresh 0\n"
               f"ext2spice -o {name}_pex.spice\n", f"extract_pex_{name}")
    return dict(lvs=os.path.join(wd, f"{name}_lvs.spice"), pex=os.path.join(wd, f"{name}_pex.spice"))


def write_schematic(devices, ports, path, name):
    """A reference netlist for LVS: devices as (name, kind 'nfet'/'pfet', d, g, s, b, w, l)."""
    lines = [f".subckt {name} " + " ".join(ports)]
    lines += [f"X{n} {d} {g} {s} {b} sky130_fd_pr__{k}_01v8 w={w:g} l={l:g}" for n, k, d, g, s, b, w, l in devices]
    lines += [f".ends {name}", ""]
    with open(path, "w") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines))
    return path


def lvs(tcfg, layout_spice, schematic_spice, name):
    """netgen LVS with the PDK setup.  Returns dict(match, report)."""
    wd = tcfg["workdir"]
    rpt = os.path.join(wd, f"lvs_{name}.rpt")
    cmd = [tcfg["netgen"], "-batch", "lvs", f"{layout_spice} {name}", f"{schematic_spice} {name}", tcfg["netgen_setup"], rpt]
    p = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=wd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
    with open(os.path.join(wd, f"lvs_{name}.log"), "w") as f:
        f.write(p.stdout + p.stderr)
    text = open(rpt).read() if os.path.exists(rpt) else p.stdout
    return dict(match="Circuits match uniquely" in text and "Netlists do not match" not in text, report=rpt)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# From the extraction to a simulation netlist
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _um(v):
    v = v.lower()
    for suf, m in (("u", 1.0), ("n", 1e-3), ("p", 1e-6)):
        if v.endswith(suf):
            return float(v[:-1]) * m
    x = float(v)
    return x * 1e6 if x < 1e-3 else x


def parse_pex(path):
    """Devices and capacitors of a Magic ngspice-format extraction: (ports, devices, caps), devices as
    dict(name, d, g, s, b, kind, w, l, params) and caps as (node1, node2, farads)."""
    text = open(path).read().replace("\n+", " ")
    ports, devices, caps = None, [], []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        t = line.split()
        if not t or t[0].startswith("*"):
            continue
        low = t[0].lower()
        if low == ".subckt":
            ports = t[2:]
        elif low == ".option" and any(x.lower().startswith("scale=") for x in t):
            raise RuntimeError(f"unexpected {line!r} in {path}; the code assumes ext2spice scale off")
        elif low.startswith("x") and len(t) >= 6 and "sky130_fd_pr__" in t[5]:
            params = {k.lower(): v for k, v in (x.split("=", 1) for x in t[6:] if "=" in x)}
            kind = "pfet" if "pfet" in t[5] else "nfet"
            devices.append(dict(name=t[0], d=t[1], g=t[2], s=t[3], b=t[4], kind=kind, w=_um(params["w"]),
                                l=_um(params["l"]), params=params))
        elif low.startswith("c") and len(t) >= 4:
            v = t[3].lower()
            mult = {"f": 1e-15, "a": 1e-18, "p": 1e-12, "n": 1e-9}
            caps.append((t[1], t[2], float(v[:-1]) * mult[v[-1]] if v[-1] in mult else float(v)))
    return ports, devices, caps


def map_extraction(pex_path, schematic, labels):
    """Rename an extraction onto a schematic.

    schematic : [(name, kind, d, g, s, b, w, l)] in the order the simulation netlist uses
    labels    : {extracted net name: schematic net name} for the labelled nets (several may map to one net)
    Unlabelled internal nets are inferred from the terminals of transistors whose gate is already known.
    Returns dict(devices=[dict(name, kind, d, g, s, b, w, l, ad, as_, pd, ps)] in schematic order,
                 caps=[(net1, net2, farads)], node_cap={net: farads}, netmap)."""
    _, devs, caps = parse_pex(pex_path)
    netmap = dict(labels)
    taken = {}                                   # schematic net -> extracted net, for inferred nets only
    out = {}
    remaining = list(devs)
    while len(out) < len(schematic):
        progress = False
        for name, kind, d, g, s, b, w, l in schematic:
            if name in out:
                continue
            hits = []
            for ed in remaining:
                if ed["kind"] != kind or abs(ed["w"] - w) > 1e-6 or abs(ed["l"] - l) > 1e-6 or netmap.get(ed["g"]) != g:
                    continue
                for flip in (False, True):
                    ed_d, ed_s = (ed["s"], ed["d"]) if flip else (ed["d"], ed["s"])
                    pairs = [(ed_d, d), (ed_s, s), (ed["b"], b)]
                    if all(netmap.get(e, sn) == sn and taken.get(sn, e) == e for e, sn in pairs):
                        hits.append((sum(e in netmap for e, _ in pairs), flip, ed))
            if not hits:
                continue
            best = max(h[0] for h in hits)
            top = [h for h in hits if h[0] == best]
            if len(top) != 1:
                continue
            _, flip, ed = top[0]
            ed_d, ed_s = (ed["s"], ed["d"]) if flip else (ed["d"], ed["s"])
            for e, sn in ((ed_d, d), (ed_s, s), (ed["b"], b)):
                if e not in netmap:
                    netmap[e], taken[sn] = sn, e
            p = ed["params"]
            ad, as_ = (p.get("as"), p.get("ad")) if flip else (p.get("ad"), p.get("as"))
            pd_, ps = (p.get("ps"), p.get("pd")) if flip else (p.get("pd"), p.get("ps"))
            out[name] = dict(name=name, kind=kind, d=d, g=g, s=s, b=b, w=w, l=l, ad=ad, as_=as_, pd=pd_, ps=ps)
            remaining.remove(ed)
            progress = True
        if not progress:
            missing = [n for n, *_ in schematic if n not in out]
            raise RuntimeError(f"cannot match extracted devices to {missing}; unmatched: {[d['name'] for d in remaining]}")
    if remaining:
        raise RuntimeError(f"extracted devices left over: {[d['name'] for d in remaining]}")
    unknown = {n for a, b_, _ in caps for n in (a, b_) if n not in netmap}
    if unknown:
        raise RuntimeError(f"capacitors on nets that are not in the schematic: {sorted(unknown)}")
    caps = [(netmap[a], netmap[b_], v) for a, b_, v in caps]
    node_cap = {}
    for a, b_, v in caps:
        if a != b_:
            for n in (a, b_):
                node_cap[n] = node_cap.get(n, 0.0) + v
    return dict(devices=[out[n] for n, *_ in schematic], caps=caps, node_cap=node_cap, netmap=netmap)
```

    Overwriting sky130_layout.py


> **Next cell.** 1. Writes `puf_layout.py`, which draws the point-symmetric 6T cell, and 2. `comparator_layout.py`, which draws the mirror-symmetric StrongARM core, rectangle by rectangle, with the design rule each coordinate respects in the comments.


```python
%%writefile puf_layout.py
"""SKY130 6T SRAM-PUF cell: layout, DRC, extraction and LVS, for the post-layout Monte Carlo of puf_spice.py.

The cell is drawn with the KLayout Python API (pip package `klayout`, headless in Colab); the devices are those of
puf_spice.CELL (pull-down W = 0.64, pull-up and pass gate W = 0.42, all L = 0.15 um).  It is point-symmetric, like a
production bit cell: one half (inverter A, pass gate A, node q) is drawn and the other half is the same shapes rotated
by 180 degrees, so q and qb see identical wiring and the layout adds no systematic skew to the PUF.  The cross-couple
needs no crossing wires: each inverter's gate poly runs out as a branch to a contact under the opposite storage
node's li1 strap.  It is drawn with the logic (periphery) design rules, not the foundry's SRAM rules, so it is larger
than the foundry bit cell.  DRC, extraction and LVS (Magic, netgen) are in sky130_layout.py; `postlayout_cell` turns
the extraction into the `sram6t` subcircuit of puf_spice.cell_subckt, with the schematic's transistor names and order
so that the PDK's per-instance mismatch draws are unchanged.
"""
import sky130_layout as sl

NAME = "sram6t"
# the schematic of puf_spice.cell_subckt, in its device order: (name, kind, d, g, s, b, w, l)
def schematic(cell):
    c = cell
    return [("PUa", "pfet", "q", "qb", "vdd", "vdd", c["w_pu"], c["l"]), ("PDa", "nfet", "q", "qb", "0", "0", c["w_pd"], c["l"]),
            ("PUb", "pfet", "qb", "q", "vdd", "vdd", c["w_pu"], c["l"]), ("PDb", "nfet", "qb", "q", "0", "0", c["w_pd"], c["l"]),
            ("PGa", "nfet", "bl", "wl", "q", "0", c["w_pg"], c["l"]), ("PGb", "nfet", "blb", "wl", "qb", "0", c["w_pg"], c["l"])]

# labelled nets of the layout -> nets of the simulation subcircuit
LABELS = {"q": "q", "qb": "qb", "vdd": "vdd", "vss": "0", "bl": "bl", "blb": "blb", "wla": "wl", "wlb": "wl"}


def _half(cell):
    """Shapes of half A (inverter A drives q, pass gate A connects q to bl), in nm.  Returns a list of
    (layer, x0, y0, x1, y1).  Coordinates follow the design-rule budget in the comments; Magic's DRC is the check."""
    W = lambda k: int(round(cell[k] * 1000))
    wpd, wpu, wpg, L = W("w_pd"), W("w_pu"), W("w_pg"), W("l")
    assert L == 150 and wpd >= wpg, "geometry is laid out for L = 0.15 um and W_PD >= W_PG"
    yN, yP = -2170, 475                    # bottom of the nmos row (A), bottom of the pmos row (A)
    xa = -335                              # gate A (poly) left edge; its right edge is xa + L
    S = []
    add = lambda layer, *b: S.append((layer,) + tuple(int(v) for v in b))
    # nmos row: bl | PGa | q | PDa | vss; the PD part is wider and is reached 250 nm before the PDa gate
    xj = xa - 255                          # diffusion jog (>= 250 from PDa, >= 75 from the PGa poly)
    xpg = xj - 75 - L                      # PGa gate left edge
    add("diff", xpg - 290, yN, xj, yN + wpg)
    add("diff", xj, yN, xa + L + 290, yN + wpd)
    add("nsdm", xpg - 290 - 125, yN - 125, xa + L + 290 + 125, yN + wpd + 125)
    add("poly", xpg, yN - 450, xpg + L, yN + wpg + 130)                     # PGa gate, down to its word-line pad
    add("poly", xa, yN - 130, xa + L, yP + wpu + 130)                       # gate A: PDa and PUa
    # pmos row: q | PUa | vdd
    add("diff", xa - 300, yP, xa + L + 290, yP + wpu)
    add("psdm", xa - 300 - 125, yP - 125, xa + L + 290 + 125, yP + wpu + 125)
    # contacts on diffusion (licon 0.17, >= 0.055 from the gate, >= 0.06 inside the diffusion)
    add("licon", xpg - 230, yN + 125, xpg - 60, yN + 295)                  # bl
    add("licon", -570, yN + 125, -400, yN + 295)                            # q (nmos)
    add("licon", -125, yN + 235, 45, yN + 405)                              # vss
    add("licon", -570, yP + 125, -400, yP + 295)                            # q (pmos)
    add("licon", -125, yP + 125, 45, yP + 295)                              # vdd
    # q: one li1 strap joins the nmos and pmos drains and reaches the contact on gate B's branch
    ylic = 1290
    add("li", -570, yN + 45, -400, ylic + 250)
    add("poly", -650, ylic - 50, xa + L, ylic + 220)                        # pad and branch of gate B ...
    add("poly", -650, ylic + 10, -xa, ylic + 160)                           # ... running to gate B at x = -xa - L .. -xa
    add("licon", -570, ylic, -400, ylic + 170)
    add("npc", -670, ylic - 100, -300, ylic + 270)
    # word line: pad on the PGa poly below the nmos row
    yw = yN - 400                          # li1 pad >= 0.17 below the bit-line pad
    add("poly", xpg - 185, yw - 50, xpg + L, yw + 220)
    add("licon", xpg - 105, yw, xpg + 65, yw + 170)
    add("npc", xpg - 205, yw - 100, xpg + L + 20, yw + 270)
    add("li", xpg - 105, yw - 85, xpg + 65, yw + 255)
    # bit line pad
    add("li", xpg - 230, yN + 40, xpg - 60, yN + 380)
    # vss: li1 strap from the source down to a substrate tap
    add("li", -125, yN - 580, 45, yN + 485)
    add("tap", -245, yN - 560, 165, yN - 270)
    add("licon", -125, yN - 500, 45, yN - 330)
    add("psdm", -370, yN - 685, 290, yN - 125)
    # vdd: li1 pad, mcon and the met1 strap through the cell centre (shared with half B)
    add("li", -125, yP + 40, 45, yP + 380)
    add("mcon", -125, yP + 125, 45, yP + 295)
    add("met1", -185, -(yP + 355), 185, yP + 355)
    # n-well and its tap at the centre (both point-symmetric), tied to vdd
    add("nwell", xa - 300 - 180, -(yP + wpu + 180), -(xa - 300 - 180), yP + wpu + 180)
    add("tap", -125, -205, 125, 205)
    add("licon", -85, -85, 85, 85)
    add("nsdm", -250, -(yP - 125), 250, yP - 125)
    add("li", -85, -170, 85, 170)
    add("mcon", -85, -85, 85, 85)
    pins = [("li_pin", "q", (-570, -85, -400, 85)),
            ("li_pin", "bl", (xpg - 230, yN + 125, xpg - 60, yN + 295)),
            ("li_pin", "wla", (xpg - 105, yw, xpg + 65, yw + 170)),
            ("li_pin", "vss", (-125, yN - 500, 45, yN - 330))]
    return S, pins


def geometry(cell):
    """All shapes of the full cell and its pins: half A plus half A rotated by 180 degrees about the origin."""
    half, pins = _half(cell)
    rot = lambda b: (-b[2], -b[3], -b[0], -b[1])
    shapes = half + [(s[0],) + rot(s[1:]) for s in half]
    other = {"q": "qb", "bl": "blb", "wla": "wlb", "vss": "vss"}
    pins = pins + [(layer, other[name], rot(b)) for layer, name, b in pins]
    pins.append(("met1_pin", "vdd", (-185, -85, 185, 85)))
    return shapes, pins


def draw(path, cell):
    return sl.write_gds(*geometry(cell), path, NAME)


def cell_report(cell):
    return sl.extent(geometry(cell)[0])


def render(cell, **kw):
    return sl.render(*geometry(cell), **kw)


def drc(tcfg, gds):
    return sl.drc(tcfg, gds, NAME)


def extract(tcfg, gds):
    return sl.extract(tcfg, gds, NAME)


def schematic_netlist(cell, path):
    """LVS reference with the layout's port names (two word lines and vss, as drawn)."""
    lvs_names = {"0": "vss"}
    devs = []
    for n, k, d, g, s, b, w, l in schematic(cell):
        g = {"PGa": "wla", "PGb": "wlb"}.get(n, g)
        devs.append((n, k, lvs_names.get(d, d), g, lvs_names.get(s, s), lvs_names.get(b, b), w, l))
    return sl.write_schematic(devs, ["vdd", "vss", "bl", "blb", "wla", "wlb", "q", "qb"], path, NAME)


def lvs(tcfg, layout_spice, schematic_spice):
    return sl.lvs(tcfg, layout_spice, schematic_spice, NAME)


def postlayout_cell(pex_path, cell):
    """The extraction renamed onto puf_spice's sram6t: dict(devices, caps, node_cap, netmap)."""
    return sl.map_extraction(pex_path, schematic(cell), LABELS)
```

```python
%%writefile comparator_layout.py
"""SKY130 StrongARM comparator core (M1-M11 of comparator_spice.CORE): layout, DRC, extraction and LVS.

Drawn with the KLayout Python API, mirror-symmetric about x = 0 in the textbook arrangement, from the bottom up:
substrate taps under the ground rail; the clocked tail M7 on the axis; the input pair M1/M2 (4/0.5 um); the
latch nMOS M3/M4 above them, sharing the dp/dn wires; the n-well with the latch pMOS M5/M6 and the reset devices
M8-M11, its tap and the vdd rail at the top.  All gates are horizontal (W along x).  The only part that cannot be
mirrored is the cross-couple: outp has to reach the left gates and outn the right gates, so the two li1 routes
cross the axis at different heights (over the gate polys, which they do not contact).  The extraction shows what
that one asymmetry costs as a systematic offset.  The output buffers and the SR latch are not drawn: they stay at
schematic level in the simulation (their gate loads are in their device models).
"""
import sky130_layout as sl

NAME = "strongarm"
LABELS = {"inp": "inp", "inn": "inn", "clk": "clk", "vdd": "vdd", "vss": "0", "outp": "outp", "outn": "outn"}
PORTS = ["inp", "inn", "clk", "vdd", "vss", "outp", "outn"]


def schematic(core, sizes):
    """comparator_spice.CORE as (name, kind, d, g, s, b, w, l), in its order."""
    return [(n, "nfet" if t == "n" else "pfet", d, g, s, b, *sizes[n]) for n, t, d, g, s, b in core]


def _device(S, x0, x1, y0, L, nsd=290):
    """A transistor with a horizontal gate: diffusion x0..x1 (W = x1 - x0) by nsd | L | nsd, contacts (licon, pitch
    0.4 um) in both source/drain rows and an li1 strip over each row.  Returns the y of the gate's bottom and top."""
    add = lambda layer, *b: S.append((layer,) + tuple(int(v) for v in b))
    yg0, yg1 = y0 + nsd, y0 + nsd + L
    add("diff", x0, y0, x1, yg1 + nsd)
    add("poly", x0 - 130, yg0, x1 + 130, yg1)
    xs = list(range(x0 + 60, x1 - 60 - 170 + 1, 400))
    for row in (y0 + 60, yg1 + 60):
        for x in xs:
            add("licon", x, row, x + 170, row + 170)
        add("li", x0 - 20, row - 20, x1 + 20, row + 190)
    return yg0, yg1


def geometry(sizes):
    W = lambda n: (int(round(sizes[n][0] * 1000)), int(round(sizes[n][1] * 1000)))
    expect = {"M1": (4000, 500), "M3": (1000, 150), "M5": (2000, 150), "M7": (2000, 150), "M8": (1000, 150), "M10": (1000, 150)}
    assert all(W(k) == v for k, v in expect.items()), "geometry is laid out for comparator_spice.DEFAULT_SIZES"
    left, centre = [], []
    L = lambda layer, *b: left.append((layer,) + tuple(int(v) for v in b))
    C = lambda layer, *b: centre.append((layer,) + tuple(int(v) for v in b))

    # substrate taps under the ground rail (met1), and the clock rail
    C("tap", -4000, 60, 4000, 340)
    C("psdm", -4125, -65, 4125, 485)
    C("li", -4020, 95, 4020, 305)
    for x in range(-3880, 3880 - 170 + 1, 400):
        C("licon", x, 115, x + 170, 285)
        C("mcon", x, 115, x + 170, 285)
    C("met1", -5900, 0, 5900, 400)                         # vss
    C("met1", -5790, 830, 5790, 1120)                      # clk
    # tail M7 on the axis, its gate contacted at both ends onto the clock rail
    _device(centre, -1000, 1000, 610, 150)
    C("nsdm", -1125, 485, 1125, 1485)
    C("li", -85, 305, 85, 650)                             # source to the taps
    C("poly", -1460, 900, 1460, 1050)
    L("poly", -1460, 840, -1130, 1110)
    L("licon", -1380, 890, -1210, 1060)
    L("npc", -1480, 790, -1110, 1160)
    L("li", -1380, 810, -1210, 1140)
    L("mcon", -1380, 890, -1210, 1060)
    # input pair M1 (tail -> dp), gate pad on the left
    _device(left, -4420, -420, 1610, 500)
    L("li", -700, 1090, -530, 1860)                        # tail: M7 drain to M1 source
    L("poly", -4880, 1930, -4550, 2200)
    L("licon", -4800, 1980, -4630, 2150)
    L("npc", -4900, 1880, -4530, 2250)
    L("li", -4800, 1900, -4630, 2230)
    # latch nMOS M3 (dp -> outn) on top of M1; its gate runs to the left vertical gate poly
    _device(left, -1420, -420, 2960, 150)
    L("poly", -1550, 3250, -180, 3400)
    L("li", -1440, 2440, -400, 3210)                       # dp: M1 drain and M3 source
    L("li", -5260, 2440, -400, 2650)                       # dp, out to the reset device M10
    L("nsdm", -4545, 1485, -295, 3815)
    L("poly", -330, 3250, -180, 5200)                      # gate of M3 and M5 (net outp)
    # n-well row: M10 (dp reset), M8 (outn reset), M5 (latch pMOS)
    for x0, x1 in ((-5320, -4320), (-4020, -3020), (-2420, -420)):
        _device(left, x0, x1, 4760, 150)
    L("poly", -2550, 5050, -180, 5200)                     # M5 gate to the vertical gate poly
    L("poly", -5480, 5050, -2890, 5200)                    # M10 + M8 gate (clk) ...
    L("poly", -5810, 4990, -5480, 5260)                    # ... its pad (>= 0.235 from the p-diffusion) ...
    L("licon", -5730, 5040, -5560, 5210)
    L("npc", -5830, 4940, -5460, 5310)
    L("li", -5730, 4960, -5560, 5290)
    L("mcon", -5730, 5040, -5560, 5210)
    L("met1", -5790, 830, -5500, 5270)                     # ... and the clock up the side
    L("li", -4040, 4800, -400, 5010)                       # outn: M8 and M5 drains
    L("li", -1340, 3440, -1170, 5010)                      # outn: M3 drain up to the pMOS drains
    L("li", -5260, 2440, -5090, 5010)                      # dp up to M10
    L("li", -5340, 5240, -400, 5450)                       # vdd: pMOS sources
    for x0, x1 in ((-5320, -4320), (-4020, -3020), (-2420, -420)):
        for x in range(x0 + 60, x1 - 60 - 170 + 1, 400):
            L("mcon", x, 5260, x + 170, 5430)
    C("psdm", -5445, 4635, 5445, 5635)
    C("tap", -5260, 5760, 5260, 6050)                      # n-well tap
    C("nsdm", -5385, 5635, 5385, 6175)
    C("li", -5280, 5800, 5280, 6010)
    for x in range(-5140, 5140 - 170 + 1, 400):
        C("licon", x, 5820, x + 170, 5990)
        C("mcon", x, 5820, x + 170, 5990)
    C("nwell", -5500, 4580, 5500, 6230)
    C("met1", -5320, 5200, 5320, 6050)                     # vdd
    # cross-couple: A takes outp to the left gate poly, B takes outn to the right gate poly
    C("poly", -390, 3800, -120, 4130)
    C("licon", -340, 3880, -170, 4050)
    C("li", -420, 3880, 1340, 4050)
    C("poly", 120, 4270, 390, 4600)
    C("licon", 170, 4350, 340, 4520)
    C("li", -1340, 4350, 420, 4520)
    C("npc", -440, 3780, 440, 4660)

    mirror = lambda b: (-b[2], b[1], -b[0], b[3])
    shapes = centre + left + [(s[0],) + mirror(s[1:]) for s in left]
    pins = [("li_pin", "inp", (-4800, 1980, -4630, 2150)), ("li_pin", "outn", (-1340, 3700, -1170, 3870))]
    other = {"inp": "inn", "outn": "outp"}
    pins += [(layer, other[t], mirror(b)) for layer, t, b in pins]
    pins += [("met1_pin", "vss", (-200, 0, 200, 400)), ("met1_pin", "clk", (-200, 830, 200, 1120)),
             ("met1_pin", "vdd", (-200, 5500, 200, 5700))]
    return shapes, pins


def draw(path, sizes):
    return sl.write_gds(*geometry(sizes), path, NAME)


def cell_report(sizes):
    return sl.extent(geometry(sizes)[0])


def render(sizes, **kw):
    kw.setdefault("figsize", (7.2, 4.4))
    return sl.render(*geometry(sizes), **kw)


def drc(tcfg, gds):
    return sl.drc(tcfg, gds, NAME)


def extract(tcfg, gds):
    return sl.extract(tcfg, gds, NAME)


def schematic_netlist(core, sizes, path):
    devs = [(n, k, *("vss" if x == "0" else x for x in (d, g, s, b)), w, l) for n, k, d, g, s, b, w, l in schematic(core, sizes)]
    return sl.write_schematic(devs, PORTS, path, NAME)


def lvs(tcfg, layout_spice, schematic_spice):
    return sl.lvs(tcfg, layout_spice, schematic_spice, NAME)


def postlayout(pex_path, core, sizes):
    """The extraction renamed onto comparator_spice's core: dict(devices, caps, node_cap, netmap)."""
    return sl.map_extraction(pex_path, schematic(core, sizes), LABELS)
```

> **Next cell.** 1. Draws the SRAM-PUF cell with KLayout. 2. Runs Magic's DRC. 3. Extracts the layout with Magic. 4. Compares it with the schematic in netgen and prints the LVS verdict and the extracted transistors. 5. Reports in the card the extracted wiring capacitance of the storage nodes (Fig. 32 shows the layout). Run time: about 2 s.


```python
#@title SKY130 6T SRAM-PUF: layout, DRC, LVS and extraction
import importlib, klayout, sky130_layout as sl, puf_layout as pl
importlib.reload(sl); importlib.reload(pl)
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
t0 = time.time()
LD = WORK / "layout" / "sram6t"
TL_PUF = sl.tool_config(str(PDK_ROOT), magic=str(MAGIC), netgen=str(NETGEN), workdir=str(LD))
gds_puf = pl.draw(str(LD / "sram6t.gds"), ps.CELL)                     # 1. KLayout: rectangles from Python -> GDS
drc_puf = pl.drc(TL_PUF, gds_puf["path"])                              # 2. Magic: full SKY130 rule deck
ext_puf = pl.extract(TL_PUF, gds_puf["path"])                          # 3. Magic: devices + parasitic capacitances
lvs_puf = pl.lvs(TL_PUF, ext_puf["lvs"], pl.schematic_netlist(ps.CELL, str(LD / "sram6t_sch.spice")))   # 4. netgen
LAY_PUF = pl.postlayout_cell(ext_puf["pex"], ps.CELL)                  # the extraction as puf_spice's sram6t subcircuit
size, nc = pl.cell_report(ps.CELL), LAY_PUF["node_cap"]
cap = lambda a, b: sum(v for x, y, v in LAY_PUF["caps"] if {x, y} == {a, b})
card("SRAM-PUF cell in SKY130: layout, DRC, LVS and extraction",
     [(f"layout (KLayout {klayout.__version__}, Python API)", f"{size['width_um']:.2f} × {size['height_um']:.2f} µm, 6 transistors, point-symmetric"),
      ("DRC (Magic, full SKY130 rule deck)", f"<b>{drc_puf['count']} violations</b>"),
      ("LVS (netgen, against the schematic)", "<b>circuits match uniquely</b>: 6 devices, 8 nets" if lvs_puf["match"] else "<b>netlists do not match</b>"),
      ("extracted wiring capacitance on q / qb", f"<b>{1e15 * nc['q']:.3f} / {1e15 * nc['qb']:.3f} fF</b>, of which {1e15 * cap('q', 'qb'):.3f} fF couples q to qb"),
      ("run time", f"{time.time() - t0:.0f} s")], tone="ok" if drc_puf["count"] == 0 and lvs_puf["match"] else "bad")
print("netgen LVS report:", *[l.strip() for l in open(lvs_puf["report"]) if "match" in l.lower()][-2:], sep="\n  ")
print("Magic extraction, transistors:", *[l.rstrip() for l in open(ext_puf["pex"]) if l.startswith("X")], sep="\n  ", end="")

# the layout drawings label the pins with the names of the schematics (the GDS keeps the netlist's names)
NET = {"q": "$q$", "qb": r"$\bar{q}$", "bl": "BL", "blb": r"$\overline{\mathrm{BL}}$", "wla": "WL", "wlb": "WL", "vdd": r"$V_\mathrm{DD}$",
       "vss": "GND", "inp": r"$V_\mathrm{in+}$", "inn": r"$V_\mathrm{in-}$", "outp": r"$\mathrm{out}_p$", "outn": r"$\mathrm{out}_n$",
       "dp": "$d_p$", "dn": "$d_n$", "clk": r"$\phi$"}
def name_pins(ax):
    for t in ax.texts:
        t.set_text(NET.get(t.get_text(), t.get_text()))
    ax.set_xlabel("$x$ (µm)"); ax.set_ylabel("$y$ (µm)")
fig, (a0, a1) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(W2, 4.8), gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[1.0, 1.3]))
pl.render(ps.CELL, ax=a0, legend=False, pin_size=7); name_pins(a0)
panel(a0, "a", "layout (2 halves, rotated 180°)")
groups = [("ground", lambda n: cap(n, "0")), (NET["vdd"], lambda n: cap(n, "vdd")), ("other node", lambda n: cap("q", "qb")),
          ("bit lines", lambda n: cap(n, "bl") + cap(n, "blb")), ("word line", lambda n: cap(n, "wl"))]
yb = np.arange(len(groups))
for j, (node, c, h) in enumerate((("q", COL["ok"], ""), ("qb", COL["bad"], "////"))):
    a1.barh(yb + (j - 0.5) * 0.36, [1e15 * f(node) for _, f in groups], height=0.34, color=c, hatch=h, ec=COL["ink"], lw=0.5, label=NET[node])
a1.set_yticks(yb, [g for g, _ in groups]); a1.invert_yaxis()
a1.set_xlabel("Extracted capacitance (fF)"); a1.legend(loc="lower right"); a1.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
panel(a1, "b", r"where the wiring capacitance of $q$ and $\bar{q}$ goes")
fig.legend(handles=[Patch(fc=c, ec=c, alpha=min(1, a + 0.25), label=n) for n, c, a in sl.STYLE], loc="lower center", ncol=6,
           fontsize=8, frameon=False, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.02))
fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.07, 1, 1)); plt.show()
```

<p align="center" style="text-align:center"><b>Fig. 27.</b> SRAM-PUF cell layout and extracted capacitance. (a) SKY130 6T cell: half A (bottom left) and the same shapes rotated by 180° (top right); layers as in the legend, pins labelled. (b) Extracted wiring capacitance of the storage nodes q (solid) and q̄ (hatched), by the net it couples to.</p>

**Result (SRAM-PUF layout).** The cell measures 2.21 × 5.50 µm with 6 transistors; Magic finds 0 DRC violations, and netgen reports that the circuits match uniquely (6 devices, 8 nets). The extracted wiring capacitance is 0.973 fF on q and 0.973 fF on q̄, of which 0.209 fF couples the two nodes to each other (card; Fig. 27(b)): **the two storage nodes are loaded identically**, as the point symmetry was meant to ensure, so the layout does not favour either power-up value.

**Interpretation.** With equal capacitance on q and q̄, the layout gives neither node an advantage in the power-up race, so it is not expected to bias the cells; the Monte Carlo of the extracted cell, next, tests this together with any change in noise.

> **Next cell.** 1. Takes the Monte Carlo of the extracted cell on 128 cells × 5 power-ups × 3 temperatures from the recorded post-layout run, or, with `PEX_LIVE = True`, simulates it live with the seeds of the recorded runs (about 105 s on two cores). 2. Compares it cell by cell with the schematic cell (recorded run) on the same cells and noise, so that every difference is caused by the layout. 3. In a live run, checks bit for bit that it reproduces the recorded post-layout run. 4. Takes the post-layout model fit from the recorded 1,024-cell run (from the live run with `PUF_MODE = "full"`).


```python
#@title SKY130 6T SRAM-PUF: schematic vs post-layout
# the extracted cell in the Monte Carlo of Section VII-C: same seeds, so the same cells (mismatch) and the same noise
POST = dict(ps.CELL, layout=LAY_PUF)
t0 = time.time()
PUF_POST_LIVE = PEX_LIVE or PUF_MODE == "full"
REC_POST = np.unpackbits(np.frombuffer(base64.b64decode(""), np.uint8))[: len(TEMPS) * 5 * 128].reshape(len(TEMPS), 5, 128).astype(np.int8)
if PUF_POST_LIVE:                                                  # simulate the extracted cell in this session
    env_post = ps.noise_envelope(pcfg, TEMPS, cell=POST, name="envelope_post")
    mc_post = ps.run_montecarlo(pcfg, SET["n_cells"], TEMPS, SET["repeats"], env_post, chunk=64, mismatch_seed=1, cell=POST,
                                name="mc_post", log=lambda *a: None)
else:                                                              # the recorded run of the same code and seeds
    mc_post = dict(bits=REC_POST)
an_post = ps.analyse(mc_post["bits"], TEMPS)
# the schematic run on the same cells and noise draws (each chunk of 64 cells has its own seed, so a live run of n cells
# simulates exactly the first n cells of the recorded runs), and the recorded post-layout run on those cells
_n, _r = mc_post["bits"].shape[2], mc_post["bits"].shape[1]
sch = mc["bits"][:, :_r, :_n]; an_sch = ps.analyse(sch, TEMPS)
ref_post = mc_post["bits"] if PUF_MODE == "full" else REC_POST[:, :_r, :_n]
same_rec = float((mc_post["bits"] == ref_post).mean())
maj = lambda b: np.round(b.mean(axis=0))
table(["Temperature", "P(1): schematic", "post-layout", "BER: schematic", "post-layout", "Unstable: sch.", "post", "Same majority bit"],
      [(f"{T} °C".replace("-", "−"), f"{100 * a['bias']:.1f} %", f"{100 * b['bias']:.1f} %", f"{100 * a['ber']:.2f} %", f"{100 * b['ber']:.2f} %",
        a["n_unstable"], b["n_unstable"], f"{100 * np.mean(maj(sch[k]) == maj(mc_post['bits'][k])):.1f} %")
       for k, (T, a, b) in enumerate(zip(TEMPS, an_sch["rows"], an_post["rows"]))],
      caption=f"Table VI: SKY130 6T SRAM-PUF, schematic vs extracted layout on the same {_n} cells, {_r} power-ups and noise "
              f"draws: post-layout " + (f"simulated in this session ({time.time() - t0:.0f} s)" if PUF_POST_LIVE else
                                         "from the recorded run (PEX_LIVE = True re-runs it, about 105 s on two cores)")
              + f", schematic from {MC_SRC}")
# the recorded full runs (1,024 cells x 8 power-ups x 3 temperatures, same code and seeds; demo.py and demo_postlayout.py)
PUF_POST_FULL = json.loads('{"n_cells": 1024, "repeats": 8, "s25": 0.022531638899614112, "s25_ci95": [0.014842421513862617, 0.03404676587717018], "tc": 0.020509989782846683, "mu": -0.01805408965245689, "ber": [0.013671875, 0.009905133928571428, 0.0313720703125], "ber_ci": [[0.008544921875, 0.019656372070312497], [0.005719866071428571, 0.014512416294642852], [0.0219696044921875, 0.041143798828124994]], "bias": [0.497802734375, 0.4927978515625, 0.4949951171875], "noiseless_agree": 0.978515625}')
use = ps.fit_ber_matched(mc_post["bits"], TEMPS, n_boot=30, log=lambda *a: None) if PUF_MODE == "full" else PUF_POST_FULL
PUF_FIT_POST = dict(s25=use["s25"], tc=use["a"] if "a" in use else use["tc"], bias=float(ndtr(use["mu"])))
card("SRAM-PUF model fit, schematic vs post-layout (recorded full runs)",
     [("noise / mismatch s<sub>25</sub>", f"{PUF_FULL['s25']:.4f} → <b>{PUF_POST_FULL['s25']:.4f}</b> "
                                           f"(post-layout 95 % interval {PUF_POST_FULL['s25_ci95'][0]:.4f}–{PUF_POST_FULL['s25_ci95'][1]:.4f})"),
      ("temperature coefficient a", f"{PUF_FULL['tc']:.3f} → <b>{PUF_POST_FULL['tc']:.3f}</b>"),
      ("P(1)", f"{ndtr(PUF_FULL['mu']):.3f} → <b>{ndtr(PUF_POST_FULL['mu']):.3f}</b>"),
      ("noiseless power-up value unchanged by the layout", f"{100 * PUF_POST_FULL['noiseless_agree']:.1f} % of 1,024 cells"),
      ("used from here on", "the post-layout values" + (" of this run" if PUF_MODE == "full" else " (recorded full run)")),
      (f"post-layout run of this session against the recorded one (same {_n} cells, {_r} power-ups, {len(TEMPS)} temperatures)",
       f"<b>{100 * same_rec:.2f} %</b> of the power-up bits identical" if PUF_POST_LIVE else
       "not re-run (PEX_LIVE = False): the recorded run is shown")])

# the recorded full runs (1,024 cells x 8 power-ups), with their 95 % bootstrap intervals over cells, and the 128-cell paired
# comparison of the same cells (small markers), whose sampling scatter is several times larger
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(W1 + 1.3, 3.0))
Tf = np.array(TEMPS, float)
for d, (lab, ber, ci, m, c, lw) in zip((-1.5, 1.5), (
        ("schematic", PUF_FULL["ber"], [r["ber_ci"] for r in an["rows"]], "o", COL["faint"], 1.3),
        ("post-layout", PUF_POST_FULL["ber"], PUF_POST_FULL["ber_ci"], "s", COL["ok"], 1.6))):
    y, lo, hi = 100 * np.array(ber), 100 * np.array([x[0] for x in ci]), 100 * np.array([x[1] for x in ci])
    ax.errorbar(Tf + d, y, yerr=[y - lo, hi - y], fmt=m + "-", color=c, mfc="white", lw=lw, ms=5, capsize=3, elinewidth=1.0,
                label=f"{lab} (1,024 cells × 8 power-ups)")
ax.plot(Tf - 4.5, [100 * r["ber"] for r in an_sch["rows"]], "o", color=COL["faint"], ms=3.5, label=f"schematic, the same {_n} cells")
ax.plot(Tf + 4.5, [100 * r["ber"] for r in an_post["rows"]], "s", color=COL["ok"], ms=3.5,
        label=f"post-layout, {'this session' if PUF_POST_LIVE else 'recorded'} ({_n} cells)")
ax.set_xlabel("Temperature (°C)"); ax.set_ylabel("BER vs 25 °C enrolment (%)"); ax.set_xticks(TEMPS)
ax.set_xlim(TEMPS[0] - 12, TEMPS[-1] + 12); ax.set_ylim(0, None)
ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=8); fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

<p align="center" style="text-align:center"><b>Fig. 28.</b> SRAM-PUF cell bit-error rate before and after layout (enrolment: one power-up at 25 °C). Open markers: recorded runs of 1,024 cells × 8 power-ups, schematic (grey) and extracted layout (blue), with 95 % bootstrap intervals over cells. Filled markers: the same 128 cells × 5 power-ups, paired (post-layout recorded unless PEX_LIVE = True). Series offset in temperature for legibility.</p>

**Result (SRAM-PUF, schematic against post-layout).** On the same 128 cells, power-ups and noise draws (Table VI; post-layout from the recorded run unless `PEX_LIVE = True`, schematic from its recorded run), the fraction of ones changes by at most 1.5 percentage points (46.9–48.6 % after layout against 47.8–49.2 % before), and the majority value of each cell agrees in 98.4–99.2 % of the cells at every temperature. The bit-error rates differ by a few bit errors per temperature (at 25 °C, 1.17 % against 0.98 %, that is 6 against 5 errors in 512 comparisons), which is within the sampling scatter of 128 cells: in Fig. 28 the small markers of the paired comparison scatter around the full-run curves by about as much as they differ from each other, which is why the conclusion rests on the 1,024-cell runs with their intervals. In the recorded full runs, the fit changes from s<sub>25</sub> = 0.0205 to 0.0225 (post-layout 95 % interval 0.0148–0.0340, which contains the schematic value), a from 0.023 to 0.021 and P(1) from 0.496 to 0.493; 97.9 % of the 1,024 cells keep their noiseless power-up value. The full post-layout run has a BER of 0.99 % at 25 °C (Fig. 28), against 0.45·s<sub>25</sub> = 1.01 % from the theory of Section VII-C; at −40 and 85 °C it has 1.37 and 3.14 % (Section VII-E), against 1.34 and 2.31 % for the schematic (0.91 % at 25 °C). The 95 % intervals of the two runs overlap at every temperature, so **the layout leaves the error rate unchanged within its statistical error**. This holds also at 85 °C, the temperature that sizes the code: the full runs differ by 0.83 percentage points (3.14 against 2.31 %), but the schematic value lies inside the post-layout 95 % interval (2.20–4.11 %), and the paired comparison on 128 cells goes the other way (3.91 % after layout against 4.53 % before, Table VI). The difference is therefore sampling scatter and is not attributed to the layout; the code is sized from the post-layout run only because that run includes the wiring. With `PEX_LIVE = True`, the card's last row compares a live run of the session with the recorded post-layout run on the same 128 cells, 5 power-ups and 3 temperatures, bit by bit. The published run uses the default `PEX_LIVE = False`, so its row states that the recorded run is shown, and the live comparison is not part of it.

**Interpretation.** As predicted for a symmetric cell, **the layout introduces no measurable bias** (the change of P(1) is far below the ±1.6 % sampling error of 1,024 cells) and no significant change in noise (s<sub>25</sub> moves by 10 %, well inside its interval). The 2.1 % of cells that change their noiseless value are those whose mismatch is so small that a sub-femtofarad change of the node capacitance reverses their preferred value; on a real chip the enrolment is made after fabrication, so these cells are enrolled with their post-layout value. Whether the code in the session reproduces the recorded post-layout run from which the model's parameters are taken can be checked with `PEX_LIVE = True`, bit by bit on its first 128 cells; the remaining cells are simulated by the same code with their own seeds.

> **Next cell.** 1. Draws the comparator core with KLayout. 2. Runs DRC, extraction and LVS. 3. Reports in the card the extracted wiring capacitance of the internal nodes against the 1 fF the schematic assumed (Fig. 32 shows the layout).


```python
#@title SKY130 StrongARM comparator: layout, DRC, LVS and extraction
import comparator_layout as cl
importlib.reload(cl)
t0 = time.time()
LD = WORK / "layout" / "strongarm"
TL_CMP = sl.tool_config(str(PDK_ROOT), magic=str(MAGIC), netgen=str(NETGEN), workdir=str(LD))
gds_cmp = cl.draw(str(LD / "strongarm.gds"), cfg["sizes"])            # 1. KLayout
drc_cmp = cl.drc(TL_CMP, gds_cmp["path"])                              # 2. Magic DRC
ext_cmp = cl.extract(TL_CMP, gds_cmp["path"])                          # 3. Magic extraction
lvs_cmp = cl.lvs(TL_CMP, ext_cmp["lvs"], cl.schematic_netlist(cs.CORE, cfg["sizes"], str(LD / "strongarm_sch.spice")))   # 4. netgen
LAY_CMP = cl.postlayout(ext_cmp["pex"], cs.CORE, cfg["sizes"])         # tail, dp, dn are found from the transistors
size, nc = cl.cell_report(cfg["sizes"]), LAY_CMP["node_cap"]
card("StrongARM comparator core in SKY130: layout, DRC, LVS and extraction",
     [(f"layout (KLayout {klayout.__version__})", f"{size['width_um']:.1f} × {size['height_um']:.2f} µm, 11 transistors (M1–M11), mirror-symmetric"),
      ("DRC (Magic, full SKY130 rule deck)", f"<b>{drc_cmp['count']} violations</b>"),
      ("LVS (netgen, against the schematic)", "<b>circuits match uniquely</b>: 11 devices, 10 nets" if lvs_cmp["match"] else "<b>netlists do not match</b>"),
      ("extracted capacitance dp / dn", f"{1e15 * nc['dp']:.3f} / {1e15 * nc['dn']:.3f} fF (schematic assumed {1e15 * cfg['c_par']:.0f} fF)"),
      ("extracted capacitance outp / outn", f"{1e15 * nc['outp']:.3f} / {1e15 * nc['outn']:.3f} fF: the one asymmetry, from the cross-couple"),
      ("run time", f"{time.time() - t0:.0f} s")], tone="ok" if drc_cmp["count"] == 0 and lvs_cmp["match"] else "bad")
print("netgen LVS report:", *[l.strip() for l in open(lvs_cmp["report"]) if "match" in l.lower()][-2:], sep="\n  ")
print("internal nets inferred from the extraction:", {k: v for k, v in LAY_CMP["netmap"].items() if k != v and "#" in k})

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(W2, 5.6))
a0 = fig.add_axes([0.06, 0.42, 0.92, 0.53]); a1 = fig.add_axes([0.10, 0.12, 0.86, 0.20])
cl.render(cfg["sizes"], ax=a0, legend=False, pin_size=7); name_pins(a0)          # pins named as in the schematic
panel(a0, "a", "layout")
nodes = ["dp", "dn", "outp", "outn", "tail"]
xb = np.arange(len(nodes))
a1.bar(xb - 0.18, [1e15 * cfg["c_par"] if n != "tail" else 0 for n in nodes], 0.34, color="white", ec=COL["ink"], hatch="////", lw=0.6,
       label="schematic (assumed)")
a1.bar(xb + 0.18, [1e15 * nc[n] for n in nodes], 0.34, color=COL["ok"], ec=COL["ink"], lw=0.6, label="extracted")
a1.set_xticks(xb, [NET.get(n, n) for n in nodes]); a1.set_ylabel("Wiring $C$ (fF)"); a1.legend(loc="upper left", ncol=2)
a1.grid(axis="x", visible=False); a1.set_ylim(0, 1.45 * max(1e15 * nc[n] for n in nodes))   # room for the legend
panel(a1, "b", "wiring capacitance of the internal nodes")
fig.legend(handles=[Patch(fc=c, ec=c, alpha=min(1, a + 0.25), label=n) for n, c, a in sl.STYLE], loc="lower center", ncol=11,
           fontsize=7.5, frameon=False, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.0), handlelength=1.0, columnspacing=0.9)
```

<p align="center" style="text-align:center"><b>Fig. 29.</b> StrongARM comparator layout and extracted capacitance. (a) SKY130 core, mirror-symmetric about x = 0; from the bottom: ground rail and taps, tail M7, input pair M1/M2, latch nMOS M3/M4, and in the n-well the latch pMOS M5/M6 and reset devices M8–M11. (b) Wiring capacitance of the internal nodes, extracted (solid) and assumed in the schematic (hatched; none for the tail).</p>

**Result (comparator layout).** The core measures 11.8 × 6.05 µm with 11 transistors (M1–M11); DRC finds 0 violations and LVS reports that the circuits match uniquely (11 devices, 10 nets), with the internal nodes d<sub>p</sub>, d<sub>n</sub> and the tail identified from the transistors' terminals. The integrating nodes carry 0.989 fF each (d<sub>p</sub> and d<sub>n</sub>), **within 1.1 % of the 1 fF the schematic assumed**. The outputs carry 1.332 and 1.339 fF (out<sub>p</sub>, out<sub>n</sub>): about a third more than assumed, and the only asymmetry of the layout, 7 aF, caused by the cross-coupling route that crosses the axis (card; Fig. 29).

**Interpretation.** Because the integrating nodes match the schematic's assumption, the theory predicts no change of σ<sub>n</sub> or σ<sub>os</sub>. The larger output capacitance slows the regeneration slightly, which is of no consequence at 10 MHz, where the decision has 50 ns to complete, and the 7 aF imbalance is expected to appear as a small systematic offset. The next cell measures all three, together with the energy.

> **Next cell.** 1. Takes the extracted comparator's energy, noise and offset from the recorded run of this cell, or, with `PEX_LIVE = True` (or if no record is present), measures them live with the testbenches and seeds of Section VII-B, so that the 96 offset instances are the same comparators as before (about 50 s on two cores). 2. Tabulates schematic against post-layout, with the paired change of each instance's offset. 3. Maps the post-layout noise onto the model.

<p align="center" style="text-align:center"><b>Fig. 30.</b> StrongARM comparator before and after layout, same mismatch draws and noise (post-layout recorded unless PEX_LIVE = True). (a) Probability of deciding 1 against ΔV<sub>in</sub>, schematic (circles) and post-layout (squares), with probit fits. (b) Offset of each of the 96 instances after layout against before; dashed: no change; box: σ<sub>os</sub> and the paired mean shift.</p>

Fig. 30 compares the two measurements on which the model's comparator setting rests, before and after the wiring is added, on the same axes: if the layout changed the noise, the two probit curves of panel (a) would have different slopes; if it changed the offsets, the points of panel (b) would leave the diagonal.

**Result (comparator, schematic against post-layout).** With the same mismatch draws and noise (Table VII, Fig. 30; post-layout from the recorded run of the cell, or simulated in the session if `PEX_LIVE = True` or no record is present, as the table caption states):

* **Noise** (Fig. 30(a)): σ<sub>n</sub> = 0.560 ± 0.028 mV before and 0.575 ± 0.028 mV after layout (+2.7 %). The simulated probabilities of both netlists lie on one curve, and the two fits have the same slope within their errors: the change, 0.015 mV, is about half of one standard error, so **the layout does not change the noise measurably**, as predicted.
* **Offset spread:** σ<sub>os</sub> = 4.34 mV before and 4.37 mV after (+0.6 %); the 96 instances keep their offsets almost exactly (Fig. 30(b), points on the diagonal).
* **Systematic offset:** the mean offset of the same 96 instances moves from −0.068 to +0.027 mV, a paired shift of +0.095 ± 0.010 mV, consistent with the +0.124 mV shift of μ in the noise fit (each ±0.030 mV). This is the effect of the cross-coupling asymmetry: resolved precisely because the comparison is paired, and 2.2 % of σ<sub>os</sub>.
* **Energy:** the core is unchanged (104 → 105 fJ, +0.9 %), but the clock energy rises from 23 to 35 fJ (+49.1 %), because the extracted clock wiring adds a few femtofarads that the clock driver charges every cycle, at 3.2 fJ per fF. The total rises from 186 to 199 fJ per decision (+7.0 %).
* **Model setting:** `comp_noise` = σ<sub>n</sub>/V<sub>unit</sub> becomes 1.279 × 10⁻³ (schematic 1.245 × 10⁻³).

**Interpretation.** The layout leaves the two quantities that matter for the modulator, noise and offset spread, unchanged within the statistics, and adds a systematic offset of 0.1 mV that is negligible against σ<sub>os</sub>; **its only significant effect is the clock energy**. The post-layout values are nevertheless adopted below, because a fabricated circuit includes its wiring, so they are the closer approximation to silicon. Fig. 32 below shows both layouts. A transient comparison of both cells before and after extraction (Fig. 31) shows where the parasitics act: the comparator takes the same six decisions and all four SRAM cells settle to the same value. The model's parameters are set from these values in Section VII-E.

#### Schematic against post-layout waveforms

**Goal.** Compare the transient behaviour of both cells before and after extraction on identical stimuli, to show where the layout parasitics act and that they do not change any decision.

**Setup.** Transistor level. Comparator: the six-decision transient of Fig. 20 repeated on the extracted netlist, with the same inputs. SRAM-PUF cell: the four power-ups of Fig. 24 at 25 °C repeated on the extracted cell with the same mismatch draws and the same noise sequence (the post-layout noise envelope at 25 °C). Metrics: the comparator's decisions and internal waveforms of the +0.2 mV cycle; each SRAM cell's final value and the supply voltage at which it resolves (|q − q̄| first exceeding V<sub>DD</sub>/2).

> **Next cell.** 1. Simulates the comparator transient on the extracted netlist. 2. Simulates the four SRAM power-ups on the extracted cell. 3. Overlays schematic and post-layout waveforms. 4. Compares the decisions and the final values.


```python
#@title Schematic vs post-layout waveforms
# the same transients as Sections VII-B and -C (same inputs, same mismatch, same noise), on the extracted netlists
t0 = time.time()
tr_post = cs.run_transient_demo(cfg_post, name="tran_demo_post")
env_w = env_post if PUF_POST_LIVE else ps.noise_envelope(pcfg, [25], cell=POST, name="envelope_post25")   # 25 °C is enough here
waves_post, _ = ps.run_waveforms(pcfg, 4, [25], 1001, env_w, cell=POST, name="waves_post")
fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(W2, 5.0))
k = 2                                                     # the +0.2 mV decision
for ax, (a, b, la, lb), lab in zip(axs[0], (("v(c0_dp)", "v(c0_dn)", "$d_p$", "$d_n$"),
                                            ("v(c0_outp)", "v(c0_outn)", r"$\mathrm{out}_p$", r"$\mathrm{out}_n$")), ("a", "b")):
    for r, name, col in ((tr, "schematic", COL["faint"]), (tr_post, "post-layout", COL["ok"])):
        w, e = r["wave"], r["edges"][k]
        m = (w["time"] > e - 0.2e-9) & (w["time"] < e + 1.5e-9)
        tz = (w["time"][m] - e) * 1e9
        ax.plot(tz, w[a][m], color=col, lw=1.5, label=f"{la}, {name}")
        ax.plot(tz, w[b][m], color=col, lw=1.5, ls="--", label=f"{lb}, {name}")
    ax.set_xlabel("Time after the rising clock edge (ns)"); ax.set_ylabel("Voltage (V)")
    ax.legend(loc="upper right" if lab == "a" else "center right", fontsize=7.5)
    panel(ax, lab, "comparator, +0.2 mV: integration nodes" if lab == "a" else "comparator, +0.2 mV: latch outputs")
ws, wp = waves[0][0], waves_post[0][0]
cols = [COL["ok"], COL["bad"], COL["aqua"], COL["yellow"]]
for c in range(4):
    axs[1, 0].plot(ws["vdd"], ws["q"][c] - ws["qb"][c], color=COL["faint"], lw=1.0, ls="--")
    axs[1, 0].plot(wp["vdd"], wp["q"][c] - wp["qb"][c], color=cols[c], lw=1.5, label=f"cell {c + 1}")
axs[1, 0].plot([], [], color=COL["faint"], ls="--", label="schematic")
axs[1, 0].set_xlabel(r"$V_\mathrm{DD}$ (V)"); axs[1, 0].set_ylabel(r"$q - \bar{q}$ (V)"); axs[1, 0].legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=7.5, ncol=2)
panel(axs[1, 0], "c", "SRAM-PUF power-up, 25 °C")
dv_s, dv_p = ps.decision_vdd(ws), ps.decision_vdd(wp)
xb = np.arange(4)
axs[1, 1].bar(xb - 0.18, dv_s, 0.34, color="white", ec=COL["ink"], hatch="////", lw=0.6, label="schematic")
axs[1, 1].bar(xb + 0.18, dv_p, 0.34, color=COL["ok"], ec=COL["ink"], lw=0.6, label="post-layout")
axs[1, 1].set_xticks(xb, [f"cell {c + 1}" for c in range(4)]); axs[1, 1].set_ylabel(r"$V_\mathrm{DD}$ at the decision (V)")
axs[1, 1].set_ylim(0, 1.3 * np.nanmax(np.r_[dv_s, dv_p]))
axs[1, 1].legend(loc="upper center", ncol=2, fontsize=7.5); axs[1, 1].grid(axis="x", visible=False)
panel(axs[1, 1], "d", "supply voltage at which each cell resolves")
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
card("Waveforms, schematic vs post-layout",
     [("comparator decisions (6 inputs, ±0.2 to ±20 mV)", "identical" if (tr["decisions"] == tr_post["decisions"]).all() else "<b>differ</b>"),
      ("SRAM cells: same final value", f"{int(sum((ws['q'][c][-1] > ws['qb'][c][-1]) == (wp['q'][c][-1] > wp['qb'][c][-1]) for c in range(4)))} of 4"),
      ("run time", f"{time.time() - t0:.0f} s")], tone="ok")
```

```python
#@title Fig.: the layouts in KLayout
# KLayout's own renderer (klayout.lay draws without a window) with the PDK's KLayout layer table, sky130A.lyp: the colours and
# stipples of the KLayout window, on a white background. The same views drive the interactive viewer of the next cell.
import io, klayout.lay as klay, klayout.db as kdb
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
LYP = PDK_ROOT / "sky130A" / "libs.tech" / "klayout" / "tech" / "sky130A.lyp"
def kl_view(gds):
    """The GDS on a white background, without KLayout's grid (its ruler is part of the grid: the figures draw their own scale).
    The fill colours are the PDK's; the outlines of its very light layers (li1, licon1, mcon) are darkened to stay visible."""
    v = klay.LayoutView()
    v.load_layout(str(gds), True); v.load_layer_props(str(LYP))
    v.set_config("background-color", "#ffffff"); v.set_config("grid-visible", "false"); v.max_hier(); v.zoom_fit()
    it = v.begin_layers()
    while not it.at_end():
        n = it.current(); rgb = [(n.fill_color >> s) & 255 for s in (16, 8, 0)]
        if 0.2126 * rgb[0] + 0.7152 * rgb[1] + 0.0722 * rgb[2] > 0.78 * 255:      # luminance of the fill: a light layer
            n.frame_color = 0xFF000000 | sum(int(0.55 * c) << s for c, s in zip(rgb, (16, 8, 0)))
        it.next()
    return v
def kl_layers(v):
    """The layers the layout uses: (name, fill colour, an iterator to the view's layer entry)."""
    out, it = [], v.begin_layers()
    while not it.at_end():
        n = it.current()
        if not n.bbox().empty():
            out.append((n.name.split(" - ")[0], f"#{n.fill_color & 0xFFFFFF:06x}", it.dup()))
        it.next()
    return out
def kl_size(v, w, h):
    v.resize(w, h); v.zoom_fit()                                               # the window size, then the whole cell
kl_png = lambda v: v.get_pixels_with_options(v.viewport_width(), v.viewport_height(), 0, 2).to_png_data()   # 2x oversampled
def kl_fit(v, h=700, foot=0.1):
    """The window (h pixels high) and the view: the whole cell with a small margin and a free strip below it, `foot` times the
    cell's height, for the scale bar. Returns the image's aspect ratio (width / height)."""
    b = v.active_cellview().cell.dbbox(); m = 0.03 * max(b.width(), b.height())
    box = kdb.DBox(b.left - m, b.bottom - m - foot * b.height(), b.right + m, b.top + m)
    v.resize(round(h * box.width() / box.height()), h); v.zoom_box(box)
    return box.width() / box.height()
def kl_scalebar(ax, v, img, um):
    """A scale bar of `um` µm at the lower left of a rendered view, its length written above it."""
    px = img.shape[1] / v.box().width()                                        # pixels per µm
    x0, y0 = 0.04 * img.shape[1], 0.965 * img.shape[0]
    ax.plot([x0, x0 + um * px], [y0, y0], color=COL["ink"], lw=2.5, solid_capstyle="butt")
    ax.text(x0 + um * px / 2, y0 - 0.012 * img.shape[0], f"{um:g} µm", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8.5, color=COL["ink"])
KL = {"6T SRAM-PUF cell": kl_view(gds_puf["path"]), "StrongARM comparator": kl_view(gds_cmp["path"])}

asp = [kl_fit(v) for v in KL.values()]
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(W2, W2 / sum(asp) + 0.8), gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=asp))
for ax, v, lab, title in zip(axs, KL.values(), "ab", ("6T cell", "StrongARM comparator")):
    img = plt.imread(io.BytesIO(kl_png(v)), format="png")
    ax.imshow(img); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([]); ax.grid(False)
    kl_scalebar(ax, v, img, 2)
    panel(ax, lab, title)
fig.tight_layout()
for ax in axs:
    ax.apply_aspect()                                                          # the images' final size, for the legend below
used = {n: (c, f"#{it.current().frame_color & 0xFFFFFF:06x}") for v in KL.values() for n, c, it in kl_layers(v)}
fig.legend(handles=[Patch(fc=c, ec=e, lw=0.8, label=n.replace(".drawing", "")) for n, (c, e) in used.items()], loc="upper center",
           bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, min(ax.get_position().y0 for ax in axs) - 0.01), ncol=7, fontsize=7.5, frameon=False,
           handlelength=1.0, columnspacing=0.9)
plt.show()
```

```python
def kl_size(v, w, h):

# a small KLayout window: the same renderer and layer table, with zoom, pan, fit, the layer list, the labels and the background
import ipywidgets as W
def kl_window(views, w=760, h=470):
    """An interactive viewer of {name: kl_view(...)}: cell choice, fit, zoom, pan, layer visibility, labels, background.
    It shows KLayout's ruler, whose length follows the zoom (the grid stays hidden: its three styles are invisible)."""
    for v in views.values():
        kl_size(v, w, h)
        for k, x in (("grid-visible", "true"), ("grid-style0", "invisible"), ("grid-style1", "invisible"), ("grid-style2", "invisible")):
            v.set_config(k, x)
    img = W.Image(format="png", width=w, height=h)
    cell = W.Dropdown(options=list(views), description="Cell", layout=W.Layout(width="290px"))
    txt = W.Checkbox(value=True, description="labels", indent=False, layout=W.Layout(width="80px"))
    dark = W.Checkbox(value=False, description="dark", indent=False, layout=W.Layout(width="70px"))
    box, layers = W.HTML(), W.VBox(layout=W.Layout(width="210px", max_height=f"{h}px", overflow_y="auto"))
    def draw(*_):
        v = views[cell.value]
        v.set_config("text-visible", "true" if txt.value else "false")
        v.set_config("background-color", "#000000" if dark.value else "#ffffff")
        img.value = kl_png(v)
        box.value = f"view: {v.box().width():.2f} × {v.box().height():.2f} µm"
    def button(label, act, tip):
        b = W.Button(description=label, tooltip=tip, layout=W.Layout(width="44px" if len(label) == 1 else "56px"))
        b.on_click(lambda _: (act(views[cell.value]), draw()))
        return b
    def layer_list(*_):
        rows = []
        for name, col, it in kl_layers(views[cell.value]):
            cb = W.Checkbox(value=it.current().visible, description=name, indent=False, layout=W.Layout(width="170px"))
            cb.observe(lambda ch, it=it: (setattr(it.current(), "visible", ch["new"]), draw()), "value")
            rows.append(W.HBox([W.HTML(f'<div style="width:14px;height:14px;margin:6px 6px 0 0;background:{col};'
                                       f'border:1px solid #{it.current().frame_color & 0xFFFFFF:06x}"></div>'), cb]))
        layers.children = [W.HTML("<b>Layers</b>")] + rows
    cell.observe(lambda _: (layer_list(), draw()), "value"); txt.observe(draw, "value"); dark.observe(draw, "value")
    tools = [button("Fit", lambda v: v.zoom_fit(), "zoom to the whole cell"), button("+", lambda v: v.zoom_in(), "zoom in"),
             button("−", lambda v: v.zoom_out(), "zoom out")] + [button(s, getattr(klay.LayoutView, f"pan_{d}"), f"pan {d}")
                                                                 for s, d in (("←", "left"), ("→", "right"), ("↑", "up"), ("↓", "down"))]
    layer_list(); draw()
    win = W.VBox([W.HBox([cell] + tools + [txt, dark, box], layout=W.Layout(align_items="center")), W.HBox([img, layers])])
    win._static_png = img.value                    # the initial view, shown by viewers without a kernel
    return win
_win = kl_window(KL); display_widget(_win, _win._static_png)
```
