### E. The model with SKY130 parameters

**Goal.** Replace the model's illustrative circuit settings with the values simulated above (post-layout SPICE), and size the BCH code of the fuzzy extractor from the simulated PUF parameters, so that every later section runs on SKY130-derived numbers.

**Theory: the settings.** Five settings are replaced. `comp_noise` = σ<sub>n</sub>/V<sub>unit</sub> (Section VII-B). `puf_sigma`, `puf_tc` and `puf_bias` are s<sub>25</sub>, a and P(1) of the cell model (Section VII-C). The fifth, `int_noise`, is the thermal noise of the first integrator, which no simulation here provides; it is derived from the measurement of [1] instead: the input-referred noise current of 9.48 pA rms in a 100 kHz band, multiplied by the TIA gain and the buffer gain of 0.5, divided by the modulator's full scale of Section V-A, V<sub>DD</sub>/2 = 0.6 V of the 1.2 V chip of [1], and spread as white noise over the 5 MHz Nyquist band of one 10 MHz clock (a factor √(5 MHz/100 kHz)); because the model adds it at the first integrator's output, it is multiplied by that integrator's gain g<sub>1</sub> = 0.5.

**Theory: sizing the code.** The key is reconstructed correctly if a power-up has at most t flipped cells among the n = 600 fingerprint cells, t being the number of errors the BCH code corrects. At temperature T, cell *j* of a chip disagrees with its enrolled value with a probability p<sub>j</sub>(T); the number of flipped cells N is a sum of independent Bernoulli variables with different probabilities (a Poisson-binomial variable), and the key-failure probability P<sub>fail</sub>(t, T) = P(N > t) is computed exactly. The design rule is P<sub>fail</sub> < 10⁻⁶ at every temperature from 0 to 85 °C.

**Theory: which cell model.** Section VII-C showed that the linear law s(T) = s<sub>25</sub>(1 + a·|T − 25 °C|), symmetric about 25 °C, underestimates the 85 °C error rate of the extracted cell (1.75 % against 3.14 % simulated). A noise-only model anchored to each simulated error rate removes that bias but has a second flaw: at 85 °C part of the errors are reproducible flips, the same cells wrong at every hot power-up (Section VII-F), which a larger random noise does not represent. A chip with F fixed flips fails almost surely when F > t, so the failures concentrate on the chips with many flips, and one chip with one enrolment read does not show that spread. The code is therefore sized with a **two-component cell model over a chip population**. Cell *j* has the mismatch m<sub>j</sub>(T) = μ + m<sub>0,j</sub> cos θ(T) + m<sub>⊥,j</sub> sin θ(T), with m<sub>0</sub> and m<sub>⊥</sub> independent standard normal and μ the bias, and power-up noise of rms s(T); a rotation θ reverses the sign of a fixed fraction θ/π of the cells. s(T) follows from the disagreement between repeated power-ups at T, θ(T) from the error rate against the 25 °C enrolment; θ is taken with opposite signs below and above 25 °C (a monotonic change of the nMOS/pMOS mismatch weight). Each simulated chip draws its own cells and its own enrolment read, and the result is the fraction of chips that meet 10⁻⁶ and the 99th percentile of the t they require. s(T) and θ(T) are piecewise linear with a knot at 25 °C, so the worst case over 0–85 °C lies at 0, 25 or 85 °C.

**Theory: secrecy.** The helper data, the BCH syndrome over GF(2¹⁰), is 10t public bits, so the secret left in the fingerprint is n·H<sub>∞</sub> − 10t bits, where H<sub>∞</sub> = −log<sub>2</sub> max(P(1), 1 − P(1)) is the min-entropy of one cell and P(1) the probability that a cell powers up to 1. P(1) is estimated from a finite number of simulated cells, so H<sub>∞</sub> is bounded from below by the one-sided 95 % Clopper–Pearson upper bound on max(P(1), 1 − P(1)): P(1) = 0.5 by the symmetry of the cell, plus a bias margin that covers the observed bias and its sampling error. The budget is reported as an interval, from this lower bound to the point estimate. The key is a hash of the corrected fingerprint; by the leftover-hash lemma, a 128-bit key within statistical distance ε of uniform requires at least 128 + 2·log<sub>2</sub>(1/ε) bits of min-entropy. With ε = 2⁻³² (and SHA-256 treated as a universal hash), **the requirement is 192 secret bits**, not 128. Spatial correlation between cells, which would lower the entropy further, is not modelled: the simulated cells are independent.

**Prediction.** With P(1) = 0.493 from 1,024 cells, the lower bound on H<sub>∞</sub> is near 0.91 bit (point estimate 0.979), so 600 cells hold about 545–588 bits and the 192-bit requirement allows t ≈ 35 at the lower bound. At 85 °C the simulated error rate of 3.14 % gives 18.8 flipped cells on average; if about half of them are fixed flips, the spread between chips is that of the flip count, and the 99th-percentile chip needs roughly t ≈ 40, more than the secrecy bound allows.

**Setup.** Behavioural level (the Section V model), with the circuit values from the post-layout results of Section VII-D (the recorded full run of 1,024 cells × 8 power-ups for the PUF) and the schematic values alongside for comparison. Population: 1,000 Monte Carlo chips of 600 cells (the two-component cell model fitted to the post-layout SPICE Monte Carlo), each enrolled by one simulated noisy read at 25 °C (seeded from `chip_seed`); s(T) from the mean disagreement between the 28 pairs of power-ups at each of −40, 25 and 85 °C of the recorded run, θ(T) from its error rates (1.37 %, 0.99 % and 3.14 %). The 85 °C error rate carries a 95 % bootstrap interval over cells (2.20–4.11 %); the population is evaluated at both ends as well, so that the required t is an interval. Secrecy: P(1) and its bound from the 1,024 cells. For comparison, the earlier method (a noise-only model of this chip, one enrolment read, anchored to the same error rates) and the linear law are sized by the same 10⁻⁶ criterion; the schematic values by the earlier method. The behavioural simulations of the later sections keep the code of the earlier sizing, the largest t that leaves 128 secret bits at the point estimate (t = 45), so that their results and the RTL of Section XII stay comparable; the card states whether that code meets the two requirements. The sizing is then repeated with the law and s<sub>25</sub> = 0.06, the other settings unchanged, as a robustness check, because the simulated noise is thermal only and therefore a lower bound.

> **Next cell.** 1. Derives the first integrator's thermal noise from the 9.48 pA measured in [1]. 2. Replaces the model's illustrative settings with the circuit results (comparator noise; PUF noise, temperature coefficient and bias), from the schematic and from the extracted layout, and tabulates both. 3. Sizes the BCH code from the simulated error rates of the extracted cell (and, for comparison, with the linear law and from the schematic error rates). 4. Repeats the sizing with the conservative s<sub>25</sub> = 0.06.


```python
#@title Set the model's circuit parameters and size the BCH code
# Everything the rest of the notebook uses, now from SKY130 simulation of the extracted layouts or the paper's measurements
# 1. modulator thermal noise from the paper's 9.48 pA rms (100 kHz) at the TIA input, referred to the modulator
#    input (TIA gain, x0.5 buffer, full scale VDD/2) and spread over the 5 MHz Nyquist band of one clock; the model adds
#    int_noise to the first integrator's output, where an input-referred noise appears multiplied by g1 = 0.5
v_tia = 9.48e-12 * DEFAULTS["rtia"]
int_noise_in = v_tia * DEFAULTS["buffer"] / (VDD / 2) * np.sqrt((FS / 2) / 100e3)    # referred to the modulator input
int_noise = 0.5 * int_noise_in                                                       # at the first integrator's output
cal_from = lambda comp, fit: dict(comp_noise=float(comp["comp_noise"]), int_noise=float(int_noise), puf_sigma=float(fit["s25"]),
                                  puf_tc=float(fit["tc"]), puf_bias=float(fit["bias"]))
CAL_SCH, CAL = cal_from(COMP, PUF_FIT), cal_from(COMP_POST, PUF_FIT_POST)      # schematic, and post-layout (used)
before = {k: DEFAULTS[k] for k in CAL}

# 2. BCH strength, first by the earlier method (kept for comparison): one chip, a noise-only cell model whose noise-to-mismatch
#    ratio s(T) reproduces the simulated bit-error rate at each temperature (interpolated linearly in between; anchor_s and
#    anchored() also give the cell model of each process corner in Section VII-F). The linear law s25 (1 + a|T - 25 °C|)
#    is symmetric about 25 °C and underestimates the 85 °C rate; it is sized as a second comparison.
from scipy.optimize import brentq
_mref, _nref = rng_for(99).standard_normal(8192), rng_for(100).standard_normal(8192)
def anchor_s(mu, ber, s_enrol=None):
    """s at which the model's mean error rate (cells N(mu, 1) enrolled by one read with noise s_enrol) equals ber."""
    m = _mref + mu
    err = lambda s0, s: np.where(m + s0 * _nref > 0, ndtr(-m / s), ndtr(m / s)).mean()
    f = (lambda s: err(s, s) - ber) if s_enrol is None else (lambda s: err(s_enrol, s) - ber)
    lo, hi = 1e-4, (4.0 if s_enrol is None else 20.0)
    if f(lo) >= 0:                    # below the floor that the noisy enrolment read sets: the closest the model can get
        return lo
    return brentq(f, lo, hi) if f(hi) > 0 else hi
def anchored(mu, ber_T):
    """s(T), T in deg C, from the measured error rates {T: ber} against a 25 °C enrolment."""
    s25 = anchor_s(mu, ber_T[25]); sT = {T: (s25 if T == 25 else anchor_s(mu, b, s25)) for T, b in ber_T.items()}
    return lambda T: float(np.interp(T, sorted(sT), [sT[x] for x in sorted(sT)]))
def size_bch(mu, ber, bias):
    """(t that meets 1e-6 over 0-85 °C or None, largest t leaving 128 secret bits, P(more than t errors) for t = 0..120)."""
    s_of = anchored(mu, dict(zip(TEMPS, ber)))
    puf = SRAMPUF(DEFAULTS["chip_seed"], PUF_BITS, s_of(25), bias, 0.0)
    w_ = puf.read(25, rng_for(DEFAULTS["chip_seed"] * 7919 + 1)); worst_ = np.zeros(121)
    for T in range(0, 86, 5):
        s = s_of(T); pe = np.where(w_ == 1, ndtr(-puf.mismatch / s), ndtr(puf.mismatch / s))
        worst_ = np.maximum(worst_, np.cumsum(err_dist(pe)[::-1])[::-1][1:122])
    t_sec = max(t for t in range(121) if puf_residual({**DEFAULTS, "puf_bias": bias, "bch_t": t}) >= 128)
    return next((t for t in range(121) if worst_[t] < 1e-6), None), t_sec, worst_
def size_law(cal):                         # the same criterion with the linear law of Section VII-C (comparison only)
    Pl = {**DEFAULTS, **cal}
    puf = SRAMPUF(Pl["chip_seed"], PUF_BITS, Pl["puf_sigma"], Pl["puf_bias"], Pl["puf_tc"])
    wl = enroll(puf, 40, rng_for(Pl["chip_seed"] * 7919 + 1))["w"]
    dists = {T: err_dist(puf.p_err(wl, T)) for T in range(0, 86, 5)}
    return next((t for t in range(5, 121) if max(d[t + 1:].sum() for d in dists.values()) < 1e-6), None)
from scipy.special import ndtri
from scipy.stats import beta as _beta
BER_POST = [r["ber"] for r in an_post["rows"]] if PUF_MODE == "full" else PUF_POST_FULL["ber"]   # 1,024 cells x 8 power-ups
BER_SCH = [r["ber"] for r in an["rows"]]
t_meet, t_secret, worst = size_bch(float(ndtri(CAL["puf_bias"])), BER_POST, CAL["puf_bias"])
t_meet_sch, t_secret_sch, _ = size_bch(float(ndtri(CAL_SCH["puf_bias"])), BER_SCH, CAL_SCH["puf_bias"])
t_law = size_law(CAL)
i85 = TEMPS.index(85); ber85_law = float(ps.model_ber([85], CAL["puf_sigma"], CAL["puf_tc"], float(ndtri(CAL["puf_bias"])))[0])

# 3. The secret budget as an interval (review M2). The min-entropy per cell is bounded from below by the one-sided 95 %
#    Clopper-Pearson upper bound on max(P(1), 1 - P(1)), i.e. P(1) = 0.5 plus a bias margin of the observed bias and its
#    sampling error; the upper end of the interval is the point estimate. The 128-bit key is hashed from the fingerprint, so by
#    the leftover-hash lemma the secret must exceed 128 + 2 log2(1/eps) bits for a key within statistical distance eps of
#    uniform; eps = 2^-32 (SHA-256 is treated as a universal hash). Spatial correlation between cells is not modelled (the
#    SPICE draws are independent).
EPS_HASH = 2.0 ** -32
SECRET_REQ = 128 + int(round(2 * np.log2(1 / EPS_HASH)))                       # 192 bits
def h_bounds(ones, n, conf=0.95):
    """Min-entropy per cell: (lower confidence bound, point estimate), from `ones` of n cells powering up to 1."""
    k = max(int(ones), n - int(ones))
    return float(-np.log2(_beta.ppf(conf, k + 1, n - k))), float(-np.log2(k / n))
budget = lambda h, t, n=PUF_BITS: int(np.floor(n * h - 10 * t))                 # secret bits left after 10t helper bits
N_POST = PUF_POST_FULL["n_cells"]
H_TT = (h_bounds(round(CAL["puf_bias"] * N_POST), N_POST)[0], min_ent_bit(CAL["puf_bias"]))   # 1,024-cell post-layout run (tt)
t_bound = max(t for t in range(121) if budget(H_TT[0], t) >= SECRET_REQ)     # largest t meeting the requirement at the bound

# 4. Flip-aware key reliability over a chip population (review M3). Two-component cell model: cell i has the mismatch
#    m_i(T) = mu + m0_i cos(theta(T)) + mp_i sin(theta(T)) (m0, mp independent standard normal; theta, the rotation of
#    Section VII-F, makes a reproducible set of cells change sign) and power-up noise of rms s(T). s(T) comes from the
#    disagreement between repeated power-ups at T, theta(T) from the bit-error rate against the 25 °C enrolment; theta has the
#    opposite sign below 25 °C (a monotonic change of the nMOS/pMOS weight). Each chip is enrolled by its own noisy read(s);
#    P(fail) is exact per chip (Poisson-binomial). s(T) and theta(T) are piecewise linear with a knot at 25 °C, so the worst
#    case over 0-85 °C lies at 0, 25 or 85 °C.
_m0, _mp, _ne = rng_for(201).standard_normal(16384), rng_for(202).standard_normal(16384), rng_for(203).standard_normal(16384)
def s_from_q(mu, q):
    """Noise-to-mismatch ratio at which two power-ups of cells N(mu, 1) disagree with probability q."""
    m = _m0 + mu
    return brentq(lambda s: (2 * ndtr(m / s) * ndtr(-m / s)).mean() - q, 1e-5, 5.0)
def theta_from_ber(mu, s_e, s_T, ber):
    """Rotation (rad) at which a read with noise s_T disagrees with a one-read enrolment (noise s_e) with probability ber."""
    w = mu + _m0 + s_e * _ne > 0
    def f(th):
        m = mu + _m0 * np.cos(th) + _mp * np.sin(th)
        return np.where(w, ndtr(-m / s_T), ndtr(m / s_T)).mean() - ber
    return 0.0 if f(0.0) >= 0 else brentq(f, 0.0, np.pi / 2)
def two_component(mu, ber, q):
    """{T: s(T)}, {T: signed theta(T)} from the bit-error rates {T: ber} (25 °C enrolment) and power-up disagreements {T: q}."""
    sT = {T: s_from_q(mu, v) for T, v in q.items()}
    th = {T: (0.0 if T == 25 else np.sign(T - 25) * theta_from_ber(mu, sT[25], sT[T], ber[T])) for T in q}
    return sT, th
from numba import prange
@njit(cache=False, parallel=True)
def fail_tails(p, tmax):
    """P(more than t of the cells err), t = 0..tmax, for each row of p: exact, the probability mass leaving 'at most t'."""
    C, n = p.shape
    out = np.zeros((C, tmax + 1))
    for c in prange(C):
        d = np.zeros(tmax + 1); d[0] = 1.0
        for i in range(n):
            q = p[c, i]
            for k in range(tmax, 0, -1):
                out[c, k] += d[k] * q
                d[k] = d[k] * (1 - q) + d[k - 1] * q
            out[c, 0] += d[0] * q
            d[0] *= 1 - q
    return out
def chip_population(mu, sT, th, enrol=(25,), n_chips=1000, n_arr=PUF_BITS, n_key=PUF_BITS, reads=3, temps=(0, 25, 85),
                    tmax=120, seed=0):
    """Worst P(fail) over temps for t = 0..tmax, per chip, and the t each chip requires for 1e-6 (tmax + 1: none).
    enrol = (25,): one read at 25 °C; (Ta, Tb): `reads` reads at each, the cells stable and equal at both kept (enrolled
    value: the first read at Ta), the first n_key kept cells of the n_arr-cell array used (fewer kept: the chip fails)."""
    r = rng_for(seed); Ts = sorted(sT)
    s_of = lambda T: float(np.interp(T, Ts, [sT[x] for x in Ts])); th_of = lambda T: float(np.interp(T, Ts, [th[x] for x in Ts]))
    m0, mp = r.standard_normal((n_chips, n_arr)), r.standard_normal((n_chips, n_arr))
    mT = lambda T: mu + m0 * np.cos(th_of(T)) + mp * np.sin(th_of(T))
    read = lambda T: mT(T) + s_of(T) * r.standard_normal((n_chips, n_arr)) > 0
    if len(enrol) == 1:
        w, idx, kept = read(enrol[0]), None, None
    else:
        Ra, Rb = (np.stack([read(T) for _ in range(reads)]) for T in enrol)
        keep = (Ra.all(0) | ~Ra.any(0)) & (Rb.all(0) | ~Rb.any(0)) & (Ra[0] == Rb[0])
        w, kept = Ra[0], keep.sum(1)
        idx = np.argsort(~keep, axis=1, kind="stable")[:, :n_key]             # the first n_key kept cells
    worst = np.zeros((n_chips, tmax + 1))
    for T in temps:
        p = np.where(w, ndtr(-mT(T) / s_of(T)), ndtr(mT(T) / s_of(T)))
        worst = np.maximum(worst, fail_tails(p if idx is None else np.take_along_axis(p, idx, 1), tmax))
    if kept is not None:
        worst[kept < n_key] = 1.0
    ok = worst <= 1e-6
    return dict(worst=worst, kept=kept, treq=np.where(ok.any(1), ok.argmax(1), tmax + 1))
# the recorded 1,024-cell post-layout run: mean disagreement between the 28 pairs of its 8 power-ups at each temperature and the
# reproducible flips at 85 °C (dev/spice_puf/results/full_ng41_postlayout/bits.npy; recomputed from the live bits in full mode)
Q_POST = {-40: 0.012137, 25: 0.010917, 85: 0.016009}; FLIP85_POST = 0.0146
if PUF_MODE == "full" and mc_post["bits"].shape[2] >= 1024:
    _b = mc_post["bits"]; _R = _b.shape[1]
    Q_POST = {T: float(np.mean([(_b[i, a] != _b[i, c]).mean() for a in range(_R) for c in range(a + 1, _R)])) for i, T in enumerate(TEMPS)}
    _st = _b[i85].min(0) == _b[i85].max(0); FLIP85_POST = float((_st & (_b[i85, 0] != _b[TEMPS.index(25), 0])).mean())
mu_post = float(ndtri(CAL["puf_bias"]))
BER85_CI = PUF_POST_FULL["ber_ci"][i85]                                     # 95 % bootstrap interval over cells
POP = {}
for lab, b85 in (("lo", BER85_CI[0]), ("mid", BER_POST[i85]), ("hi", BER85_CI[1])):
    sT_, th_ = two_component(mu_post, {**dict(zip(TEMPS, BER_POST)), 85: b85}, Q_POST)
    POP[lab] = dict(chip_population(mu_post, sT_, th_, seed=DEFAULTS["chip_seed"]), sT=sT_, th=th_)
t99 = {k: int(np.percentile(v["treq"], 99, method="higher")) for k, v in POP.items()}
t50 = int(np.median(POP["mid"]["treq"]))

# 5. The code of the behavioural simulations. Sections VIII to XII (and the RTL of Section XII) keep
#    the code of the earlier sizing, t = the largest value leaving 128 secret bits at the point estimate of P(1); the card
#    states whether it meets the reliability target (population, upper end of the 85 °C interval) and the secrecy requirement
#    (lower bound of the budget). The schematic column uses the same rule.
t_star, t_sch = t_secret, t_secret_sch
REL_MET = t99["hi"] <= t_star
SEC_MET = budget(H_TT[0], t_star) >= SECRET_REQ
TARGET_MET = REL_MET and SEC_MET
CAL["bch_t"], CAL_SCH["bch_t"], before["bch_t"] = t_star, t_sch, DEFAULTS["bch_t"]
P = {**DEFAULTS, **CAL}
w = enroll(SRAMPUF(P["chip_seed"], PUF_BITS, P["puf_sigma"], P["puf_bias"], P["puf_tc"]), 40, rng_for(P["chip_seed"] * 7919 + 1))["w"]

src = dict(comp_noise="StrongARM noise of the extracted layout (Section VII-D), σn / (VDD/4)",
           int_noise="paper's 9.48 pA, referred to the modulator input (1.80e-5 FS) and multiplied by g1 = 0.5 at the first integrator's output",
           puf_sigma="SRAM-PUF Monte Carlo of the extracted cell (Section VII-D), noise / mismatch at 25 °C",
           puf_tc="the same Monte Carlo, temperature fit", puf_bias="the same Monte Carlo, fraction of cells powering up to 1",
           bch_t="the code of the behavioural simulations: the largest t that leaves 128 secret bits at the point estimate of P(1) "
                 "(the card below gives its reliability and its secret budget)")
table(["Setting", "Before", "Schematic", "Post-layout (used)", "Source"],
      [(f"<code>{k}</code>", f"{before[k]:.4g}", f"{CAL_SCH[k]:.4g}", f"<b>{CAL[k]:.4g}</b>", src[k]) for k in CAL],
      caption="Table VIII: model settings replaced by SKY130 simulation (post-layout) and the measurements of [1]",
      align=["left", "right", "right", "right", "left"])
pct = lambda v: f"{100 * v:.1f} %"
card(f"BCH code and secret budget (post-layout, {PUF_BITS} cells, 25 °C enrolment, {len(POP['mid']['treq']):,} simulated chips): t = {t_star}",
     [("simulated bit-error rate, " + ", ".join(f"{T} °C" for T in TEMPS).replace("-", "−"), ", ".join(f"{100 * b:.2f} %" for b in BER_POST)
       + f" (85 °C: 95 % interval {100 * BER85_CI[0]:.2f}–{100 * BER85_CI[1]:.2f} %)"),
      ("two-component cell model at 85 °C", f"noise s = {POP['mid']['sT'][85]:.3f} (from repeated power-ups), rotation θ = "
       f"{np.degrees(POP['mid']['th'][85]):.1f}°: θ/π = {pct(POP['mid']['th'][85] / np.pi)} of the cells change sign "
       f"(reproducible flips counted in the recorded bits: {pct(FLIP85_POST)})"),
      ("t required for P(key fails) &lt; 10<sup>−6</sup> over 0–85 °C: median, 99th percentile of the chips",
       f"{t50}, <b>{t99['mid']}</b> (99th percentile {t99['lo']}–{t99['hi']} over the 85 °C interval)"),
      (f"chips meeting 10<sup>−6</sup> at t = {t_star}", f"<b>{pct(np.mean(POP['mid']['treq'] <= t_star))}</b> "
       f"({pct(min(np.mean(v['treq'] <= t_star) for v in POP.values()))} to {pct(max(np.mean(v['treq'] <= t_star) for v in POP.values()))} over the 85 °C interval)"),
      ("for comparison: noise-only model of one chip (the earlier method); linear law",
       f"t = {t_meet if t_meet is not None else '&gt; 120'}; t = {t_law} (the law gives {100 * ber85_law:.2f} % at 85 °C, against "
       f"{100 * BER_POST[i85]:.2f} % simulated)"),
      (f"min-entropy per cell, P(1) = {CAL['puf_bias']:.3f} from {N_POST:,} cells: 95 % lower bound – point estimate",
       f"{H_TT[0]:.3f}–{H_TT[1]:.3f} bit"),
      (f"secret bits left after publishing h at t = {t_star}", f"<b>{budget(H_TT[0], t_star)}–{budget(H_TT[1], t_star)}</b> "
       f"(need ≥ {SECRET_REQ} = 128 + 2 log<sub>2</sub>(1/ε), ε = 2<sup>−32</sup>)"),
      (f"largest t that leaves {SECRET_REQ} secret bits at the lower bound", f"t = {t_bound}"),
      ("the same sizing from the schematic values (noise-only, one chip)", f"t = {t_meet_sch} required; 128 secret bits at the point "
       f"estimate up to t = {t_secret_sch}"),
      ("verdict", "<b>both limits met</b>" if TARGET_MET else
       ("<b>reliable, not secret enough</b>" if REL_MET else "<b>neither limit met over the 85 °C interval</b>" if not SEC_MET else "<b>secret, not reliable</b>")
       + f": with {PUF_BITS} cells and a 25 °C enrolment, reliability needs t ≥ {t99['hi']} and secrecy allows t ≤ {t_bound}; "
       f"t = {t_star} is kept for the behavioural simulations, and Sections VIII-F and XI size the final key generator")],
     tone="ok" if TARGET_MET else "bad")
DEFAULTS.update(CAL)                       # every section below runs on these values (the explorer link of Section XIII too)

# robustness: the SPICE cell has thermal noise only (no 1/f, RTN or supply noise), so s25 is a lower bound.
# With the conservative s25 = 0.06 (the value assumed before the SKY130 simulations), what would the code need?
pc = SRAMPUF(P["chip_seed"], PUF_BITS, 0.06, P["puf_bias"], P["puf_tc"])
dc = {T: err_dist(pc.p_err(w, T)) for T in range(0, 86, 5)}
t_cons = next((t for t in range(5, 61) if max(d[t + 1:].sum() for d in dc.values()) < 1e-6), None)
card(f"Robustness check with the conservative noise s<sub>25</sub> = 0.06 ({0.06 / CAL['puf_sigma']:.1f}× the SPICE value)",
     [("BCH strength needed (linear law, this chip)", (f"t = {t_cons}, leaving {max(0, budget(H_TT[0], t_cons))}–{budget(H_TT[1], t_cons)} secret bits" if budget(H_TT[1], t_cons) > 0
       else f"t = {t_cons}, which leaves no secret bits") + f" (need ≥ {SECRET_REQ})" if t_cons else "no t up to 60 meets 10<sup>−6</sup> with 600 cells")],
     note="The SPICE cell has thermal noise only, so real silicon may need more cells or a concatenated code (Section XV).", tone="bad")

**Result.** Table VIII lists the settings assumed before the simulations, from the schematic and from the extracted layout. The comparator noise becomes `comp_noise` = 1.279 × 10⁻³ (from 10⁻³), the PUF's noise-to-mismatch ratio 0.02253 (from 0.06), its temperature coefficient 0.02051 (from 0.008) and its bias 0.4928 (from 0.5); `int_noise` = 0.899 × 10⁻⁵ at the first integrator's output (1.80 × 10⁻⁵ referred to the modulator input) is essentially the value already used (0.9 × 10⁻⁵).

* *Cell model at 85 °C.* The repeated power-ups give a noise of s = 0.035; the rest of the 3.14 % error rate is a rotation θ = 4.9°, so θ/π = 2.7 % of the cells change sign. The recorded bits count 1.5 % reproducible flips (cells wrong in all eight hot power-ups); the remaining sign changes lie near the threshold and are also unstable.
* *Reliability over the population.* Over the 1,000 Monte Carlo chips, the t required for 10⁻⁶ from 0 to 85 °C has a median of 29 and a **99th percentile of 39**; across the 85 °C interval the 99th percentile ranges from 33 to 46. At t = 45, all chips meet the target at the point estimate, and 98.9 % at the upper end of the interval.
* *Comparison.* The earlier noise-only sizing of the one simulated chip (the recorded 1,024-cell post-layout run) requires t = 48, the linear law t = 32 (it gives 1.75 % at 85 °C against 3.14 % simulated); the schematic values, by the earlier method, require t = 41.
* *Secrecy.* The min-entropy per cell lies between 0.908 bit (95 % lower bound) and 0.979 bit (point estimate). At t = 45, **94–137 secret bits** remain after the helper data is published, against the 192 required; at the lower bound, 192 bits allow at most t = 35.
* *Verdict.* With 600 cells and a 25 °C enrolment, reliability over the 85 °C interval needs t ≥ 46 and secrecy allows t ≤ 35: neither the code of the simulations (t = 45) nor any other meets both. With the conservative s<sub>25</sub> = 0.06 (2.7× the SPICE value), the law requires t = 60, which leaves no secret bits.

**Interpretation.** The SKY130 values lower the PUF's noise-to-mismatch ratio by a factor of 2.7, but the temperature dependence is stronger than assumed: the simulated error rate at 85 °C is 3.2 times that at 25 °C. Two corrections to the earlier sizing pull in opposite directions. The flip-aware population model needs a weaker code than the noise-only model of one chip at the point estimate (99th percentile 39 against 48), because fixed flips vary less from power-up to power-up than the equivalent noise; the sampling interval of the 85 °C error rate, carried through, raises the 99th percentile to 46. The bounded entropy budget with a hash margin is the larger change: it lowers the strongest admissible code from t = 45 to t = 35. **With 600 cells enrolled once at 25 °C, the key generator does not meet the secrecy requirement and meets the reliability requirement only at the point estimate**, so t = 45 is a working setting for the system simulations, not the final key generator. The final key generator needs more entropy per corrected error: the enrolment at two temperatures of Section VIII-F, which removes the flipping cells and so allows a much weaker code, and the larger arrays of the compiler in Section XI, both sized with the same bounded budget. `DEFAULTS` now holds these values (t = 45), and every later section, including the explorer of Section XIII, runs on them. They were all obtained at the typical corner; Section VII-F asks how they change across process, voltage and temperature.

### F. Process, voltage and temperature corners

**Goal.** Measure how the noise, offset and energy of the extracted comparator, and the power-up statistics of the extracted SRAM cell, change across process, supply and temperature, and which physical mechanisms cause the changes. All results so far are at the typical corner; a fabricated chip lies elsewhere within the process spread, runs from a supply that deviates from 1.8 V, and works across the temperature range of its application.

**Theory: the comparator.** Each quantity of Section VII-B has a predictable first-order dependence:

* **Noise.** σ<sub>n</sub><sup>2</sup> ≈ (kT/C<sub>P</sub>)·4γ(I<sub>D</sub>/g<sub>m</sub>)/V<sub>TH</sub>. The kT term alone predicts a rise by √(398.15 K/233.15 K) = 1.31 from −40 to 125 °C. The integration ends when the output nodes have fallen by about one threshold voltage, so a corner or a temperature that lowers the threshold shortens the integration and adds noise beyond kT. A higher supply raises the input common mode (V<sub>DD</sub>/2) and with it the overdrive I<sub>D</sub>/g<sub>m</sub> of the input pair, which also adds noise.
* **Offset.** Pelgrom's law depends on device area, not on the process corner, which shifts the mean thresholds rather than their mismatch; σ<sub>os</sub> should therefore be nearly the same at all corners. It may rise when the integration gain decreases (hot), because the latch's mismatch is then referred to the input with less attenuation.
* **Energy.** The dynamic part, C<sub>sw</sub>V<sub>DD</sub><sup>2</sup>, should rise by (1.98/1.62)<sup>2</sup> = 1.49 from the lowest to the highest supply and not depend on temperature. Subthreshold leakage, which grows exponentially with temperature and is largest where the threshold is lowest, adds to it at hot, fast corners.

**Theory: the SRAM-PUF cell.** The power-up race is decided while V<sub>DD</sub> ramps through about 0.5–0.9 V, close to the threshold voltages. A process corner moves the nMOS and pMOS thresholds, in the same direction (ss, ff) or in opposite directions (sf: slow nMOS, fast pMOS; fs: fast nMOS, slow pMOS). This changes the supply at which a cell resolves and, above all, the relative weight of the nMOS and pMOS mismatch in its preference. Two kinds of error can therefore be expected against a 25 °C enrolment: noise errors, from cells that are unstable at every temperature, and reproducible flips, from cells whose preference reverses with temperature and which then take the opposite value in every power-up. The two respond differently to masking at enrolment: discarding the cells that are unstable at 25 °C removes noise errors only, whereas keeping only cells that are stable and agree at two enrolment temperatures (25 and 85 °C) also removes flips. The supply corner does not apply to this cell, because it decides long before V<sub>DD</sub> reaches its final value.

**Setup.** Both extracted cells of Section VII-D, at the five process corners of the PDK: tt; ss and ff, with both transistor types slow or fast; and sf and fs, with nMOS and pMOS skewed in opposite directions.

* **Comparator:** 45 conditions, the 5 corners × 1.62, 1.8 and 1.98 V (±10 %) × −40, 27 and 125 °C, each with the quick noise, offset (the same 96 instances) and energy measurements and seeds of Section VII-B on the extracted core, with the input common mode at V<sub>DD</sub>/2 (the noise-injection grid and window of Section VII-B were verified at tt and 27 °C only and are assumed at the other conditions); the systematic offset is the 50 % point μ of the noise fit of the mismatch-free comparator, which the layout sets.
* **SRAM-PUF cell:** the 5 corners × −40, 25 and 85 °C, 512 cells × 5 power-ups per temperature, with the Monte Carlo and seeds of Section VII-C on the extracted cell; the noise envelope is recomputed at each corner, and each corner receives the BER-matched fit of Section VII-C. The recorded run also contains power-ups at 125 °C, outside the specified 0–85 °C range; as in Sections VII-C and D, they are not used.
* **A cell model for each corner.** The cell model's linear temperature law cannot follow corners whose errors rise abruptly above 25 °C, so each corner receives a model anchored to its own simulated error rates: the noise-to-mismatch ratio s(T) that reproduces the simulated BER at each simulated temperature, interpolated in between. Section VIII-F evaluates the key with these models.
* **Error composition at 85 °C.** From the recorded bits: reproducible flips and unstable cells, and the error rate after each masking, cross-validated (the cells to keep are chosen from power-ups 1–3, the error rate is measured on the held-out power-ups 4–5).
* **Recorded runs.** Both grids are recorded runs of the same code with the same seeds, which require about 20 minutes (comparator) and 45 minutes (SRAM-PUF) on four cores, too long for a Colab session. Each script draws, checks and extracts the layout once and stops unless it is DRC- and LVS-clean. The comparator grid is regenerated with `python dev/spice_comparator/demo_pvt.py --pdk-root <pdk>`, the SRAM-PUF grid with `python dev/spice_puf/demo_pvt.py --pdk-root <pdk>`; the summary card of the next cell repeats both commands. The tables, the figure and the two analyses that follow are computed live from these records.

> **Next cell.** 1. Loads the recorded PVT grids of both extracted cells. 2. Tabulates the comparator across the 45 conditions, grouped by process corner, temperature and supply. 3. Tabulates the SRAM-PUF cell at every process corner and derives the cell model of each corner, the noise-to-mismatch ratio s(T) that reproduces each simulated error rate. 4. Decomposes the errors at 85 °C into reproducible flips and unstable cells, and measures the effect of masking at enrolment, cross-validated on held-out power-ups. 5. Prints a summary card with the commands that regenerate both grids.

":[{"T":-40,"bias":0.46992187500000004,"ber":0.025,"ber_ci":[0.0140625,0.037890625],"unstable":13},{"T":25,"bias":0.464453125,"ber":0.01953125,"ber_ci":[0.009765625,0.02978515625],"unstable":16},{"T":85,"bias":0.45585937499999996,"ber":0.01953125,"ber_ci":[0.01015625,0.03046875],"unstable":14}],"fit":{"s25":0.04315665912217613,"s25_ci95":null,"a":0.004117839889152635,"mu":-0.08922103315098846}},{"corner":"ff","rows":[{"T":-40,"bias":0.455078125,"ber":0.028125,"ber_ci":[0.016787109375,0.041015625],"unstable":18},{"T":25,"bias":0.448046875,"ber":0.0244140625,"ber_ci":[0.01416015625,0.03564453125],"unstable":26},{"T":85,"bias":0.47148437499999996,"ber":0.1,"ber_ci":[0.077333984375,0.12656250000000002],"unstable":20}],"fit":{"s25":0.057342602817183244,"s25_ci95":null,"a":0.018814601206353802,"mu":-0.13059746271067252}},{"corner":"sf","rows":[{"T":-40,"bias":0.48476562500000003,"ber":0.0484375,"ber_ci":[0.032802734375,0.0640625],"unstable":22},{"T":25,"bias":0.48046875,"ber":0.03369140625,"ber_ci":[0.02197265625,0.046875],"unstable":31},{"T":85,"bias":0.48398437499999997,"ber":0.05,"ber_ci":[0.034755859374999996,0.067587890625],"unstable":26}],"fit":{"s25":0.07523798919766786,"s25_ci95":null,"a":0.012954007771311577,"mu":-0.04897715720213194}},{"corner":"fs","rows":[{"T":-40,"bias":0.45234375000000004,"ber":0.01171875,"ber_ci":[0.00390625,0.02109375],"unstable":4},{"T":25,"bias":0.453125,"ber":0.0078125,"ber_ci":[0.00244140625,0.0146484375],"unstable":9},{"T":85,"bias":0.4890625,"ber":0.27812499999999996,"ber_ci":[0.24061523437500001,0.31368164062500004],"unstable":26}],"fit":{"s25":0.01859600808334736,"s25_ci95":null,"a":0.045218489294364846,"mu":-0.1177698745790953}}],"bits_shape":[5,3,5,512],"bits":""}}')
BITS = np.unpackbits(np.frombuffer(base64.b64decode(PVT["puf"].pop("bits")), np.uint8))[:np.prod(PVT["puf"]["bits_shape"])]
BITS = BITS.reshape(PVT["puf"]["bits_shape"])          # recorded power-up bits: corner, temperature, power-up, cell
# 3. the comparator across the grid, grouped by process corner, by temperature and by supply (each group averages the other two)
def _grp(sel):
    g = [r for r in PVT["cmp"] if sel(r)]
    x = lambda k, s: [s * r[k] for r in g]
    f = lambda v, d: f"{np.mean(v):.{d}f} ({min(v):.{d}f}–{max(v):.{d}f})"
    return (f(x("sigma_n", 1e3), 2), f(x("sigma_os", 1e3), 2), f"{max(np.abs(x('mu_n', 1e6))):.0f}", f(x("energy", 1e15), 0))
rows_c = [("process corner" if i == 0 else "", c, *_grp(lambda r, c=c: r["corner"] == c)) for i, c in enumerate(PVT["corners"])]
rows_c += [("temperature" if i == 0 else "", f"{t:+.0f} °C".replace("-", "−"), *_grp(lambda r, t=t: r["temp"] == t))
           for i, t in enumerate(sorted({r["temp"] for r in PVT["cmp"]}))]
rows_c += [("supply" if i == 0 else "", f"{v:.2f} V", *_grp(lambda r, v=v: r["vdd"] == v))
           for i, v in enumerate(sorted({r["vdd"] for r in PVT["cmp"]}))]
table(["Grouped by", "Value", "σ<sub>n</sub> (mV)", "σ<sub>os</sub> (mV)", "Systematic offset, max (µV)", "Energy (fJ)"], rows_c,
      caption="Table IX: extracted StrongARM comparator across the 45 PVT conditions (recorded run), grouped by process corner "
              "(each row over 3 supplies × 3 temperatures), by temperature and by supply (each over 5 corners × 3 values of the "
              "other); mean (minimum–maximum). Systematic offset: the 50 % point of the mismatch-free comparator, set by the layout")

# 4. a cell model for every corner. The linear temperature law of Section VII-E cannot follow the fast-nMOS corners,
#    whose errors jump above 25 °C (reproducible flips), so each corner gets a cell model anchored to its measurements: the
#    noise-to-mismatch ratio s(T) that reproduces the measured bit-error rate at each simulated temperature, interpolated
#    linearly in between. Section VIII-F evaluates the key with these models.
# (anchor_s and anchored(): defined with the BCH sizing of Section VII-E)
# two-temperature enrolment, cross-validated on the recorded bits: the mask (cells stable and equal at 25 and 85 °C) is chosen
# from power-ups 1-3, and the kept cells' error rate is measured on the held-out power-ups 4-5
E_RD, H_RD = [0, 1, 2], [3, 4]
i25, i85 = TEMPS.index(25), TEMPS.index(85)
rows_k, PUF_CELL = [], {}
for j, c in enumerate(PVT["puf"]["corners"]):
    b, mu = BITS[j], c["fit"]["mu"]; w0 = b[i25, 0]
    st3 = lambda i: b[i][E_RD].min(axis=0) == b[i][E_RD].max(axis=0)
    keep = st3(i25) & st3(i85) & (b[i25, E_RD[0]] == b[i85, E_RD[0]])
    floor = 0.5 / (keep.sum() * len(H_RD))                                  # half a count: no zero rates
    ber_k = {T: max(float((b[TEMPS.index(T)][H_RD][:, keep] != w0[keep]).mean()), floor) for T in TEMPS}
    s1 = anchored(mu, {x["T"]: x["ber"] for x in c["rows"]})                 # 25 °C enrolment
    s2 = anchored(mu, ber_k)                                                 # 25 + 85 °C enrolment, kept cells
    PUF_CELL[c["corner"]] = dict(mu=mu, s1=s1, s2=s2, keep=float(keep.mean()), ber_k=ber_k,
                                 st25=float((b[i85][H_RD][:, st3(i25)] != w0[st3(i25)]).mean()))
    r = {x["T"]: x for x in c["rows"]}
    rows_k.append((c["corner"], f"{r[25]['bias']:.3f}", f"{100 * r[25]['ber']:.2f} %", f"{100 * r[85]['ber']:.2f} %",
                   f"{s1(25):.3f} / {s1(85):.3f}", f"{r[25]['unstable']}"))
table(["Corner", "P(1), 25 °C", "BER 25 °C", "BER 85 °C", "s(25 °C) / s(85 °C)", "Unstable cells, 25 °C"],
      rows_k, caption=f"Table X: extracted SRAM-PUF cell at every process corner ({PVT['puf']['settings']['n_cells']} cells × "
                      f"{PVT['puf']['settings']['repeats']} power-ups per temperature, recorded run), against a 25 °C enrolment. s(T): the "
                      f"noise-to-mismatch ratio that reproduces the measured error rate at each simulated temperature (interpolated in "
                      f"between), the cell model of each corner; unstable: cells whose value varies between the power-ups at 25 °C. P(1) from "
                      f"{PVT['puf']['settings']['n_cells']} cells has a sampling error of about ±2 %")
# 5. what the errors at 85 °C consist of, from the recorded bits: cells that flip reproducibly (the same value in all power-ups at
#    85 °C, opposite to the enrolment) and cells that are unstable; and what masking at enrolment does to them (cross-validated)
rows_f = []
for j, c in enumerate(PVT["puf"]["corners"]):
    b = BITS[j]; w0 = b[i25, 0]; st = b.min(axis=1) == b.max(axis=1); q = PUF_CELL[c["corner"]]
    rows_f.append((c["corner"], f"{100 * (b[i85] != w0).mean():.1f} %", f"{100 * (st[i85] & (b[i85, 0] != w0)).mean():.1f} %",
                   f"{100 * (~st[i85]).mean():.1f} %", f"{100 * q['st25']:.1f} %", f"{100 * q['keep']:.0f} %",
                   f"<b>{100 * q['ber_k'][85]:.2f} %</b>", f"{int(np.ceil(PUF_BITS / q['keep']))}"))
table(["Corner", "BER 85 °C", "Reproducible flips", "Unstable cells", "BER 85 °C, masked at 25 °C",
       "Kept, masked at 25 and 85 °C", "BER 85 °C of the kept cells", f"Array for {PUF_BITS} kept cells"], rows_f,
      caption=f"Table XI: composition of the SRAM-PUF errors at 85 °C against the 25 °C enrolment, and the effect of masking "
              f"at enrolment (recorded bits, {PVT['puf']['settings']['n_cells']} cells × {PVT['puf']['settings']['repeats']} power-ups "
              f"per temperature). Reproducible flips: cells with the same value in every power-up at 85 °C, opposite to the "
              f"enrolment; unstable: cells whose value varies between power-ups. Masking is cross-validated: the cells to keep "
              f"(stable at 25 °C; or stable and equal at 25 and 85 °C) are chosen from power-ups 1–3, and the error rates are "
              f"measured on the held-out power-ups 4–5")
rng_ = lambda k: (min(r[k] for r in PVT["cmp"]), max(r[k] for r in PVT["cmp"]))
card("Process, voltage and temperature corners: summary",
     [("comparator, 45 conditions (5 corners × 1.62/1.8/1.98 V × −40/27/125 °C)",
       f"σ<sub>n</sub> {1e3 * rng_('sigma_n')[0]:.2f}–{1e3 * rng_('sigma_n')[1]:.2f} mV, σ<sub>os</sub> {1e3 * rng_('sigma_os')[0]:.2f}–"
       f"{1e3 * rng_('sigma_os')[1]:.2f} mV, energy {1e15 * rng_('energy')[0]:.0f}–{1e15 * rng_('energy')[1]:.0f} fJ per decision"),
      ("SRAM-PUF, 5 process corners × " + "/".join(str(T) for T in TEMPS).replace("-", "−") + " °C", f"{PVT['puf']['settings']['n_cells']} cells × "
       f"{PVT['puf']['settings']['repeats']} power-ups per temperature at every corner"),
      ("SRAM-PUF errors at 85 °C (25 °C enrolment)", ", ".join(f"{c['corner']} {100 * next(x['ber'] for x in c['rows'] if x['T'] == 85):.1f} %"
                                                               for c in PVT["puf"]["corners"])),
      ("source", "recorded runs; to regenerate: <code>python dev/spice_comparator/demo_pvt.py --pdk-root &lt;pdk&gt;</code> (about "
       "20 min on four cores) and <code>python dev/spice_puf/demo_pvt.py --pdk-root &lt;pdk&gt;</code> (about 45 min)")], tone="ok")

Marks the mean at each temperature, which shows whether temperature or process sets the level. 3. Plots the SRAM-PUF cell's bit-error rate against a 25 °C enrolment at each process corner.


```python
#@title Fig.: PVT corners of both extracted cells
# The recorded PVT grids at a glance: the comparator's noise and offset at the 45 conditions, grouped by process corner, with
# the mean at each temperature, and the SRAM-PUF cell's bit-error rate against a 25 C enrolment at each process corner
corners = list(PVT["corners"])
tcol, vmark = {-40.0: COL["ok"], 27.0: COL["aqua"], 125.0: COL["bad"]}, {1.62: "v", 1.8: "o", 1.98: "^"}
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(W2, 3.1))
for ax, (key, scale, unit, lab, title) in zip(axs[:2], (("sigma_n", 1e3, r"$\sigma_\mathrm{n}$ (mV)", "a", "comparator noise"),
                                                    ("sigma_os", 1e3, r"$\sigma_\mathrm{os}$ (mV)", "b", "comparator offset"))):
    for r in PVT["cmp"]:
        x = corners.index(r["corner"]) + 0.26 * (list(tcol).index(r["temp"]) - 1) + 0.07 * (list(vmark).index(r["vdd"]) - 1)
        ax.plot(x, scale * r[key], vmark[r["vdd"]], color=tcol[r["temp"]], ms=5, mec=COL["ink"], mew=0.4)
    for t, c in tcol.items():                       # the mean at each temperature: temperature, not process, sets the level
        m = scale * np.mean([r[key] for r in PVT["cmp"] if r["temp"] == t])
        ax.axhline(m, color=c, lw=0.9, ls=":", zorder=0)
        ax.annotate(f"{m:.2f}", (1, m), xycoords=("axes fraction", "data"), xytext=(3, 0), textcoords="offset points",
                    ha="left", va="center", fontsize=7.5, color=c)
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(corners)), corners); ax.set_ylabel(unit); ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False); panel(ax, lab, title)
h = [plt.Line2D([], [], ls="", marker="s", color=c, label=f"{t:+.0f} °C".replace("-", "−")) for t, c in tcol.items()]
h += [plt.Line2D([], [], ls="", marker=m, color=COL["faint"], label=f"{v:.2f} V") for v, m in vmark.items()]
pcol = {"tt": COL["ink"], "ss": COL["ok"], "ff": COL["bad"], "sf": COL["aqua"], "fs": COL["yellow"]}
for c in PVT["puf"]["corners"]:                      # (c) the SRAM-PUF cell's bit-error rate at each corner (tt dashed)
    Tc = TEMPS[:len(c["rows"])]
    axs[2].plot(Tc, [100 * x["ber"] for x in c["rows"]], "o-" if c["corner"] != "tt" else "s--", color=pcol[c["corner"]],
                mfc="white", lw=1.5, ms=4, label=c["corner"])
axs[2].set_xticks(Tc); axs[2].set_xlabel("Temperature (°C)"); axs[2].set_ylabel("BER vs 25 °C enrolment (%)")
axs[2].legend(ncol=2, fontsize=7, loc="upper left"); panel(axs[2], "c", "SRAM-PUF errors")
fig.legend(handles=h, ncol=6, fontsize=7.5, loc="lower center", frameon=False)   # below the panels: no marker is hidden
fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.08, 1, 1)); plt.show()
```

<p align="center" style="text-align:center"><b>Fig. 34.</b> Extracted cells across PVT (recorded grids). (a) Comparator input-referred noise σ<sub>n</sub> and (b) offset spread σ<sub>os</sub> (96 Monte Carlo instances) at the five process corners, three supplies (marker shape) and three temperatures (colour); dotted: mean at each temperature. (c) SRAM-PUF bit-error rate against a 25 °C enrolment, one line per process corner (tt dashed).</p>

**Result.** Fig. 34 shows both recorded grids at a glance, so that the observations below can be checked by eye before they are read from the tables. In panels (a) and (b), of process, supply and temperature, temperature dominates the comparator's noise and offset over the 45 PVT conditions, as the means at each temperature (dotted lines) show. Panel (c) shows the opposite for the SRAM-PUF cell: there the process corner decides how the error rate responds to temperature; the ss curve stays nearly flat, tt rises moderately, and the fast-nMOS corners ff and fs rise steeply above 25 °C, fs from the lowest error rate of all corners at 25 °C to the highest at 85 °C. Table IX, Table X and Table XI give the following observations, each compared with the theory above; their consequences for the system follow in Section VIII.

*Comparator* (Table IX).

1. **The noise is governed by temperature and by the pMOS corner.** The mean input-referred noise rises from 0.47 mV at −40 °C to 0.77 mV at 125 °C, a factor of 1.64, against 1.31 for the kT dependence alone: the excess is the shorter integration that the theory predicts at lower thresholds. At a fixed supply and temperature, the five process corners differ by at most a factor of 1.26 at eight of the nine supply–temperature pairs. The ninth, 1.62 V and −40 °C, reaches 1.56 because of a single point: ss gives σ<sub>n</sub> = 0.574 mV there, where the other four corners give 0.37–0.45 mV and ss itself gives 0.45 mV at 1.8 V. This outlier is not explained by the first-order theory and was not investigated; the noise-injection window, verified at tt and 27 °C only, is the least certain at this slowest condition. On average, the corners with fast pMOS (ff and sf, 0.62 and 0.63 mV) are noisier than those with slow pMOS (ss and fs, 0.59 and 0.58 mV), whereas the nMOS corner, which governs the input pair, appears to have little effect. These differences, 0.03–0.05 mV, are only about one to two standard errors of a single point (±5 %, about ±0.03 mV), so the ordering is suggestive rather than established. It would be consistent with the pMOS threshold voltage setting the duration of the integration phase, which ends when the output nodes have discharged by approximately |V<sub>THp</sub>| and the cross-coupled pMOS begin to regenerate: a lower |V<sub>THp</sub>|, at a fast-pMOS corner or at high temperature, shortens the integration and reduces its gain. The noise also increases with the supply (0.56 to 0.64 mV from 1.62 to 1.98 V), consistent with the larger overdrive of the input pair at the higher common-mode voltage V<sub>DD</sub>/2.
2. **The offset is set by random mismatch and depends little on the process corner.** The mean σ<sub>os</sub> lies between 4.55 and 4.68 mV at the five corners, as Pelgrom's law predicts for devices of fixed area. It increases with temperature (4.14 to 5.25 mV from −40 to 125 °C), consistent with the lower integration gain, which refers a larger part of the latch mismatch to the input. The systematic offset caused by the single asymmetric route of the cross-coupling remains below 240 µV in all 45 conditions, at most 6 % of σ<sub>os</sub>; it is largest at high supply and at the fast-pMOS corners.
3. **The energy follows C·V<sub>DD</sub><sup>2</sup> except where leakage takes over.** At 27 °C and 1.8 V, every corner requires 199–214 fJ per decision. Averaged over corners and temperatures, the energy rises from 182 fJ at 1.62 V to 308 fJ at 1.98 V (Table IX), a factor of 1.69 against the 1.49 of the dynamic energy alone. The excess comes from the hot, fast-nMOS conditions: at 125 °C the energy rises moderately at tt, ss and sf (at most 240 fJ at 1.8 V) but steeply at the two corners with fast nMOS, 366 fJ at ff and 586 fJ at fs (822 fJ at 1.98 V). This is the signature of subthreshold leakage, which increases exponentially with temperature and is largest for low-threshold nMOS.

*SRAM-PUF cell* (Fig. 34(c), Table X, Table XI). In observations 4–6, a and s<sub>25</sub> are those of the linear law s(T) = s<sub>25</sub>(1 + a·|T − 25 °C|) fitted to each corner's error rates at −40, 25 and 85 °C (the BER-matched fit of Section VII-C, applied to this 512-cell run). The column s(25 °C) of Table X is a different quantity: the ratio that reproduces the 25 °C error rate alone, which the key calculation uses. The two agree where the linear law fits well and differ where it does not (fs: fitted s<sub>25</sub> = 0.019 against 0.017 in Table X; sf: 0.075 against 0.073). Likewise, the fitted a = 0.030 at tt comes from this smaller run (512 cells × 5 power-ups) and therefore differs from the 0.0205 of the 1,024-cell × 8-power-up post-layout run of Section VII-D; likewise, its 85 °C error rate at tt (2.70 %) is lower than the 3.14 % of the post-layout run, two runs of the same cell, which Section VII-E uses for sizing the code.

4. **The ss corner is almost insensitive to temperature, and tt degrades moderately.** At ss, the bit-error rate stays between 1.95 and 2.50 % from −40 to 85 °C, and the fitted temperature coefficient is a = 0.004, against 0.030 at tt, where the error rate rises from 0.98 % at 25 °C to 2.70 % at 85 °C (Table X).
5. **The fast-nMOS corners degrade sharply above room temperature, through reproducible flips rather than noise.** At ff and fs, the error rate reaches 10.0 and 27.8 % at 85 °C (a = 0.019 and 0.045). Table XI shows that most of these errors are not noise: at fs, 25.6 % of the cells settle in every power-up at 85 °C to the value opposite to their enrolment, whereas only 5.1 % vary between power-ups (ff: 8.4 and 3.9 %). The preferred state of these cells therefore changes with temperature, the second error type that the theory anticipated. This is consistent with a change in the relative weight of the nMOS and pMOS mismatch in the decision: the cell resolves while V<sub>DD</sub> ramps through 0.5–0.9 V, close to the threshold voltages, so a low nMOS threshold, further reduced at high temperature, alters which devices dominate; because the nMOS and pMOS mismatches are independent, the outcome of some cells is reversed.
6. **The ranking at 25 °C does not predict the ranking at temperature.** fs has the lowest error rate of all corners at 25 °C (0.78 %, fitted s<sub>25</sub> = 0.019) and the highest at 85 °C. Conversely, sf has the highest noise-to-mismatch ratio at 25 °C (fitted s<sub>25</sub> = 0.075, with 31 of 512 cells unstable) but a moderate temperature coefficient: its errors are noise and are present already at room temperature. Accordingly, as the theory of masking predicts, discarding the cells that are unstable at 25 °C reduces the error rate of sf at 85 °C from 5.0 to 1.9 %, but leaves that of fs unchanged (27.8 %).

**Interpretation.** For the comparator, PVT changes the numbers but not their scale: across all 45 conditions σ<sub>n</sub> stays between 0.37 and 0.81 mV and σ<sub>os</sub> between 4.01 and 5.85 mV (a spread of 2.2× and 1.5×), both small fractions of V<sub>unit</sub> = 0.45 V, and the energy is at most 822 fJ per decision (8.2 µW at 10 MHz). Whether these ranges matter for the sensor's accuracy, power and the original design's security is evaluated at system level in Section VIII-A to C. For the SRAM-PUF, **PVT changes the nature of the errors**: at the fast-nMOS corners temperature reverses the preference of some cells rather than making them noisier, and masking at 25 °C cannot remove these cells. The two analyses below quantify the comparator's energy terms and derive the error law behind the flips; Section VIII-F evaluates what the corners do to the key, and Section XI designs the code that meets the target at every corner under the per-corner cell models.

#### Comparator energy across PVT: the dynamic and the leakage term

**Goal.** Separate the two physical components of the comparator's energy per decision across the 45 PVT conditions, and identify the conditions at which leakage, rather than switching, sets the energy.

**Theory.** A StrongARM comparator draws no static current. In every cycle it charges its internal nodes in the reset phase and discharges them in the decision, so its energy per decision is

$$E \approx C_{sw}\,V_{DD}^2 + I_{leak}\,V_{DD}\,T_{clk},$$

where $C_{sw}$ is the switched capacitance (set by the devices and the layout), $I_{leak}$ the leakage current and $T_{clk}$ = 100 ns the clock period. The ratio $E/V_{DD}^2$ is the effective switched capacitance. *Prediction:* the dynamic term makes $E/V_{DD}^2$ constant, independent of the supply and nearly independent of the temperature. Leakage grows exponentially with temperature and is largest for low-threshold (fast) nMOS devices; it should therefore appear as a rise of $E/V_{DD}^2$ at 125 °C at the fast-nMOS corners (ff, fs).

**Setup.** Transistor level, recorded: the energy per decision of the extracted comparator, measured from the supply current with the output toggling in every cycle, at the 45 conditions of the grid above (the same recorded run, regenerated by the command in the card above). The metrics are $E$ and $E/V_{DD}^2$, grouped by process corner.

> **Next cell.** 1. Reads the energy per decision at the 45 conditions. 2. Computes the effective switched capacitance $E/V_{DD}^2$ and its range at 27 °C. 3. Finds the condition with the largest $E/V_{DD}^2$. 4. Prints the card and draws Fig. 35.


```python
#@title Fig.: comparator energy across PVT
# The comparator's energy per decision at the 45 PVT conditions (recorded grid), and the effective switched capacitance
# E / VDD^2, which separates the dynamic CV^2 term from leakage
tcol, vmark = {-40.0: COL["ok"], 27.0: COL["aqua"], 125.0: COL["bad"]}, {1.62: "v", 1.8: "o", 1.98: "^"}   # PVT marker key
corners = list(PVT["corners"])
E = np.array([r["energy"] for r in PVT["cmp"]]); Vd = np.array([r["vdd"] for r in PVT["cmp"]]); Tm = np.array([r["temp"] for r in PVT["cmp"]])
Ceff = E / Vd ** 2
c27 = Ceff[Tm == 27.0]
CMP_E = dict(e_rng=(E.min(), E.max()), p_max=E.max() * 10e6, c_sw=(c27.min(), c27.max()))
hot = max(PVT["cmp"], key=lambda r: r["energy"] / r["vdd"] ** 2)
card("Comparator energy across PVT: dynamic and leakage terms",
     [("energy per decision, 45 PVT conditions", f"{1e15 * E.min():.0f}–{1e15 * E.max():.0f} fJ"),
      ("theory: switched capacitance E/V<sub>DD</sub><sup>2</sup> at 27 °C", f"{1e15 * c27.min():.0f}–{1e15 * c27.max():.0f} fF over all corners and "
       f"supplies: nearly constant, as for a purely dynamic CV<sup>2</sup> energy"),
      ("leakage", f"E/V<sub>DD</sub><sup>2</sup> rises to {1e15 * hot['energy'] / hot['vdd'] ** 2:.0f} fF at {hot['corner']}, "
       f"{hot['temp']:.0f} °C, {hot['vdd']:.2f} V: the I<sub>leak</sub>V<sub>DD</sub>T<sub>clk</sub> term of the fast-nMOS corners")], tone="ok")
# the effective switched capacitance only: the energy itself is E = (E / VDD^2) x VDD^2, and its range is in the card
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(W1, 2.6))
for r, yy in zip(PVT["cmp"], 1e15 * Ceff):
    x = corners.index(r["corner"]) + 0.26 * (list(tcol).index(r["temp"]) - 1) + 0.07 * (list(vmark).index(r["vdd"]) - 1)
    ax.plot(x, yy, vmark[r["vdd"]], color=tcol[r["temp"]], ms=5, mec=COL["ink"], mew=0.4)
ax.axhspan(1e15 * c27.min(), 1e15 * c27.max(), color=COL["faint"], alpha=0.25, lw=0)
ax.annotate(f"27 °C: {1e15 * c27.min():.0f}–{1e15 * c27.max():.0f} fF (dynamic $CV^2$)", (1.55, 1e15 * c27.max()), xytext=(0, 3),
            textcoords="offset points", ha="left", va="bottom", fontsize=7.5, color=COL["ink"])   # between the ss and ff groups
xh = corners.index(hot["corner"]) + 0.26 + 0.07
ax.annotate(f"leakage: {1e15 * hot['energy'] / hot['vdd'] ** 2:.0f} fF\n({hot['corner']}, {hot['temp']:.0f} °C, {hot['vdd']:.2f} V)",
            (xh, 1e15 * hot["energy"] / hot["vdd"] ** 2), xytext=(-12, -4), textcoords="offset points", ha="right", va="top",
            fontsize=7.5, color=COL["ink"], arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=COL["faint"], lw=0.6))
ax.set_xticks(range(len(corners)), corners); ax.set_ylabel(r"$E/V_\mathrm{DD}^2$ (fF)"); ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
ax.set_xlim(-0.6, len(corners) - 0.4)
h = [plt.Line2D([], [], ls="", marker="s", color=c, label=f"{t:+.0f} °C".replace("-", "−")) for t, c in tcol.items()]
h += [plt.Line2D([], [], ls="", marker=m, color=COL["faint"], label=f"{v:.2f} V") for v, m in vmark.items()]
ax.legend(handles=h, ncol=2, fontsize=7, loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0, 0.93))
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()

<p align="center" style="text-align:center"><b>Fig. 35.</b> Comparator energy across PVT (extracted comparator, recorded grid). Effective switched capacitance E/V<sub>DD</sub><sup>2</sup> at the 45 conditions, grouped by process corner; marker shape: supply; colour: temperature; grey band: range at 27 °C; the largest value is labelled.</p>

**Result.** The energy per decision is 144–822 fJ over the 45 conditions (card). At 27 °C, $E/V_{DD}^2$ is 59–70 fF over all corners and supplies, nearly constant, as the dynamic $CV^2$ term predicts (Fig. 35). The largest value, 210 fF, occurs at fs, 125 °C and 1.98 V, three times the 27 °C value: the leakage term of a fast-nMOS corner, as predicted.

**Interpretation.** Below 125 °C the comparator's energy is switching energy and scales with $V_{DD}^2$; at 125 °C and fast nMOS, leakage over the 100 ns clock period adds up to two thirds of the energy. **The block-level energy is therefore bounded by 822 fJ per decision at every one of the 45 simulated conditions**; Section VIII-C converts it into the comparator's share of the sensor's power.

#### The SRAM-PUF error law across corners: noise and mismatch rotation

**Goal.** Explain the SRAM-PUF errors of Table X and Table XI with a closed-form law that separates the two error types, noise and reproducible flips, and test it against the recorded transistor-level Monte Carlo of all five corners.

**Theory.**

1. *The power-up decision.* Cell $i$ settles to $b_i = [\,m_i + \sigma_n\,n > 0\,]$, where $m_i \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma_m^2)$ is its mismatch, fixed at fabrication, $\mu$ the bias of the mismatch, $\sigma_m$ its spread, and $n \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)$ the noise, drawn anew at every power-up with rms $\sigma_n$. Only the noise-to-mismatch ratio $s = \sigma_n/\sigma_m$ and the bias matter.
2. *The error rate in closed form.* A read disagrees with the enrolment when the decision variables at enrolment and at temperature $T$ have different signs. For two jointly Gaussian variables with correlation $\rho$, this happens with probability $\arccos(\rho)/\pi$ (Sheppard's formula). The read differs from the enrolment in two ways. The first is noise: $s_e$ at enrolment, $s_T$ at temperature $T$. The second is a **rotation** $\theta(T)$ of the mismatch itself: the relative weight of the nMOS and the pMOS mismatch changes with temperature, so that the mismatch at $T$ is $m' = m\cos\theta + m_\perp\sin\theta$, with $m_\perp$ an independent mismatch component of the same spread. With $\mu = 0$, the bit-error rate (BER) is
   $$\mathrm{BER}(T) = \frac{1}{\pi}\arccos\frac{\cos\theta(T)}{\sqrt{(1+s_e^2)(1+s_T^2)}} \;\approx\; \frac{1}{\pi}\sqrt{s_e^2 + s_T^2 + \theta^2}.$$
   Noise and reproducible flips add in quadrature. Two power-ups at the same temperature disagree with probability $\arccos\!\big(1/(1+s_T^2)\big)/\pi$, so the Monte Carlo gives $s_T$ directly, and $\theta$ then follows from the BER. θ is therefore not fitted and not an independent prediction: it is a reparametrisation of the BER in excess of the noise-only value. What can be tested is its physical reading: a rotation θ reverses the preferred value of a fraction θ/π of the cells, so θ/π should match the cells that the recorded bits show to be wrong in every hot power-up. *Prediction:* at the corners with a large excess, θ/π approaches the counted reproducible flips from above (the count misses the sign-changed cells that are also unstable).

**Setup.** Transistor level, recorded: the Monte Carlo of the extracted 6T cell of the grid above, 512 cells × 5 power-ups at −40, 25 and 85 °C, at each of the five process corners, at the nominal supply. The enrolment is the first power-up at 25 °C; the BER at each temperature counts the other power-ups' disagreements with it. $s_T$ follows from the mean disagreement between pairs of power-ups at the same temperature, through the relation of item 2; the noise-only BER ($\theta = 0$) uses $s_e = s_{25}$ and $s_T$, and $\theta(T)$ is the rotation that makes the closed form equal the simulated BER. The independent check counts the reproducible flips at 85 °C: cells with the same value in all five hot power-ups, opposite to the enrolment. The metrics are the BER, $\theta$, and θ/π against the counted flips.

> **Next cell.** 1. For each corner and temperature, measures the BER against the 25 °C enrolment and $s_T$ from repeated power-ups. 2. Computes the noise-only BER. 3. Extracts the rotation $\theta(T)$ from the excess BER. 4. Counts the reproducible flips at 85 °C and compares them with θ/π. 5. Prints the card and draws Fig. 36.


```python
#@title Fig.: SRAM-PUF error law across corners
# The SRAM-PUF error law against the transistor-level Monte Carlo of the five corners. BER vs a 25 °C
# enrolment (first power-up), s_T from the disagreement between repeated power-ups at T, the noise-only prediction
# arccos(1/sqrt((1+s_e^2)(1+s_T^2)))/pi, and the mismatch rotation theta(T) that explains the rest
i25 = TEMPS.index(25)
TH = {}
for j, c in enumerate(PVT["puf"]["corners"]):
    b = BITS[j].astype(np.int8); w0 = b[i25, 0]; R = b.shape[1]
    rows = []
    for i, T in enumerate(TEMPS):
        reads = b[i, 1:] if T == 25 else b[i]
        ber = float((reads != w0).mean())
        q = float(np.mean([(b[i, a] != b[i, a2]).mean() for a in range(R) for a2 in range(a + 1, R)]))   # same-T disagreement
        rows.append(dict(T=T, ber=ber, sT=float(np.sqrt(max(1 / np.cos(np.pi * q) - 1, 0)))))
    se = rows[i25]["sT"]
    for r in rows:
        r["noise_only"] = float(np.arccos(1 / np.sqrt((1 + se ** 2) * (1 + r["sT"] ** 2))) / np.pi)
        r["theta"] = float(np.degrees(np.arccos(min(1.0, np.cos(np.pi * r["ber"]) * np.sqrt((1 + se ** 2) * (1 + r["sT"] ** 2))))))
    st85 = b[TEMPS.index(85)].min(axis=0) == b[TEMPS.index(85)].max(axis=0)                      # stable in every hot power-up
    TH[c["corner"]] = dict(rows=rows, flips85=float((st85 & (b[TEMPS.index(85), 0] != w0)).mean()))   # counted reproducible flips
FL = {k: (v["rows"][TEMPS.index(85)]["theta"] / 180, v["flips85"]) for k, v in TH.items()}   # theta/pi and the counted flips, 85 °C
TH = {k: v["rows"] for k, v in TH.items()}
worst = max(((k, r) for k, v in TH.items() for r in v if r["T"] == 85), key=lambda kr: kr[1]["theta"])
card("SRAM-PUF error law against the transistor-level Monte Carlo of the five corners",
     [("noise s<sub>T</sub> from repeated power-ups, " + ", ".join(f"{T} °C" for T in TEMPS).replace("-", "−"),
       ", ".join(f"{k} " + "/".join(f"{r['sT']:.3f}" for r in v) for k, v in TH.items())),
      ("BER at 85 °C: measured | noise-only theory", ", ".join(f"{k} {100 * v[TEMPS.index(85)]['ber']:.1f} | {100 * v[TEMPS.index(85)]['noise_only']:.1f} %"
                                                       for k, v in TH.items())),
      ("rotation θ at 85 °C (the excess over noise, reparametrised)", ", ".join(f"{k} {v[TEMPS.index(85)]['theta']:.0f}°" for k, v in TH.items())),
      ("θ/π against the counted reproducible flips at 85 °C (independent count)", ", ".join(f"{k} {100 * a_:.1f} | {100 * f_:.1f} %" for k, (a_, f_) in FL.items())
       + f": largest at {worst[0]}, θ = <b>{worst[1]['theta']:.0f}°</b>")], tone="ok")
pcol = {"tt": COL["ink"], "ss": COL["ok"], "ff": COL["bad"], "sf": COL["aqua"], "fs": COL["yellow"]}
pmk = {"tt": "o", "ss": "s", "ff": "^", "sf": "D", "fs": "v"}          # marker shape by corner as well (ff and fs differ in shape)
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(W2, 2.9))
ax = axs[0]                                               # theta/pi from the BER against the counted flips (85 °C)
mx = 100 * max(max(v) for v in FL.values()) * 1.15
ax.plot([0, mx], [0, mx], ":", color=COL["faint"], lw=1)
for k, (a_, f_) in FL.items():
    ax.plot(100 * f_, 100 * a_, pmk[k], color=pcol[k], ms=6, mec=COL["ink"], mew=0.4, label=k)
ax.set_xlim(0, mx); ax.set_ylim(0, mx); ax.set_xlabel("Counted reproducible flips (%)"); ax.set_ylabel(r"$\theta/\pi$ from the BER (%)")
ax.legend(fontsize=7, ncol=2, loc="upper left"); panel(ax, "a", r"85 °C: $\theta/\pi$ vs flip count")
ax = axs[1]                                               # 85 °C: measured against noise only, per corner
i85 = TEMPS.index(85); xb = np.arange(len(TH))
meas = [100 * v[i85]["ber"] for v in TH.values()]; noise = [100 * v[i85]["noise_only"] for v in TH.values()]
ax.bar(xb - 0.19, meas, 0.36, color=[pcol[k] for k in TH], ec=COL["ink"], lw=0.5)
ax.bar(xb + 0.19, noise, 0.36, color="white", ec=COL["ink"], lw=0.5, hatch="////")
for x, y in zip(xb - 0.19, meas):
    ax.annotate(f"{y:.1f}", (x, y), xytext=(0, 2), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7.5)
ax.set_xticks(xb, list(TH)); ax.set_ylabel("BER at 85 °C vs 25 °C enrolment (%)"); ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
ax.set_ylim(0, 1.32 * max(meas))
ax.legend(handles=[Patch(fc=COL["faint"], ec=COL["ink"], lw=0.5, label="measured (corner colour)"),
                   Patch(fc="white", ec=COL["ink"], lw=0.5, hatch="////", label=r"noise only ($\theta = 0$)")], fontsize=7, loc="upper left")
panel(ax, "b", "85 °C: noise vs flips")
ax = axs[2]
for k, v in TH.items():
    ax.plot(TEMPS, [r["theta"] for r in v], "-", marker=pmk[k], color=pcol[k], ms=4, mec=COL["ink"], mew=0.3, lw=1.4, label=k)
ax.set_xticks(TEMPS); ax.set_xlabel("Temperature (°C)"); ax.set_ylabel(r"Mismatch rotation $\theta$ (°)")
ax.legend(fontsize=7, ncol=2, loc="upper left"); panel(ax, "c", r"the rotation $\theta(T)$")
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

<p align="center" style="text-align:center"><b>Fig. 36.</b> SRAM-PUF error law across process corners (extracted cell, recorded Monte Carlo, 512 cells × 5 power-ups per condition). (a) Fraction θ/π of cells reversed by the rotation at 85 °C against the counted reproducible flips; dotted: equality. (b) BER at 85 °C against a 25 °C enrolment, counted in the Monte Carlo (solid) and noise only (hatched). (c) Mismatch rotation θ against temperature.</p>

**Result.**

* *Noise.* The repeated power-ups give $s_T$ between 0.009 (fs, −40 °C) and 0.064 (sf, 25 °C); at tt, 0.026, 0.020 and 0.023 at −40, 25 and 85 °C.
* *At 85 °C.* The simulated BER of the PVT grid exceeds the noise-only value at every corner, most at the fast-nMOS corners: 10.0 against 2.1 % at ff and 27.8 against 1.8 % at fs (tt 2.7 against 1.0 %, ss 2.0 against 1.4 %, sf 5.0 against 2.7 %; Fig. 36(b)).
* *The rotation.* The excess corresponds to a rotation of the mismatch of up to θ = 50° at fs and 85 °C (Fig. 36(c)); ff follows with 18°, the other corners stay below 10°.
* *The independent check.* θ/π and the counted reproducible flips at 85 °C are 27.8 and 25.6 % at fs, 9.8 and 8.4 % at ff, 4.2 and 2.5 % at sf, 2.5 and 2.0 % at tt and 1.4 and 1.0 % at ss (Fig. 36(a)). At every corner θ/π lies above the count, by 0.4 to 2.2 percentage points, as predicted.

**Interpretation.** The closed form does not predict the BER; it splits it, without a fitted parameter, into noise measured from repeated power-ups and a rotation θ, and the flip count confirms that θ describes a fixed set of cells that reverse their preferred value, not extra noise. **At the fast-nMOS corners the mismatch itself rotates with temperature, and the cells reverse their preferred state**. Noise-based reasoning at 25 °C cannot reveal it: fs, the corner with the most flips at 85 °C, has the lowest noise of all corners at 25 °C. Section VIII-F builds the key-failure model on these two components.

#### The fast-nMOS flips: mechanism check and supply ramp

**Goal.** Test the physical reading of the rotation θ of Fig. 36 at the two corners where it is largest, ff and fs, against a competing explanation, and check whether the error rates of this section depend on the one supply ramp (1 µs) that every recorded run uses.

**Theory.**

1. *Two candidate mechanisms.* The error law reads the excess BER at 85 °C as a rotation of the mismatch: the relative weight of the nMOS and the pMOS mismatch changes with temperature, so that some cells change their preferred value. Every recorded run, however, powers the cell up with both bit lines tied to the ramping supply and the word line at 0 V. The pass gates are then off but leak, and their subthreshold leakage, which grows steeply with temperature and is largest at the fast-nMOS corners, injects a current into the storage nodes that carries the pass gates' own mismatch. This would also make the preferred value depend on temperature, but it is a property of the testbench, not of the cell in the array, whose bit lines are precharged or floating at power-up.
2. *Discriminating test.* If the flips come from the latch (rotation), they do not change when the bit lines float or are grounded, nor when the mismatch of the two pass gates is switched off. If they come from pass-gate leakage, they fall when the bit lines float or are grounded (no leakage path from the supply) and when the pass gates have no mismatch (equal leakage on both sides). *Prediction (rotation):* the BER and the reproducible flips at 85 °C agree between the four testbenches within the counting scatter.
3. *Direct measurement of the rotation.* A voltage source in series with the gate of one inverter, bisected without noise to the value at which the cell's decision changes, gives each cell's input-referred mismatch ΔV<sub>m</sub>. The correlation ρ of ΔV<sub>m</sub> between 25 and 85 °C gives the rotation directly, θ = arccos ρ, independently of the BER from which Fig. 36 derives it. *Prediction:* the two values of θ agree.
4. *Supply ramp.* The cell resolves at a supply voltage, not at a time, so a slower ramp should not change the decision much; a faster ramp than the cell's own time constant can move the resolve voltage up and change the outcome of marginal cells. *Prediction:* from 1 to 100 µs, the BER against the 1 µs enrolment stays near the 25 °C repeatability; at 0.1 µs it may rise.

**Setup.** Transistor level, recorded: the extracted 6T cell of Section VII-D, 128 cells with the same mismatch draws and noise sequences as the first 128 cells of the PVT grid, so that the testbench with tied bit lines reproduces the recorded grid. *Mechanism:* corners ff and fs, 25 and 85 °C, five noisy power-ups, one noiseless power-up and the bisection of ΔV<sub>m</sub> (nine steps over ±0.2 V) per temperature, for four testbenches: bit lines tied to V<sub>DD</sub> (as recorded), floating (20 fF to ground each), grounded, and tied with the pass-gate mismatch switched off (the latch transistors keep their mismatch). *Ramp:* typical corner, 25 °C, bit lines tied, ramps of 0.1, 1, 10 and 100 µs, five noisy power-ups each. The metrics are the BER at 85 °C against the 25 °C enrolment, the reproducible flips, θ from ΔV<sub>m</sub> and from the BER, and the BER of each ramp against the 1 µs enrolment and against its own first power-up. The run takes about an hour on two cores and is not repeated by the notebook; the cell reads its compact summary.

MECH, MECH_RAMP = MECH_REC["mech"], MECH_REC["ramp"]

def _puf_mechanism():                                     # local names only: later cells keep theirs (cs, t, rows, ...)
    TB = {"tied": "bit lines tied to V<sub>DD</sub>", "float": "bit lines floating", "gnd": "bit lines grounded",
          "pg_mm0": "no pass-gate mismatch"}
    rows = []
    for co, cv in MECH.items():
        t = cv["tied"]
        rows.append((f"{co}, 85 °C: BER | reproducible flips, per testbench",
                     "; ".join(f"{k} {100 * s['rows']['85']['ber']:.1f} | {100 * s['rows']['85']['flip']:.1f} %" for k, s in cv.items())))
        rows.append((f"{co}: rotation θ at 85 °C, from the bisected mismatch | from the BER",
                     "; ".join(f"{k} {s['theta_direct_deg']:.0f}° | {s['theta_ber_deg']:.0f}°" for k, s in cv.items())))
        rows.append((f"{co}: σ<sub>m</sub> at 25 | 85 °C (tied)", f"{t['rows']['25']['sigma_m_mV']:.1f} | {t['rows']['85']['sigma_m_mV']:.1f} mV; "
                     f"resolve voltage (median) {t['rows']['25']['vres_median']:.2f} | {t['rows']['85']['vres_median']:.2f} V; "
                     f"reproduces the recorded PVT run on {100 * t['repro_pvt']:.1f} % of its bits"))
    rk = sorted(MECH_RAMP, key=float)
    rows.append(("tt, 25 °C: BER against the 1 µs enrolment, per ramp time",
                 ", ".join(f"{float(k) * 1e6:g} µs {100 * MECH_RAMP[k]['rows']['25']['ber_vs_1us']:.1f} %" for k in rk)))
    rows.append(("tt, 25 °C: BER against the ramp's own first power-up",
                 ", ".join(f"{float(k) * 1e6:g} µs {100 * MECH_RAMP[k]['rows']['25']['ber_own']:.1f} %" for k in rk)))
    rows.append(("tt, 25 °C: resolve voltage (median)", ", ".join(f"{float(k) * 1e6:g} µs {MECH_RAMP[k]['rows']['25']['vres_median']:.2f} V" for k in rk)))
    rows.append(("recorded run", f"{MECH_REC['cells']} cells × {MECH_REC['repeats']} power-ups per condition, ngspice {MECH_REC['ngspice']}, "
                 f"{MECH_REC['cpu_s'] / 120:.0f} min on two cores: <code>python dev/spice_puf/demo_mechanism.py --pdk-root $PDK_ROOT</code>"))
    card("SRAM-PUF at the fast-nMOS corners: testbench variants and supply ramp (recorded)", rows, tone="info")

    tcol = {"tied": COL["ink"], "float": COL["ok"], "gnd": COL["aqua"], "pg_mm0": COL["bad"]}
    fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(W2, 2.9))
    ax = axs[0]                                               # BER at 85 °C per corner and testbench: flips solid, rest hatched
    cos = list(MECH); tbs = [k for k in TB if k in MECH[cos[0]]]
    wd = 0.8 / len(tbs)
    for j, k in enumerate(tbs):
        x = np.arange(len(cos)) + (j - (len(tbs) - 1) / 2) * wd
        f = [100 * MECH[c][k]["rows"]["85"]["flip"] for c in cos]
        b = [100 * MECH[c][k]["rows"]["85"]["ber"] for c in cos]
        ax.bar(x, f, wd, color=tcol[k], label=TB[k].replace("V<sub>DD</sub>", r"$V_\mathrm{DD}$"), edgecolor=COL["ink"], lw=0.4)
        ax.bar(x, np.subtract(b, f), wd, bottom=f, color="none", edgecolor=tcol[k], hatch="////", lw=0.4)
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(cos))); ax.set_xticklabels(cos); ax.set_ylabel("BER at 85 °C (%)")
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.6 * max(100 * MECH[c][k]["rows"]["85"]["ber"] for c in cos for k in tbs))
    ax.legend(fontsize=6.5, loc="upper right", ncol=1); panel(ax, "a", "85 °C: BER by testbench")
    ax = axs[1]                                               # bisected mismatch at 25 vs 85 °C, the worst corner, tied
    cw = max(cos, key=lambda c: MECH[c]["tied"]["rows"]["85"]["ber"])
    d = np.array(MECH_REC["dvm"][cw])
    lim = 1.05 * np.nanmax(np.abs(d))
    ax.axhline(0, color=COL["faint"], lw=0.8); ax.axvline(0, color=COL["faint"], lw=0.8)
    sg = np.sign(d[0]) != np.sign(d[1])
    ax.plot(d[0][~sg], d[1][~sg], "o", ms=3, color=COL["ok"], alpha=0.7, label="same sign")
    ax.plot(d[0][sg], d[1][sg], "o", ms=3.5, color=COL["bad"], label="sign reversed")
    ax.set_xlim(-lim, lim); ax.set_ylim(-lim, lim)
    ax.set_xlabel(r"$\Delta V_\mathrm{m}$ at 25 °C (mV)")
    ax.set_ylabel(r"$\Delta V_\mathrm{m}$ at 85 °C (mV)"); ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper left")
    panel(ax, "b", f"{cw}, mismatch per cell")
    ax = axs[2]                                               # ramp time: BER vs the 1 us enrolment and vs own enrolment
    tr = np.array([float(k) for k in rk]) * 1e6
    ax.plot(tr, [100 * MECH_RAMP[k]["rows"]["25"]["ber_vs_1us"] for k in rk], "o-", color=COL["bad"], label="vs 1 µs enrolment")
    ax.plot(tr, [100 * MECH_RAMP[k]["rows"]["25"]["ber_own"] for k in rk], "s--", color=COL["ok"], label="vs own first power-up")
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xlabel("Supply ramp time (µs)"); ax.set_ylabel("BER at 25 °C (%)")
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.45 * max(100 * MECH_RAMP[k]["rows"]["25"][q] for k in rk for q in ("ber_vs_1us", "ber_own")))
    ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper left"); panel(ax, "c", "tt, 25 °C: ramp time")
    fig.tight_layout(); show()

_puf_mechanism()
