<p align="center" style="text-align:center"><b>Fig. 37.</b> SRAM-PUF flip mechanism and supply ramp (extracted cell, recorded, 128 cells × 5 power-ups per condition). (a) BER at 85 °C (25 °C enrolment) for four testbenches; solid: reproducible flips; hatched: other errors. (b) Mismatch voltage ΔV<sub>m</sub> per cell, 25 °C against 85 °C (fs, bit lines tied); orange: sign reversed. (c) BER at tt, 25 °C, against ramp time.</p>

**Result (mechanism).** The testbench with tied bit lines reproduces the corresponding cells of the recorded PVT grid bit for bit (100.0 % at ff and fs). At 85 °C, **the four testbenches give the same error rates within one cell in 128** (Fig. 37(a)): at fs, 32.5 % BER and 28.9 % reproducible flips over the 128 cells of this testbench (the PVT grid of Section VII-F gives the population values), with the bit lines tied, floating or grounded, and with the pass-gate mismatch switched off; at ff, 14.1–14.4 % BER and 11.7 % reproducible flips in all four. Switching off the pass-gate mismatch leaves every bit unchanged at both corners. The bisected mismatch voltage gives the rotation directly (Fig. 37(b)): at fs, ΔV<sub>m</sub> at 25 and 85 °C correlate with ρ = 0.61, θ = 53°, against 58° from the BER; at ff, ρ = 0.94, θ = 20°, against 25°. At fs, 32.8 % of the cells reverse the sign of ΔV<sub>m</sub> between 25 and 85 °C, the same fraction as the BER. The spread σ<sub>m</sub> of ΔV<sub>m</sub> falls from 48 mV at 25 °C to 29 mV (fs) and 33 mV (ff) at 85 °C.

**Result (supply ramp).** At the typical corner and 25 °C, the slower the ramp, the lower the supply voltage at which the cells resolve (median 1.08, 0.83, 0.58 and 0.38 V for 0.1, 1, 10 and 100 µs) and the more repeatable the power-up: the BER against the ramp's own first power-up falls from 2.1 % (0.1 µs) to 1.2 % (1 µs) and 0.4 % (10 and 100 µs) (Fig. 37(c)). Against the 1 µs enrolment, however, every other ramp gives about 4 % (4.1 % at 0.1 µs, 4.4 % at 10 and 100 µs), because 5 of the 128 cells settle to the other value even without noise (3.9 %, 95 % interval 1.3–8.9 %). The cells that change are not the same at 0.1 µs as at 10 and 100 µs, and the 10 and 100 µs runs, which use different time-step limits, agree bit for bit.

**Interpretation.** The competing explanation is rejected: neither the bit-line condition nor the pass-gate mismatch changes the flips, so they are not an artefact of the testbench but a property of the latch, as the error law assumed. The direct SPICE extraction of ΔV<sub>m</sub> agrees with the rotation within 5° at both corners, so θ is not only a reparametrisation of the excess BER: in simulation, the mismatch of each cell changes direction with temperature, strongly at fs, where the pMOS and nMOS mismatch weights change most. The ramp study adds a requirement that the earlier sections did not state: **the key generator must reconstruct with the supply ramp it was enrolled with**. A ramp ten times slower or faster than the enrolment changes about 4 % of the cells, more than the 1.2 % of repeated power-ups at the same ramp and more than the 3.14 % at 85 °C of the extracted cell (Section VII-D), which the code would then have to absorb as well. A slow, controlled ramp is favourable, since it makes the power-up more repeatable. These are 128 cells of one simulated chip at one corner for the ramp; the run supports the mechanism and shows the size of the ramp effect, but does not size the code for an uncontrolled ramp.

### Summary of Section VII

The SKY130 simulations replace the assumed comparator and SRAM-cell parameters of the model with simulated ones (the integrator noise is derived from the measurement of [1]):

1. **Comparator noise.** σ<sub>n</sub> = 0.560 mV (schematic) and 0.575 mV (post-layout), within the predicted range of a kT/C-limited StrongARM latch; `comp_noise` = 1.279 × 10⁻³ (Sections VII-B, D).
2. **Comparator offset.** σ<sub>os</sub> = 4.34 mV (schematic) and 4.37 mV (post-layout), consistent with Pelgrom's law for the 4/0.5 µm input pair; the layout adds a systematic +0.095 mV (Sections VII-B, D).
3. **Comparator operation and energy.** Six noiseless transient decisions, down to ±0.2 mV, are all correct; the energy is 186 fJ (schematic) and 199 fJ per decision (post-layout), the increase being caused by the extracted clock wiring (Sections VII-B, D).
4. **SRAM-PUF cell.** Post-layout s<sub>25</sub> = 0.0225, a = 0.0205 per °C, P(1) = 0.493: a noise-to-mismatch ratio 2.7 times smaller than assumed, but with errors that rise on both sides of 25 °C because cells change their preference with temperature. The error rates are 1.37, 0.99 and 3.14 % at −40, 25 and 85 °C; the symmetric linear law cannot follow both −40 and 85 °C and underestimates the 85 °C rate (1.75 %) (Sections VII-C, D).
5. **Layout.** Both cells are DRC- and LVS-clean and symmetric; the extraction changes no quantity beyond its statistical error except the clock energy and a 0.1 mV systematic offset; in particular, the 85 °C error rates of the two SRAM runs differ by less than their sampling error. `PEX_LIVE = True` re-runs the post-layout checks live and compares the SRAM run bit for bit with the record on its first 128 cells (not part of the published run).
6. **Code.** Sized over 1,000 Monte Carlo chips (a flip-aware cell model fitted to the post-layout SPICE Monte Carlo), a key-failure probability below 10⁻⁶ from 0 to 85 °C needs t = 39 at the 99th percentile (33–46 across the 95 % interval of the 85 °C error rate); the bounded entropy budget (95 % lower bound on the min-entropy, 192 bits for a 128-bit key with the hash margin) allows at most t = 35: with 600 cells and a 25 °C enrolment, the two limits cannot both be met. The simulations keep t = 45, which leaves 94–137 secret bits (lower bound to point estimate), a working setting for the system simulations; the two-temperature enrolment of Section VIII-F is the key generator that meets both limits (the earlier noise-only sizing of one simulated chip needed t = 48, the schematic values t = 41, the law alone t = 32). With the conservative s<sub>25</sub> = 0.06, t = 60 would be needed, leaving no secret bits. The target is met by the two-temperature enrolment of Section VIII-F and the compiled codes of Section XI (Section VII-E).
7. **PVT.** Over 45 conditions the comparator spans σ<sub>n</sub> 0.37–0.81 mV, σ<sub>os</sub> 4.01–5.85 mV and 144–822 fJ per decision, its energy dynamic except at 125 °C at the fast-nMOS corners, where leakage triples E/V<sub>DD</sub><sup>2</sup>; the SRAM-PUF error rate at 85 °C reaches 27.8 % at fs, mainly through reproducible flips, which the error law explains as a rotation of the mismatch of up to 50° (Section VII-F) A recorded simulation with floating or grounded bit lines and without pass-gate mismatch leaves these flips unchanged and gives the rotation directly (53° at fs), so in simulation they are a property of the latch, not of the testbench; a supply-ramp sweep (0.1–100 µs) changes about 4 % of the cells against the 1 µs enrolment, so the key must be reconstructed with the enrolment ramp (Section VII-F).

**Handed to Section VIII.** The model now runs on the following settings (Table VIII) and ranges:

# **VIII. From transistor to system: accuracy, power and security**
---
**The question.** Section VII characterises two circuits at transistor level: the StrongARM comparator of the modulator and the 6T SRAM-PUF cell, each across process, supply voltage and temperature (PVT). This section asks what those circuit values do to the system: the accuracy of the sensor's reading, its power and, above all, its **security**, both for the original design of [1] and for the proposal.

**Why it matters.** A circuit value alone, such as a comparator's noise in millivolts or a cell's error rate in per cent, does not say whether the sensor is accurate or secure. The system-level claims of the abstract rest on this section: in the behavioural model with the simulated comparator values, the sensor keeps its SNDR across the 45 PVT conditions with a wide margin in comparator noise and needs only a moderate OTA gain; in the model, with its simplified dither, neither the comparator nor the integrators' mismatch protects the original design against an attacker who owns a second chip, so its security must come from a key; at the fast-nMOS corners SRAM cells reverse their preferred state with temperature, so the key generator must be sized and enrolled for its worst corner; and each of these effects is predicted by a first-order theory before it is simulated.

**What it takes from earlier sections.** The bit-exact model of the link and its attack tools (Section V), consistent with the measurements of [1] (Section VI); the simulated circuit values and the BCH code sized from them (Section VII-E); and the recorded PVT grids of both extracted cells (Section VII-F).

**Roadmap.**

* *Circuit-to-system paths and PVT coverage:* which circuit quantity reaches which system metric, and which PVT conditions each study covers.
* *Simulation setup:* the abstraction level, the common settings, the replica attack, and the testbench cell shared by all studies.
* *The complete sensor, end to end:* one frame of the complete proposed design through every block, at the nominal condition and at the comparator's noisiest PVT condition, with its spectra and a third frame with assumed circuit impairments (clock jitter, 1/f noise, distortion); the reference for the studies.
* **A. Accuracy:** the comparator's noise and offset against the SNDR and the DC error of the reading.
* **B. Security of the original design:** the replica attack against the comparator's offset alone (part 1), then against its noise and offset at the 45 PVT conditions and far beyond them (part 2).
* **C. Power:** the comparator's share of the sensor's power across PVT.
* **D. The modulator's own non-idealities:** the integrator's thermal noise and the OTA's DC gain, for accuracy and for security.
* **E. Security of the original design:** the chip-to-chip mismatch of the integrator capacitors.
* **F. Security of the proposal:** the key that the SRAM-PUF cells give at every process corner and temperature, for two enrolment strategies, with the cell error law of Section VII-F.
* **G. The circuit-to-system map:** the results of studies A to F in one table, followed by the summary of the section.

Each study follows the same steps: Goal, Theory (with the prediction to be tested), Setup, the Next cell note and the code, the figure and its caption, Result and Interpretation.

### Circuit-to-system paths and PVT coverage

Every circuit quantity reaches the system along one path. The table names, for each quantity, the path, the system metric it sets, the PVT conditions at which it is evaluated, and the study that follows it. The symbols are: σ<sub>n</sub>, the comparator's input-referred noise (rms); σ<sub>os</sub>, the standard deviation of its input-referred offset over Monte Carlo instances; SNDR, the signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio of the decoded reading. "Nominal" means the tt corner, 27 °C (25 °C for the SRAM-PUF) and 1.8 V.

| Circuit quantity (SKY130, Section VII) | Path to the system | System metric | PVT coverage | Study |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Comparator noise σ<sub>n</sub> | noise at the 1-bit quantiser of the second-order modulator | **accuracy:** modulator SNDR | the 45 PVT conditions, plus a sweep at nominal | A |
| Comparator offset σ<sub>os</sub> | a constant at the quantiser input, inside the loop | **accuracy:** DC error of the decoded reading | a sweep at nominal, and 3× the largest PVT σ<sub>os</sub> | A |
| Comparator offset alone | the only difference between a victim chip and an attacker's replica | **security of the original design:** the replica attack | nominal (schematic σ<sub>os</sub>) | B, part 1 |
| Comparator noise and offset | the analog difference between victim and replica | **security of the original design:** the replica attack | the 45 PVT conditions, plus sweeps at nominal | B, part 2 |
| Comparator energy | energy per decision × 10 MHz clock | **power** | the 45 PVT conditions | C |
| Integrator thermal noise (from [1]), OTA DC gain | noise added at the first integrator; leaky integrators | **accuracy:** SNDR; **security of the original design:** replica attack | sweeps at nominal only | D |
| Integrator capacitor ratios, chip to chip | different loop coefficients in victim and replica | **security of the original design:** replica attack | sweeps at nominal only | E |
| SRAM-PUF noise and temperature behaviour | errors in the 600-bit fingerprint, corrected by the BCH code | **security of the proposal:** key failure | 5 process corners × −40/25/85 °C (no supply axis) | F |
| SRAM-PUF bias | the min-entropy of each fingerprint bit | **security of the proposal:** secret bits left | nominal bias only | F |

The 45 PVT conditions are the grid of Section VII-F: five process corners (tt, ss, ff, sf, fs) × 1.62/1.80/1.98 V × −40/27/125 °C. Each comparator quantity is also swept far beyond its PVT range. The sweep gives the margin: how far the circuit would have to deteriorate (or, for the original design's security, improve) before the system metric changes.

**Limits of the PVT coverage.** Four limits apply to every result below.

1. The SRAM-PUF Monte Carlo covers process × temperature only. It has no supply-voltage axis.
2. Studies D and E sweep at the nominal corner only. The integrators are not simulated at transistor level in this work, so they have no PVT data.
3. The secrecy limit of study F (secret bits left after the helper data is published) uses the nominal bias, not each corner's bias.
4. In study A, the SNDR at each PVT condition is simulated with that condition's noise and no offset. The offset is evaluated separately, because the theory of study A shows that it only shifts the loop's state.

### Simulation setup

**Abstraction level: behavioural, with circuit parameters from SPICE.** The studies run the bit-exact model of Section V with the SKY130-derived settings of Section VII-E. In each run only the circuit quantity under study is changed. The comparator enters the model as a decision threshold: it decides $v[k] = \operatorname{sgn}(x_2[k] + o + n[k])$, where $x_2$ is the second integrator's output, $o$ the chip's offset (one draw from $\mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_{os}^2)$ per chip) and $n[k]$ its noise (a new draw from $\mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_n^2)$ at every decision), with σ<sub>n</sub> and σ<sub>os</sub> from SPICE. The SRAM cell enters as its noise-to-mismatch ratio, temperature behaviour and bias, also from SPICE. This abstraction makes thousands of system runs possible; one frame of 107,400 clocks with the comparator at transistor level would take hours. Section XII tests the abstraction itself, decision by decision, with the transistor-level comparator inside the loop.

**Model units.** The second integrator's output $x_2 = 1$ corresponds to $V_{DD}/4$ at the comparator input (Section VII-B), which is 450 mV at 1.8 V. The post-layout σ<sub>n</sub> = 0.575 mV is therefore 1.28 × 10<sup>−3</sup> model units.

**Common settings** (all from earlier sections; the testbench card below prints them):

| Setting | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Comparator | σ<sub>n</sub> = 0.575 mV, σ<sub>os</sub> = 4.37 mV (post-layout, tt, 27 °C, 1.8 V); at PVT, σ<sub>n</sub> up to 0.812 mV and σ<sub>os</sub> up to 5.85 mV | Section VII-D and -F |
| First integrator's thermal noise | 1.80 × 10<sup>−5</sup> of full scale (FS) rms per clock referred to the modulator input, added to x<sub>1</sub> as g<sub>1</sub> × 1.80 × 10<sup>−5</sup> = 0.90 × 10<sup>−5</sup> | the 9.48 pA measured in [1], Section VII-E |
| SRAM-PUF | noise-to-mismatch ratio s<sub>25</sub> = 0.0225 at 25 °C; 600-cell fingerprint; BCH t = 45 | Section VII-E |
| Accuracy input | a sine at the sensor's full-scale current, through the TIA and buffer, which reaches the modulator with amplitude 0.249 of its full scale, 107,400 clocks (one frame) | Section V-C |
| Accuracy metric | SNDR of the receiver's decoded output (CIC and compensation filters, OSR = 50; 2,048-point Blackman-Harris FFT); sweeps average three noise seeds | Section V-C |
| Attack input | a constant sensor current of 0.5 µA (modulator input 0.134), 30,000 clocks per frame, up to four frames per chip pair | the replica attack of [1], Section V-E |

**The replica attack.** This is the security metric of studies B, D and E. The original design transmits $C = D \oplus K$, the modulator bits $D$ XORed with the keystream $K$ of a 16-bit LFSR. The attacker possesses a second chip of the same design, a *replica*, applies the same known input to it and reads its modulator bits $\hat{D}$, which on the attacker's own chip are not encrypted. The attacker's estimate of the keystream is

$$\hat{K} = C \oplus \hat{D} = K \oplus (D \oplus \hat{D}),$$

which is correct wherever the two chips made the same decisions. A window of 64 bits of $\hat{K}$ *yields the key* when the LFSR that Berlekamp-Massey finds in it predicts the next 512 keystream bits with more than 99 % accuracy; the attacker can confirm a candidate by decrypting the chip ID. Two attackers are simulated on the same pairs.

* *The full-scan, multi-frame attacker (the security criterion).* It records up to four frames of 30,000 clocks from the victim (each with a new noise realisation of both chips) and examines **every** 64-bit window of each frame from clock 200 on, about 29,700 windows per frame, after the start-up in which both chips leave the same reset state. Berlekamp-Massey tolerates wrong bits only at the start of a window, within its first L + 1 = 17 bits (L = 16 is the LFSR's length): in the testbench's check (card), a single wrong bit among the first 16 bits of a window never prevents the key from being found, one at bit 17 prevents it in most trials, and one at bit 18 or later in every trial. The scan therefore runs Berlekamp-Massey on every window whose last 40 bits are clean, which includes every window that can yield the key, and stops at the first that does. A pair is *broken* when any window of its frames yields the key.
* *The attacker of [1] (secondary).* The tool `window_attack` of Section V-E runs Berlekamp-Massey on 80 windows at random positions of the first frame. This is the attack under which earlier versions of this study counted a design as protected when fewer than 10 % of the pairs were compromised; it is kept for comparison and for the theory below.

**Security criterion.** A design is secure against the replica attack when the full-scan attacker's success probability is negligible. A simulation cannot show a probability of, say, 2<sup>−64</sup>; what it can show is an upper confidence bound. This study therefore calls a setting **protected** when the full-scan attacker breaks none of at least 100 independent pairs: the 95 % Clopper-Pearson upper bound on its success probability per pair is then 3.6 %, and the bound per frame (at least 400 frames) 0.92 % or less. Every broken fraction is given with its 95 % Clopper-Pearson interval (error bars in the figures).

**Independent pairs.** Every pair draws its own seeds from the pair index: the two chips' comparator offsets, capacitor-ratio errors (study E), dither seeds and noise seeds, and every frame has its own noise realisation. The pairs at different swept points are also independent. For the theory, the testbench also measures in the first frame of each pair the fraction p of bits that differ and the fraction f<sub>64</sub> of 64-bit windows in which no bit differs (a *clean* window).

**Statistics.** Every swept point starts with 24 pairs. Each point in the transition (some but not all pairs broken), and the first point above it at which no pair is broken, is then raised to 100 pairs, so that the protection point always rests on at least 100 pairs. Each PVT condition has 8 pairs (360 in all). The SNDR sweeps average three noise seeds.

**Bare loop.** The exact identities of the theory (studies A and E) are checked on the modulator's loop without dither, noise or clipping.

**Recorded and live.** All system runs execute live, in at most about 20 s per study on two cores (each card gives its run time). Only their circuit inputs at PVT come from the recorded grids of Section VII-F, whose summary gives the commands that regenerate them.

> **Next cell.** 1. Builds the SKY130-derived settings `P_sys`: the model's defaults with the post-layout circuit values. 2. Generates the two inputs (the sine for accuracy, the constant 0.5 µA for the attack) and the original design's keystream. 3. Defines `sndr_at` (the SNDR of the decoded sine), `replica_pairs` (the replica attack on n independent chip pairs, with the full-scan and the 80-window attacker), `rp_summary` (both attackers' success with Clopper-Pearson intervals, p, f<sub>64</sub> and the theory's bound), `replica_sweep` (a sweep that raises the points near the protection point to 100 pairs), `protection` (the first swept value from which no pair is broken), `bm_tolerance` (Berlekamp-Massey's tolerance of one wrong bit, by its position in the window), `bare_loop` (the loop without dither, noise or clipping) and `crossing` (where a swept curve crosses a level). 4. Sets the sweep ranges and prints the testbench card.


```python
#@title System-level testbench
# The system-level testbench shared by studies A to F: the link of Section V with the post-layout
# circuit values, its two inputs, and the two system metrics: the decoded SNDR (accuracy) and the success of the replica
# attack (security of the original design). Only the quantity under study is changed from run to run.
t0 = time.time()
from scipy.stats import beta as beta_dist
P_sys = {**DEFAULTS, **CAL}
VU = lambda vdd: 0.25 * vdd                         # model unit of the comparator input (cs.map_to_model): x2 = 1 <-> VDD/4
u_sine = s2d(tia(sensor_current({**P_sys, "sig": "sine"}, N_DSM), P_sys["rtia"]), P_sys["buffer"])   # accuracy input
u_dc = np.full(LAB_N, s2d(tia(0.5e-6, P_sys["rtia"]), P_sys["buffer"]))                             # attack input
K16 = lfsr16_bits(DEFAULTS["key16"], ID_BITS + LAB_N)[ID_BITS:]           # the original design's keystream
REPLICA_DITHER = (0x2C4D, 0x51E7)                                         # the replica chip's own dither seeds
Qn = lambda sn_v, vdd=1.8: {**P_sys, "comp_noise": sn_v / VU(vdd)}       # settings with a comparator noise in volts

def sndr_at(P, seed=0, **kw):
    """SNDR of the decoded full-scale sine (2,048-point FFT of the receiver's output)."""
    return sndr(decode(dsm2(u_sine, P, noise_seed=seed, **kw)["D"]), P["bin"])

N_FRAMES = 4                                      # frames of 30,000 clocks per pair that the full-scan attacker records
SCAN0 = 200                                       # first window start (after the start-up, as in window_attack)
K16X = lfsr16_bits(DEFAULTS["key16"], ID_BITS + LAB_N + 600)[ID_BITS:]   # the keystream, with 576 bits past the capture
TAIL = 40                                         # a window yields the key only if its last 40 bits are clean (BM check below)

def cp95(k, n):
    """Clopper-Pearson 95 % interval of a binomial fraction k/n."""
    return (0.0 if k == 0 else float(beta_dist.ppf(0.025, k, n - k + 1)),
            1.0 if k == n else float(beta_dist.ppf(0.975, k + 1, n - k)))

def full_scan(D1, D2):
    """The full-scan attacker on one frame: every 64-bit window of the keystream guess from clock SCAN0 on. Windows whose
    last TAIL bits are clean are run through Berlekamp-Massey (the others cannot yield the key); a window yields the key
    when its register predicts the next 512 keystream bits with more than 99 % accuracy. Returns (key found, number of
    windows scanned, fraction of windows with no differing bit, f64)."""
    e = (D1 ^ D2).astype(np.int64); kg = D1 ^ K16X[:len(D1)] ^ D2
    c = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(e)]); s = np.arange(SCAN0, len(e) - 63)
    f64 = float(np.mean(c[s + 64] == c[s]))
    for s0 in s[c[s + 64] == c[s + 64 - TAIL]]:
        if bm_attack(kg[s0:s0 + 64], K16X[s0 + 64:s0 + 576])["acc"] > 0.99:
            return True, len(s), f64
    return False, len(s), f64

def replica_pairs(P, sos_v, vdd, n, seed, coef_sigma=0.0, k0=0, frames=N_FRAMES):
    """The replica attack on n victim/replica pairs (pair indices k0 ... k0 + n - 1). Every pair has its own seeds, drawn
    from (seed, k): the two chips' comparator offsets (N(0, sigma_os)), capacitor-ratio errors (N(0, coef_sigma)),
    dither seeds and noise seeds (a new noise realisation in every frame). Two attackers: the full-scan attacker scans
    every window of up to `frames` frames and stops at the first that yields the key (the security criterion); the
    attacker of [1] runs Berlekamp-Massey on 80 random 64-bit windows of the first frame (window_attack). Returns per-pair
    arrays: broken (full scan), frames scanned, broken80, f64 and p of the first frame."""
    out = {k: [] for k in ("broken", "frames", "broken80", "f64", "p")}
    for k in range(k0, k0 + n):
        r = np.random.default_rng((int(seed), k))
        o1, o2 = r.normal(0, sos_v / VU(vdd), 2)
        c1, c2 = (r.normal(0, coef_sigma, 2), r.normal(0, coef_sigma, 2)) if coef_sigma else ((0.0, 0.0), (0.0, 0.0))
        dv, dr = tuple(int(x) for x in r.integers(1, 1 << 16, 2)), tuple(int(x) for x in r.integers(1, 1 << 16, 2))
        nv, nr = (int(x) for x in r.integers(1, 1 << 30, 2))
        hit = False
        for f in range(frames):
            D1 = dsm2(u_dc, P, seeds=dv, noise_seed=nv + 7919 * f, offset=o1, coef_err=c1)["D"]
            D2 = dsm2(u_dc, P, seeds=dr, noise_seed=nr + 7919 * f, offset=o2, coef_err=c2)["D"]
            hit, _, f64 = full_scan(D1, D2)
            if f == 0:
                x = (D1 ^ D2)[SCAN0:].astype(np.int64)
                out["broken80"].append(window_attack(D1 ^ K16 ^ D2, K16, (int(seed) * 100003 + k) & 0xFFFFFFF)["broken"] > 0)
                out["f64"].append(f64); out["p"].append(float(x.mean()))
            if hit:
                break
        out["broken"].append(hit); out["frames"].append(f + 1)
    return {k: np.array(v) for k, v in out.items()}

def rp_merge(a, b):                               # more pairs of the same setting
    return {k: np.concatenate([a[k], b[k]]) for k in a}

def rp_summary(R):
    """Success of both attackers with Clopper-Pearson 95 % intervals, and the theory's ingredients."""
    n, k, k80 = len(R["broken"]), int(R["broken"].sum()), int(R["broken80"].sum())
    nf = int(R["frames"][~R["broken"]].sum())         # frames scanned without success (all frames of the unbroken pairs)
    return dict(n=n, k=k, success=k / n, ci=cp95(k, n), k80=k80, success80=k80 / n, ci80=cp95(k80, n),
                f64=float(R["f64"].mean()), p=float(R["p"].mean()), bound=float(np.mean(1 - (1 - R["f64"]) ** 80)),
                frames_clean=nf, frame_hi=cp95(0, nf)[1] if (k == 0 and nf) else None)

def replica_sweep(run, xs, n0=24, n_top=100):
    """run(x, n, k0) -> per-pair arrays. A coarse pass with n0 pairs at every point; then every point in the transition
    (some but not all pairs broken) and the first point above it with no pair broken get n_top pairs in total, repeated
    until the first unbroken point above the last broken one has n_top pairs."""
    R = [run(x, n0, 0) for x in xs]
    while True:
        ks = [int(r["broken"].sum()) for r in R]; ns = [len(r["broken"]) for r in R]
        brk = [i for i, k in enumerate(ks) if k > 0]
        want = {i for i, (k, m) in enumerate(zip(ks, ns)) if 0 < k < m}
        if brk and brk[-1] + 1 < len(xs):
            want.add(brk[-1] + 1)
        todo = [i for i in sorted(want) if ns[i] < n_top]
        if not todo:
            return [rp_summary(r) for r in R]
        for i in todo:
            R[i] = rp_merge(R[i], run(xs[i], n_top - ns[i], ns[i]))

def protection(xs, S):
    """The protection point of a sweep: the first swept value from which on no pair is broken by the full-scan attacker
    (with at least 100 pairs there), and the last value at which a pair is broken. None if the last point is broken."""
    brk = [i for i, s in enumerate(S) if s["k"] > 0]
    i = brk[-1] + 1 if brk else 0
    return (float(xs[i]) if i < len(xs) else None, float(xs[brk[-1]]) if brk else None, S[i] if i < len(xs) else None)

def bm_tolerance(trials=20):
    """How Berlekamp-Massey tolerates one wrong bit in a 64-bit window, by its position: the share of trials that still
    yield the key (random positions of the original design's keystream)."""
    r = np.random.default_rng(64); ok = np.zeros(64)
    for j in range(64):
        for _ in range(trials):
            s0 = int(r.integers(SCAN0, LAB_N - 64)); w = K16X[s0:s0 + 64].copy(); w[j] ^= 1
            ok[j] += bm_attack(w, K16X[s0 + 64:s0 + 576])["acc"] > 0.99
    return ok / trials
BM_TOL = bm_tolerance()

def bare_loop(u, offset=0.0, x2_0=0.0, g1=0.5, g2=0.5):
    """The modulator's loop without dither, noise or clipping, for the exact identities of the theory."""
    x1, x2, y, out = 0.0, x2_0, 1, np.zeros(len(u), np.uint8)
    for k in range(len(u)):
        v = 1.0 if y else -1.0
        x1 += g1 * (u[k] - v); x2 += g2 * (x1 - v)
        y = 1 if x2 + offset >= 0 else 0; out[k] = y
    return out

def crossing(xs, ys, level):                        # first x (log-interpolated) at which ys falls below level
    for (x0, y0), (x1, y1) in zip(zip(xs, ys), zip(xs[1:], ys[1:])):
        if y0 >= level > y1:
            return float(np.exp(np.log(x0) + (np.log(x1) - np.log(x0)) * (y0 - level) / (y0 - y1)))
    return None

sn0, os0 = COMP_POST["comp_noise"] * VU(1.8), COMP_POST["comp_offset_sigma"] * VU(1.8)   # the post-layout comparator
sn_max, os_max = max(r["sigma_n"] for r in PVT["cmp"]), max(r["sigma_os"] for r in PVT["cmp"])
SN_SWEEP = np.array([0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100, 300, 1000]) * 1e-3            # comparator noise sweep (V)
OS_SWEEP = np.array([1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300, 600, 1000, 2000, 3000]) * 1e-3             # comparator offset sweep (V)
amp_in = (u_sine.max() - u_sine.min()) / 2
card("System-level testbench",
     [("circuit values (post-layout, tt, 27 °C, 1.8 V)", f"comparator σ<sub>n</sub> = {1e3 * sn0:.3f} mV, σ<sub>os</sub> = {1e3 * os0:.2f} mV; "
       f"integrator noise {P_sys['int_noise']:.2e} FS rms per clock; SRAM-PUF s<sub>25</sub> = {CAL['puf_sigma']:.4f}"),
      ("PVT grid (Section VII-F)", f"{len(PVT['cmp'])} comparator conditions; σ<sub>n</sub> up to {1e3 * sn_max:.3f} mV, "
       f"σ<sub>os</sub> up to {1e3 * os_max:.2f} mV; {len(PVT['puf']['corners'])} SRAM-PUF corners × {len(TEMPS)} temperatures"),
      ("accuracy input", f"full-scale sine through the TIA and buffer: amplitude {amp_in:.3f} of the modulator's full scale, "
       f"{N_DSM:,} clocks, OSR {OSR}"),
      ("attack input", f"constant sensor current 0.5 µA (modulator input {u_dc[0]:.3f}), {LAB_N:,} clocks per chip; "
       f"each pair with its own seeds; full-scan attacker: every 64-bit window of up to {N_FRAMES} frames; attacker of [1]: 80 "
       "random windows of one frame"),
      ("Berlekamp-Massey with one wrong bit in a 64-bit window (20 trials per position)",
       f"key still recovered: positions 1–16 in {100 * BM_TOL[:16].mean():.0f} %, position 17 in {100 * BM_TOL[16]:.0f} %, "
       f"positions 18–64 in {100 * BM_TOL[17:].mean():.0f} %; the scan therefore tests every window whose last {TAIL} bits agree"),
      ("model units", f"x<sub>2</sub> = 1 ↔ V<sub>DD</sub>/4 = {1e3 * VU(1.8):.0f} mV at the comparator input (1.8 V)")])
```

### The complete sensor, end to end

**Goal.** Before each circuit quantity is studied on its own, simulate the complete sensor once at system level: one frame of the proposed design passes through every block of the link with the SKY130 circuit values, at the nominal condition and at a worst condition at which every block sits at the same process corner and temperature. The simulation establishes the reference against which studies A to G measure each effect, and shows that the sensor with its SKY130-derived parameters, key generator, cipher and receiver operate together.

**Theory.** The frame follows the signal chain of Section V, block by block.

1. *Front end.* The sensor current $i(t)$ is converted by the TIA into $v = V_{CM} + R_{TIA}\,i$, and the buffer maps $v$ onto the modulator input $u = G\,(v - V_{CM})/(V_{DD}/2)$, with $G = 0.5$.
2. *Modulator.* The second-order loop of Section V-C converts $u$ into the bit stream $D$. The comparator decides with the SKY130 noise σ<sub>n</sub> and with this chip's offset; the first integrator adds the thermal noise derived from [1]. A second-order loop shapes the quantisation error and the comparator noise by $|\mathrm{NTF}|^2 \propto (2\sin \pi f/f_s)^4$, which rises by 40 dB per decade of frequency in the signal band.
3. *Key.* At power-up the 600 SRAM cells are read at the operating temperature; the BCH decoder corrects up to t = 45 differing cells with the helper data published at enrolment, and the hash of the corrected fingerprint gives the 128-bit key (Section V-D).
4. *Encryption and frame.* Grain-128a, initialised with the key and an IV formed from the session nonce and the frame counter, produces the keystream $K$; the frame carries the preamble, the synchronisation word, the counter, the encrypted chip ID, the ciphertext $C = D \oplus K$ and the 32-bit tag.
5. *Receiver.* The server locates the synchronisation word, verifies the tag with its enrolled key, checks that the counter is fresh, decrypts $D_{rx} = C \oplus K$, and decimates $D_{rx}$ with the CIC and compensation filters to the reading $y$ at 200 kS/s.

*Prediction.* At the nominal condition the number of differing SRAM cells stays well below t, so the key is recovered, the tag verifies and $D_{rx} = D$ bit for bit. At the worst condition (sf corner, 85 °C) the cell law of that corner gives a 5.0 % error rate at 85 °C (recorded, Section VII-F), about 30 of 600 cells, plus the noise of the 25 °C enrolment read; the count comes close to t = 45, so the key should be recovered in this frame but without the 10<sup>−6</sup> reliability, which study F shows this corner reaches only with a larger code or the two-temperature enrolment. The SNDR is set by quantisation noise: the comparator noise, below 1 mV, is two orders of magnitude below the level at which it matters (study A), so the SNDR should be the same at both conditions to within the variation between noise realisations.

*Prediction for the spectra.* The bit-stream spectrum has two regions. Below about 10 kHz the white thermal noise of the first integrator sets a flat floor, since it enters at the input and is not shaped; above it, the shaped quantisation and comparator noise rise by 40 dB per decade and dominate the signal band in total. Toward half the clock rate the shaping levels off: $|\mathrm{NTF}|^2 \propto \sin^4(\pi f/f_s)$ reaches its maximum at $f_s/2$, where the 40 dB-per-decade asymptote overstates it by $40\log_{10}(\pi/2)$ = 7.8 dB. A 1-bit loop also gathers part of its quantisation error into a limit-cycle tone: for a slowly varying input $u$ the bit stream alternates at almost every clock, and the pattern repeats at $(1-|u|)\,f_s/2$. The sine input of amplitude $A$ sweeps this tone between $f_s/2$ and $(1-A)\,f_s/2$ and dwells longest at the turning points, so the bit-stream spectrum should peak close to $(1-A)\,f_s/2$, about 3.8 MHz for $A$ = 0.249, nearly 40 times the band edge.

*Prediction for the decoded output.* Decryption changes no noise: $D_{rx} = C \oplus K = D$ bit for bit, so the decoded output carries exactly the modulator's noise. The receiver's third-order CIC and compensation FIR remove the noise above the band, but not the shaped noise inside it. The floor of the decoded output should therefore not be flat: it should rise by 40 dB per decade across the band, 14.7 dB from 30 to 70 kHz, and fall steeply in the transition band of the compensation filter, centred on 80 kHz. It is flat only at the lowest frequencies, where the white thermal noise exceeds the shaped noise.

*Prediction for an impaired chip.* A floor this clean is a property of the model, not of a chip: the reference model has no clock jitter, no 1/f noise and no input-stage distortion. A third frame therefore adds these impairments with assumed values, to show what they change. (i) *Clock jitter* on the non-return-to-zero (NRZ) feedback DAC of the continuous-time loop: an edge that moves by δt changes the fed-back charge by (*v*<sub>k</sub> − *v*<sub>k−1</sub>) δt/*T*<sub>s</sub>; with ±1 levels and a transition at about half the clocks, σ<sub>t</sub> = 10 ps at *T*<sub>s</sub> = 100 ns gives a white error of about 2 · √0.5 · 10<sup>−4</sup> ≈ 1.4 × 10<sup>−4</sup> of full scale per clock, eight times the integrator noise, so the floor should rise by about 18 dB. (ii) *1/f noise* at the integrator input, with a corner *f*<sub>c</sub> at which it equals the white thermal density: the floor rises by 10 log(1 + *f*<sub>c</sub>/*f*), about 10 dB at 5 kHz for *f*<sub>c</sub> = 50 kHz. (iii) *Distortion* of the input stage, *u* + *a*<sub>2</sub>*u*<sup>2</sup> + *a*<sub>3</sub>*u*<sup>3</sup>, gives harmonics at 40 and 60 kHz, inside the band, which the loop does not suppress. Neither floor contributes much to the in-band noise, which the shaped quantisation noise dominates, so the SNDR should drop mainly through the third harmonic.

**Setup.** Behavioural model of the complete link (Section V) with the SKY130-derived settings of the testbench above; one frame of 107,400 modulator clocks (10.74 ms) with the full-scale sine input; the same seeds at both conditions, so that only the circuit values differ.

| Condition | Comparator | SRAM array |
|---|---|---|
| nominal | post-layout σ<sub>n</sub> and an offset of +1 σ<sub>os</sub>, tt, 27 °C, 1.80 V | 37 °C (body or bioreactor temperature) |
| worst | the process corner and supply of the PVT condition with the largest σ<sub>n</sub> (sf, 1.80 V), at 85 °C: σ<sub>n</sub> and σ<sub>os</sub> interpolated linearly between the recorded 27 and 125 °C points of that corner, with +1 σ<sub>os</sub> | 85 °C (the upper end of the specified range), cell law of the same corner: the noise-to-mismatch ratio that reproduces its recorded error rates at 25 and 85 °C, and its bias |

*Noise sources of the two reference frames:* the thermal noise of the first integrator (white, 1.8 × 10<sup>−5</sup> of full scale rms per clock, derived from the input-referred noise of [1]), the comparator noise and offset (SKY130, above), and the dither. Not included: clock jitter, 1/f noise, distortion, excess loop delay, DAC level mismatch, and supply and reference noise.

*Third frame, "impaired":* the nominal condition with assumed impairments, since [1] reports none of them: 10 ps rms jitter on the DAC edges (an on-chip clock derived from a crystal reference; a free-running oscillator would be worse), a 1/f corner of 50 kHz (a moderate-area SKY130 input pair), and an input stage with second- and third-harmonic distortion HD2 = −80 dBc and HD3 = −70 dBc at the test amplitude (*a*<sub>2</sub> and *a*<sub>3</sub> are set from these). Each impairment is also simulated alone, and eight further noise realisations of the nominal frame give the spread of a single frame's SNDR, against which the differences are judged.

Both conditions use one process corner for every block, so that the worst frame does not combine a comparator of one corner with the SRAM cell of another. The spectra are computed with the four-term Blackman-Harris window used by the SNDR measurement: the bit stream with Welch's method (16,384-point segments), the decoded output for the figure with Welch's method (1,024-point segments, 195 Hz bins) and for the harmonics with one 2,048-point transform. Spectra are normalised so that a full-scale sine reads 0 dBFS. *SNDR bandwidth:* `sndr()` integrates the noise of the decoded output from 391 Hz (bin 4) to 100 kHz, the Nyquist frequency of the 200 kS/s output; the compensation filter's transition band is centred on 80 kHz, so the noise between 80 and 100 kHz is attenuated but counted (the spectra card gives the SNDR integrated to 80 kHz for comparison). The process corners of the SRAM array are the subject of study F.

> **Next cell.** 1. Selects the comparator's noisiest PVT condition from the recorded grid and builds the worst condition at its corner and 85 °C (comparator values interpolated in temperature, SRAM cell law of the same corner). 2. Simulates one frame of the proposed design at each of the two conditions with `simulate()`. 3. Reports, for each condition, the modulator's bit statistics and integrator clipping, the SRAM-PUF errors against t with the key-failure probability, the receiver's checks and the SNDR. 4. Draws every block's signal for the nominal frame (the sensor current normalised, *x*<sub>2</sub> normalised to its clipping level), with the true reading (the input, delayed and scaled by the receiver's filters) under the server's output and, above it, the two checks of the frame.

```python
#@title Fig.: the complete sensor, end to end
# The complete sensor, end to end: one frame of the proposed design through every block of the link (sensor current,
# TIA, buffer, modulator with the SKY130 comparator, SRAM-PUF key, Grain-128a with MAC, frame, channel, receiver,

_q = PUF_CELL[cw["corner"]]; s25_w, s85_w = float(_q["s1"](25)), float(_q["s1"](T_W))

    "worst": dict(label=f"worst: every block at the {cw['corner']} corner and {T_W:.0f} °C ({cw['vdd']:.2f} V), the corner of the noisiest comparator",
                  over=dict(comp_noise=sn_w / VU(cw["vdd"]), comp_offset=os_w / VU(cw["vdd"]), temp=T_W, puf_sigma=s25_w,
                            puf_tc=(s85_w / s25_w - 1) / (T_W - 25), puf_bias=float(ndtr(_q["mu"]))),
                  sn=sn_w, os=os_w, vdd=cw["vdd"], T=T_W)}
FRAMES = {k: simulate(**{**P_sys, **c["over"]}) for k, c in FRAME_CASES.items()}
TIM_FRAME = time.time() - t0
def _frame_rows(k):
    c, S = FRAME_CASES[k], FRAMES[k]
    return [(f"<b>{c['label']}</b>", f"comparator σ<sub>n</sub> = {1e3 * c['sn']:.3f} mV, offset of this chip +1 σ<sub>os</sub> = "
             f"{1e3 * c['os']:.2f} mV"),
            ("modulator", f"fraction of ones {S['ones']:.3f}; longest run of equal bits {S['run']}; integrator clipping "
             f"{100 * S['clip']:.3f} % of clocks"),
            ("SRAM-PUF key", f"{S['n_err_true']} of {PUF_BITS} cells differ from the enrolment (t = {S['P']['bch_t']}; expected "
             f"Σp<sub>i</sub> = {S['p_err'].sum():.1f}); key {'recovered' if S['key_match'] else '<b>NOT recovered</b>'}; "
             f"P(key fails) at {c['T']:.0f} °C = {S['key_fail']:.1e} (cell law: noise-to-mismatch ratio {S['P']['puf_sigma']:.4f} at 25 °C, "
             f"{S['P']['puf_sigma'] * (1 + S['P']['puf_tc'] * abs(c['T'] - 25)):.4f} at {c['T']:.0f} °C)"),
            ("receiver", f"chip ID check {'passed' if S['id_ok'] else '<b>failed</b>'}; MAC {'verified' if S['mac_ok'] else '<b>rejected</b>'}; "
             f"counter fresh: {S['ctr_fresh']}; decrypted bits equal to the modulator bits: {np.array_equal(S['D_rx'], S['D'])}"),
            ("decoded reading", f"SNDR <b>{S['sndr']:.1f} dB</b>; reading − input (delayed and scaled) "
             f"{100 * np.sqrt(np.mean(reading_error(S)[3][60:-10] ** 2)):.3f} % of full scale rms")]
card("The complete sensor, end to end: one frame of the proposed design",
     _frame_rows("nominal") + _frame_rows("worst") + [("frame", f"{N_DSM:,} modulator clocks ({1e3 * N_DSM / FS:.2f} ms), "
                                                       f"{len(FRAMES['nominal']['frame']):,} bits on air; run time {TIM_FRAME:.1f} s")],
     tone="ok" if all(S["accepted"] and S["key_match"] for S in FRAMES.values()) else "bad")
plot_chain(FRAMES["nominal"]); plt.show()                         # the nominal frame; the caption names the condition
```

<p align="center" style="text-align:center"><b>Fig. 38.</b> The complete sensor, end to end: one frame of the proposed design (behavioural model with the SKY130 parameters; comparator tt, 27 °C, 1.80 V; SRAM array at 37 °C). Rows, clocks 2,100 to 2,299 (no vertical scale): sensor current, <i>x</i><sub>2</sub>, <i>D</i>, <i>K</i> (red), <i>C</i>, <i>D</i><sub>rx</sub>. Bottom, output samples 60 to 179: server output (black) on the input delayed and scaled by the receiver's filters (grey).</p>

> **Next cell.** 1. Simulates a third frame at the nominal condition with the assumed impairments (DAC clock jitter, 1/f noise, input-stage distortion), one frame with each impairment alone, and eight further noise realisations of the nominal frame. 2. Computes the power spectrum of each frame's bit stream (Welch) and of its decoded output (Welch for the figure, one transform for the harmonics). 3. Reports the noise sources of each frame, the low-frequency floor of the bit stream (2 to 8 kHz), its in-band noise from 1 kHz to the band edge, the second and third harmonics of the decoded output, the strongest bit-stream component above 1 MHz with the share of the power there, the gain of the receiver's filters near the band edge, the rise of the decoded-output floor across the band, the SNDR of each frame, the SNDR with the noise integrated only to 80 kHz, and the spread of the SNDR between realisations. 4. Draws the spectra of the nominal, worst and impaired frames, with the limit-cycle tone and the filter roll-off marked.


```python
#@title Fig.: the complete sensor, end to end: spectra
# The same two frames in the frequency domain, plus a third frame with circuit impairments that the reference model leaves
# out: (a) the spectrum of the modulator's bitstream, which shows the noise shaping of the second-order loop up to half
# the clock rate; (b) the spectrum of the receiver's decoded output in the signal band, from which the SNDR is computed
from scipy.signal import welch
# assumed impairments (no values in [1]): 10 ps rms jitter on the NRZ feedback-DAC edges, a 50 kHz 1/f corner of the
# input-referred noise, and an input stage with HD2 = -80 dBc and HD3 = -70 dBc at the test amplitude
IMPAIR = dict(jitter_ps=10.0, flicker_fc=50e3, hd2_dbc=-80.0, hd3_dbc=-70.0)
IMP_KW = dict(jitter=dict(jitter_ps=IMPAIR["jitter_ps"]), flicker=dict(flicker_fc=IMPAIR["flicker_fc"]),
              distortion=dict(hd_a2=2 * 10 ** (IMPAIR["hd2_dbc"] / 20) / amp_in, hd_a3=4 * 10 ** (IMPAIR["hd3_dbc"] / 20) / amp_in ** 2))
_nom = {**P_sys, **FRAME_CASES["nominal"]["over"]}
FRAMES_SPEC = {**FRAMES, "impaired": simulate(**{**_nom, **{k: v for kw in IMP_KW.values() for k, v in kw.items()}})}
FRAMES_ALONE = {k: simulate(**{**_nom, **kw}) for k, kw in IMP_KW.items()}   # each impairment on its own, for the breakdown
SNDR_SPREAD = np.array([simulate(**{**_nom, "seed": _nom["seed"] + 100 + i})["sndr"] for i in range(8)])   # noise realisations
F_SIG = DEFAULTS["bin"] * FS_OUT / N_FFT                          # the test tone (Hz)
F_BAND = FS / (2 * OSR)                                           # the signal band of the receiver (Hz)
def bh(n):                                                        # four-term Blackman-Harris window, as in sndr()
    x = 2 * np.pi * np.arange(n) / (n - 1)
    return 0.35875 - 0.48829 * np.cos(x) + 0.14128 * np.cos(2 * x) - 0.01168 * np.cos(3 * x)
NW_Y = 1024                                                       # Welch segments of the decoded output (195 Hz bins)
SPEC = {}
for k, S in {**FRAMES_SPEC, **FRAMES_ALONE}.items():
    f, p = welch(2.0 * S["D"] - 1.0, fs=FS, window=bh(16384), nperseg=16384, scaling="spectrum")   # bitstream, ±1
    y = np.asarray(S["y"][-N_FFT:], float); w = bh(N_FFT)
    py = np.abs(np.fft.rfft((y - y.mean()) * w)) ** 2 / (w.sum() / 2) ** 2                     # decoded output; full-scale sine = 0 dBFS
    fd, pd = welch(2.0 * S["D"] - 1.0, fs=FS, window=bh(16384), nperseg=16384, scaling="density")  # for noise integration
    fw, pw = welch(np.asarray(S["y"][60:], float), fs=FS_OUT, window=bh(NW_Y), nperseg=NW_Y, scaling="spectrum")  # decoded, averaged
    SPEC[k] = dict(f=f, p=p, pd=pd, fy=np.fft.rfftfreq(N_FFT, 1 / FS_OUT), py=py, fw=fw, pw=pw / 0.5)
# the in-band noise of the bitstream, integrated from 1 kHz to the band edge, excluding the tone: one number per case
def inband_noise(s):                                              # noise power / full-scale sine power, in dB
    m = (s["f"] > 1e3) & (s["f"] < F_BAND) & (np.abs(s["f"] - F_SIG) > 4 * FS / 16384)
    return 10 * np.log10(s["pd"][m].sum() * (s["f"][1] - s["f"][0]) / 0.5)
def floor_db(s, f0=2e3, f1=8e3):                                  # the low-frequency floor of the bitstream (dBFS per bin)
    m = (s["f"] >= f0) & (s["f"] <= f1)
    return 10 * np.log10(np.median(s["p"][m]) / 0.5)
# what shapes the two panels: (a) above 1 MHz, the strongest component of the bitstream and the share of its power there; the
# limit-cycle tone of a 1-bit loop lies at (1 - |u|) fs/2 for a slowly varying input u, so the sine of amplitude A sweeps it
# down to (1 - A) fs/2, where it dwells longest; (b) the receiver's filters (3rd-order CIC at 10 MHz x the 31-tap compensation
# FIR at 200 kS/s) and the rise of the decoded noise floor across the band against the 40 dB per decade of the shaped noise
from scipy.signal import freqz
def hf_peak(s):                                                   # (frequency, dBFS per bin, share of power above 1 MHz)
    m = s["f"] > 1e6; j = int(np.argmax(s["p"][m]))
    return s["f"][m][j], 10 * np.log10(s["p"][m][j] / 0.5), s["p"][m].sum() / s["p"].sum()
def rx_gain_db(f):                                                # receiver filter gain at f (Hz), relative to DC
    cic3 = np.abs(np.sin(np.pi * f * OSR / FS) / (OSR * np.sin(np.pi * f / FS))) ** 3
    return 20 * np.log10(cic3 * np.abs(freqz(COMP_TAPS, worN=[f], fs=FS_OUT)[1][0]))
def out_floor(s, f0, f1):                                         # median decoded-output floor between f0 and f1 (dBFS per
    m = (s["fw"] >= f0) & (s["fw"] <= f1)                         # 195 Hz bin of the Welch average)
    return 10 * np.log10(np.median(s["pw"][m]))
HF = hf_peak(SPEC["nominal"])
def sndr_to(S, f_hi):                                             # SNDR as sndr() computes it, with the noise integrated to f_hi
    y = np.asarray(S["y"][-N_FFT:], float); w = bh(N_FFT); p = np.abs(np.fft.fft((y - y.mean()) * w)) ** 2
    k = np.arange(4, int(round(f_hi / (FS_OUT / N_FFT))) + 1); k = k[k < N_FFT // 2]; b0 = DEFAULTS["bin"]
    sig = p[k[np.abs(k - b0) <= 4]].sum()
    return 10 * np.log10(sig / (p[k].sum() - sig))
def hd_dbc(s, h):                                                 # harmonic h of the decoded output relative to the tone (dBc)
    b0 = DEFAULTS["bin"]; pw = lambda b: s["py"][b - 3:b + 4].sum()
    return 10 * np.log10(pw(h * b0) / pw(b0))
card("The complete sensor, end to end: spectra",
     [("test tone", f"{F_SIG / 1e3:.2f} kHz, amplitude {amp_in:.3f} of full scale ({20 * np.log10(amp_in):.1f} dBFS); signal band 0–{F_BAND / 1e3:.0f} kHz "
       f"(clock {FS / 1e6:.0f} MHz, OSR {OSR})"),
      ("noise in the reference model (nominal, worst)", "integrator thermal noise (white, 1.8 × 10<sup>−5</sup> FS rms per clock, from [1]); "
       "comparator noise and offset (SKY130); dither; no distortion, 1/f noise, clock jitter, excess loop delay or supply noise"),
      ("assumed impairments (impaired)", f"DAC clock jitter {IMPAIR['jitter_ps']:.0f} ps rms; 1/f corner {IMPAIR['flicker_fc'] / 1e3:.0f} kHz; "
       f"input stage HD2 {IMPAIR['hd2_dbc']:.0f} dBc, HD3 {IMPAIR['hd3_dbc']:.0f} dBc; otherwise the nominal condition"),
      ("low-frequency floor of the bitstream (2–8 kHz)", ", ".join(f"{k}: {floor_db(SPEC[k]):.1f} dBFS/bin" for k in FRAMES_SPEC)),
      ("in-band quantisation and circuit noise of the bitstream (1 kHz to the band edge)",
       ", ".join(f"{k}: {inband_noise(SPEC[k]):.1f} dBFS" for k in FRAMES_SPEC)),
      ("HD2, HD3 of the decoded output", ", ".join(f"{k}: {hd_dbc(SPEC[k], 2):.1f}, {hd_dbc(SPEC[k], 3):.1f} dBc" for k in FRAMES_SPEC)),
      ("each impairment alone (floor 2–8 kHz; HD3; SNDR)", "; ".join(
          f"{k}: {floor_db(SPEC[k]):.1f} dBFS/bin, {hd_dbc(SPEC[k], 3):.1f} dBc, {S['sndr']:.1f} dB" for k, S in FRAMES_ALONE.items())),
      ("bitstream above 1 MHz (nominal): strongest component; share of the bitstream power",
       f"{HF[0] / 1e6:.2f} MHz at {HF[1]:.1f} dBFS/bin (the 1-bit loop's limit-cycle tone, swept by the sine down to (1 − A)·f<sub>s</sub>/2 = "
       f"{(1 - amp_in) * FS / 2e6:.2f} MHz); {100 * HF[2]:.0f} % of the power lies above 1 MHz"),
      ("receiver filter (CIC × compensation) gain at 20, 80, 90, 100 kHz",
       ", ".join(f"{rx_gain_db(f):.1f}" for f in (20e3, 80e3, 90e3, 100e3)) + " dB (the transition band of the 31-tap compensation FIR is centred on 0.4 f<sub>out</sub> = 80 kHz)"),
      (f"decoded-output floor, 25–35 kHz and 65–75 kHz (nominal; Welch average, {NW_Y}-point segments, {FS_OUT / NW_Y:.0f} Hz bins)",
       f"{out_floor(SPEC['nominal'], 25e3, 35e3):.1f} and {out_floor(SPEC['nominal'], 65e3, 75e3):.1f} dBFS/bin: a rise of "
       f"{out_floor(SPEC['nominal'], 65e3, 75e3) - out_floor(SPEC['nominal'], 25e3, 35e3):.1f} dB, against "
       f"{40 * np.log10(70 / 30):.1f} dB for noise rising at 40 dB per decade"),
      ("SNDR spread of single nominal frames (8 noise realisations)", f"mean {SNDR_SPREAD.mean():.1f} dB, σ {SNDR_SPREAD.std():.1f} dB, "
       f"range {SNDR_SPREAD.min():.1f} to {SNDR_SPREAD.max():.1f} dB"),
      ("SNDR bandwidth", f"sndr() integrates the noise from bin 4 ({4 * FS_OUT / N_FFT:.0f} Hz) to {FS_OUT / 2e3:.0f} kHz, the Nyquist frequency "
       f"of the decoded output; integrated only to the 80 kHz edge of the compensation filter instead: nominal "
       f"{sndr_to(FRAMES_SPEC['nominal'], 80e3):.1f} dB (to {FS_OUT / 2e3:.0f} kHz: {sndr_to(FRAMES_SPEC['nominal'], FS_OUT / 2):.1f} dB)"),
      ("SNDR of the decoded output (2,048-point Blackman-Harris FFT, noise to 100 kHz)", ", ".join(f"{k}: <b>{S['sndr']:.1f} dB</b>" for k, S in FRAMES_SPEC.items()))])
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(W2, 3.1))
sty = {"impaired": dict(color=COL["aqua"], lw=0.8), "nominal": dict(color=COL["ok"], lw=1.0),
       "worst": dict(color=COL["bad"], lw=0.8, alpha=0.8)}
ax = axs[0]
for k in ("impaired", "nominal", "worst"):
    s = SPEC[k]
    ax.semilogx(s["f"][1:], 10 * np.log10(s["p"][1:] / 0.5 + 1e-30), label=f"{k} ({FRAMES_SPEC[k]['sndr']:.1f} dB)", **sty[k])
fr = np.logspace(np.log10(2e4), np.log10(1e6), 50)
ref = 10 * np.log10(SPEC["nominal"]["p"][np.searchsorted(SPEC["nominal"]["f"], 1e6)] / 0.5)
ax.semilogx(fr, ref + 40 * np.log10(fr / 1e6), "--", color=COL["ink"], lw=0.9, label="40 dB/decade")
fl = floor_db(SPEC["nominal"])
ax.hlines(fl, 1.2e3, 1.5e4, color=COL["ink"], lw=0.9, ls=":")
ax.text(1.3e3, fl - 4, "white floor: integrator\nthermal noise", fontsize=7.5, color=COL["ink"], va="top")
ax.annotate("floor raised\nby DAC\nclock jitter", (6e3, floor_db(SPEC["impaired"])), xytext=(2.7e3, -80), ha="left", va="center",
            fontsize=7.5, color=COL["aqua"], arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", lw=0.6, color=COL["aqua"], shrinkB=1))
_fq = 4e5; _pq = 10 * np.log10(np.median(SPEC["nominal"]["p"][np.abs(SPEC["nominal"]["f"] - _fq) < 2e4]) / 0.5)
ax.annotate("shaped\nquantisation and\ncomparator noise", (_fq, _pq + 4), xytext=(1.35e5, -20), ha="left", va="center",
            fontsize=7.5, color=COL["ink"], arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", lw=0.6, color=COL["ink"], shrinkB=1))
ax.annotate("limit-cycle tone,\n$(1-A)\\,f_s/2$", (HF[0], HF[1]), xytext=(2.2e6, -72), ha="center", va="center",
            fontsize=7.5, color=COL["ink"], arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", lw=0.7, color=COL["ink"]))
ax.axvline(F_BAND, color=COL["faint"], ls=":", lw=1)
ax.text(F_BAND * 0.9, 0.97, "band edge", fontsize=7, color=COL["faint"], rotation=90, va="top", ha="right", transform=ax.get_xaxis_transform())
ax.set_ylim(-152, 0); ax.set_xlim(FS / 16384, FS / 2); ax.set_xlabel("Frequency (Hz)"); ax.set_ylabel("Power (dBFS per bin)")
ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="lower right"); panel(ax, "a", "modulator bitstream")
ax = axs[1]
for k in ("impaired", "nominal", "worst"):
    s = SPEC[k]
    ax.plot(s["fw"] / 1e3, 10 * np.log10(s["pw"] + 1e-30), **{**sty[k], "lw": 1.2}, label=k)
si = SPEC["impaired"]; _jh = int(np.argmin(np.abs(si["fw"] - 3 * F_SIG)))   # the third harmonic of the impaired frame
ax.annotate("HD3", (si["fw"][_jh] / 1e3, 10 * np.log10(si["pw"][_jh])), xytext=(3 * F_SIG / 1e3, -45), ha="center", va="center",
            fontsize=7.5, color=COL["aqua"], arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", lw=0.6, color=COL["aqua"], shrinkB=1))
_j = int(np.searchsorted(SPEC["nominal"]["fw"], 88e3))
ax.annotate("receiver filter\nroll-off, 80–100 kHz", (88, 10 * np.log10(SPEC["nominal"]["pw"][_j])), xytext=(80, -25), ha="center",
            va="center", fontsize=7.5, color=COL["ink"], arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", lw=0.6, color=COL["ink"], shrinkB=1))
ax.set_xlim(0, F_BAND / 1e3); ax.set_xlabel("Frequency (kHz)"); ax.set_ylabel("Power (dBFS per bin)")
ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.55, 0.02), ncol=3); panel(ax, "b", "decoded output, signal band")
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

<p align="center" style="text-align:center"><b>Fig. 39.</b> Spectra of the complete sensor (0 dBFS: full-scale sine). Blue: nominal; orange: noisiest comparator condition, every block at sf and 85 °C; green: nominal with assumed impairments (10 ps rms DAC clock jitter, 50 kHz 1/f corner, HD2 −80 dBc, HD3 −70 dBc). (a) Modulator bit stream (Welch, 16,384-point segments); dashed: 40 dB per decade; dotted: 100 kHz band edge. (b) Decoded output (Welch, 1,024-point segments, 195 Hz bins). Legend: SNDR of each frame.</p>

**Result.** At the nominal condition, 13 of the 600 SRAM cells differ from the enrolment (expected 11.2), far below t = 45; the key is recovered, the chip ID and the tag verify, the counter is fresh, and the decrypted bits equal the modulator bits (0 of 107,400 differ). At the worst condition, every block at the sf corner and 85 °C (comparator σ<sub>n</sub> = 0.732 mV and σ<sub>os</sub> = 4.85 mV, interpolated from the recorded 27 and 125 °C points; the SRAM cell law of the sf corner), 40 cells differ (expected 40.1), close to t = 45 as predicted. The key is recovered and every check passes in this frame, but the probability that a power-up at 85 °C yields a wrong key is 1.3 × 10<sup>−1</sup>: with a 25 °C enrolment and t = 45 the sf corner does not meet the 10<sup>−6</sup> target, as study F finds for the population (the 99th-percentile simulated sf chip needs t = 55 with this enrolment, and t = 16 with the enrolment at −40 and 85 °C). In both frames the bit stream is balanced (fraction of ones 0.500), no run of equal bits exceeds 3 clocks, and the integrators never clip. In the nominal frame (Fig. 38) the server's reading follows the input to within 0.018 % of full scale rms. In Fig. 39, the nominal and worst spectra coincide, and only the frame with the assumed impairments departs from them. The bit-stream spectrum (Fig. 39(a)) has the two regions predicted (below 2.4 kHz the main lobe of the window around DC dominates). Between 2 and 8 kHz the integrator's thermal noise sets a flat floor at −126.8 dBFS per bin at both conditions; above it, the spectrum rises at 40 dB per decade, as the second-order NTF predicts, and the two conditions overlap to within the variance of the estimate. Their in-band noise is −66.5 dBFS at both, so **the shaped quantisation noise, not the circuit noise, sets the SNDR**. Above about 1 MHz the spectrum levels off near −35 dBFS per bin, as $|\mathrm{NTF}|^2$ approaches its maximum at $f_s/2$, and its strongest component lies at 3.82 MHz (−11.1 dBFS per bin), next to the predicted turning point of the limit-cycle tone, $(1-A)\,f_s/2$ = 3.75 MHz; 96 % of the bit-stream power lies above 1 MHz, far outside the 100 kHz band. The decoded output (Fig. 39(b), Welch average of 1,024-point segments, 195 Hz bins) shows the 20.02 kHz tone at −12.1 dBFS. Its floor is not flat, as predicted: from 25–35 kHz to 65–75 kHz it rises from −107.6 to −90.1 dBFS per bin, by 17.5 dB against the 14.7 dB of noise rising at 40 dB per decade (the remainder is shaped noise folded into the band by the decimation), and it falls steeply above 80 kHz, where the receiver's filters attenuate by 6.7 dB at 80 kHz, 42.8 dB at 90 kHz and 59.5 dB at 100 kHz. The SNDR, with the noise integrated from 391 Hz to 100 kHz, is 60.0 dB at the nominal and 60.1 dB at the worst condition; integrated only to the 80 kHz edge of the compensation filter, the nominal SNDR is 60.3 dB, so the attenuated noise between 80 and 100 kHz costs 0.3 dB. Even without circuit distortion, the decoded output contains a third harmonic at −76.3 dBc (nominal): the quantisation error of a 1-bit second-order loop is correlated with its input, and the dither does not remove this correlation completely.

With the assumed impairments, the low-frequency floor rises to −107.4 dBFS per bin, 19.4 dB above the nominal. The jitter alone raises it to −108.2 dBFS per bin (+18.6 dB, against about 18 dB predicted), and the 1/f noise alone to −117.1 dBFS per bin (+9.7 dB, against about 10 dB); the floor of the impaired frame is therefore set by the clock jitter, which masks the 1/f noise. The distortion appears as a third harmonic at −66.1 dBc in the impaired frame and −65.3 dBc alone, above the applied −70 dBc because it adds to the loop's own −76 dBc harmonic; the second harmonic, −79.4 dBc, stays near the in-band noise. The in-band noise is unchanged (−66.8 dBFS against −66.5 dBFS), and the SNDR falls from 60.0 to 59.5 dB. Single nominal frames spread with σ = 0.3 dB (range 60.2 to 61.1 dB over eight realisations), so the jitter-only (60.9 dB) and 1/f-only (60.3 dB) frames do not differ measurably from the nominal; the distortion-only frame (59.4 dB) is below the range. The legend of Fig. 39(a) gives such single-frame values: the 60.0 dB of the nominal frame and the 60.3–60.4 dB of study A, which simulates one realisation per PVT condition with other seeds and no offset, differ by about this spread, not by a circuit effect.

**Interpretation (spectrum).** The clean floor of the reference frames is the white thermal noise of the integrator, the only unshaped noise source in the reference model; it is not a sign that noise is missing, but it is an idealisation. The rising floor of the decoded output is the operating principle of the converter, not a defect of the decoding: a delta-sigma modulator moves its quantisation noise towards high frequencies instead of removing it, the receiver's filters remove what lies above the band, and the noise that remains inside the band keeps the 40 dB-per-decade slope; the SNDR integrates it over the whole band. Decryption plays no part in it, since the decrypted bits equal the modulator bits. The tone near 3.8 MHz is the 1-bit loop's limit cycle; it lies almost 40 times above the band edge and does not reach the decoded output. Of the assumed impairments, the clock jitter of the continuous-time DAC dominates the floor and the input-stage distortion dominates the SNDR penalty, while neither raises the in-band noise, which the shaped quantisation noise sets. **The 60 dB of the reference model is therefore an upper bound for a chip**, and the margin found by the studies below holds for impairments of this size; a specification of the clock jitter and of the input-stage linearity belongs in the design of the chip.

**Interpretation.** **In the behavioural model, the complete link operates end to end at both conditions**: in each of the two frames the authenticated link delivers every bit, and the accuracy does not change between the nominal and the worst corner, because the loop shapes the comparator noise together with the quantisation error. The key generator tolerates the nominal read with a margin of 32 cells; at the sf corner and 85 °C the margin shrinks to 5 cells and the key fails in about one power-up in eight, which is why study F sizes the key generator per corner and enrols at −40 and 85 °C. This frame is the reference for the studies that follow, each of which changes one circuit quantity at a time to find how far it can move before an accuracy, power or security metric changes.

### A. Accuracy: comparator noise and offset

**Goal.** Find how much the comparator's noise and offset degrade the accuracy of the sensor at the 45 PVT conditions, and how large each would have to become before the accuracy is lost.

**Theory.** In model units, the second-order modulator of Section V-C is

$$x_1[k] = x_1[k-1] + g_1\big(u[k] - v[k-1]\big),\qquad x_2[k] = x_2[k-1] + g_2\big(x_1[k] - v[k-1]\big),\qquad v[k] = \operatorname{sgn}\big(x_2[k] + o + n[k]\big),$$

where $u[k]$ is the input (full scale ±1), $x_1$ and $x_2$ are the two integrators' outputs, $v[k] = \pm 1$ is the decision fed back, $g_1 = g_2 = g = 1/2$ are the integrator coefficients (capacitor ratios), $o$ is the comparator's offset and $n[k] \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_n^2)$ its noise, both referred to $V_{DD}/4$. Dither is omitted for clarity.

* *Noise is shaped like quantisation error, until it lowers the quantiser's gain.* The 1-bit quantiser is a relay. If its input $q = x_2 + n$ is Gaussian with standard deviation $\sigma_q$, the relay behaves on average like a gain plus an uncorrelated error (its stochastic describing function):
  $$v = k\,q + e,\qquad k = \sqrt{2/\pi}\,/\,\sigma_q,\qquad \sigma_e^2 = 1 - 2/\pi,\qquad \sigma_q^2 = \sigma_{x_2}^2 + \sigma_n^2 ,$$
  with $k$ the relay's gain, $e$ its error of variance $\sigma_e^2$, and $\sigma_{x_2}$ the standard deviation of $x_2$. The loop with gain $k$ gives $V(z) = \mathrm{STF}(z)\,U(z) + \mathrm{NTF}(z)\,\big(E(z) + k\,N(z)\big)$, where STF and NTF are the signal and noise transfer functions, $\mathrm{NTF}(z) = (1 - z^{-1})^2 / D(z)$ and $D(z) = (1 - z^{-1})^2 + k g z^{-1}\,(1 + g - z^{-1})$. The comparator noise therefore enters where the quantisation error does and is shaped by the same NTF, which suppresses it by 40 dB per decade towards low frequencies. Noise also widens $\sigma_q$ and so lowers $k$, which weakens the shaping. The in-band noise power is
  $$P_{\text{in}} = \big(\sigma_e^2 + k^2\sigma_n^2\big)\,\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{\text{band}} \big|\mathrm{NTF}(e^{j\omega})\big|^2\,d\omega ,$$
  with ω the normalised angular frequency and the band that of the receiver. Since $\sigma_{x_2}$ follows from the same linear loop, $k$ is solved self-consistently. The prediction uses no simulated or fitted value: only $g$, the input amplitude and the receiver's band. *Assumptions:* the quantiser's input is Gaussian and its error is uncorrelated with the input. Both hold while the loop's own signal dominates the quantiser's input, so the theory should hold for small and moderate noise and lose accuracy once σ<sub>n</sub> dominates σ<sub>q</sub>. *Prediction:* the SNDR does not change until σ<sub>n</sub> reaches a sizeable fraction of the swing of $x_2$, so its −3 dB point should lie near 100 mV, two orders of magnitude above the PVT values (the next cell evaluates it).
* *An offset is a change of initial state.* Substituting $\tilde{x}_2 = x_2 + o$ turns the loop with offset $o$ into the offset-free loop started from $\tilde{x}_2[0] = o$. Without dither, noise and clipping the two produce **identical bits**. The bit density of a stable loop converges to its input whatever its initial state, so the offset causes **no DC error**. The identity holds while the integrator stays inside its range $x_{\lim} = 2.5$ (the clipping level of the model): $|o| < x_{\lim} - \max|\tilde{x}_2|$, the integrator range, with $\max|\tilde{x}_2|$ the peak swing of the offset-free loop. Beyond it the second integrator clips and the reading is lost. *Prediction:* the bits are identical bit for bit; the DC error stays at the noise floor up to the integrator range. The limit is conservative: it adds the peak swing in either direction to the offset, and it treats any contact with the rail as failure, although a brief clip need not lose the reading.

**Setup.** Behavioural model with the testbench settings.

* *Noise at PVT:* each of the 45 conditions with its own σ<sub>n</sub>, converted to model units at its own supply; no offset in these runs (see the limits of the map); one noise seed each.
* *Noise sweep:* σ<sub>n</sub> from 0.1 mV to 1 V (11 points) at tt, 27 °C, 1.8 V, three noise seeds per point. The theory curve uses 120 points over the same range.
* *Offset identity:* the bare loop on the first 20,000 clocks of the sine, for o = 0.01, 0.3 and −1 model units.
* *DC error:* the constant attack input for 26,850 clocks, with offsets of 1 mV to 3 V (15 points), each of both signs; the error is the larger change of the decoded reading, in ppm of full scale (drawn at 10<sup>−3</sup> ppm when smaller). The reading counts as lost above 0.1 % of full scale. The same error is computed for an offset of 3× the largest PVT σ<sub>os</sub>.

> **Next cell.** 1. Simulates the SNDR at the 45 PVT conditions and over the noise sweep. 2. Evaluates the describing-function theory over the sweep and finds its −3 dB point and its largest difference from the simulation below 300 mV. 3. Checks the offset identity bit for bit on the bare loop. 4. Sweeps the offset, measures the DC error of the decoded reading, and compares the failure point with the integrator range. 5. Prints the card and draws Fig. 40.


```python
#@title Fig.: study A, accuracy
# Study A: accuracy. The comparator's noise and offset carried to the modulator SNDR and the DC error, at the 45 PVT
# conditions and swept far beyond them, against the theory: the relay's describing function for the noise, the
# state-shift identity for the offset
t0 = time.time()
sndr_sweep = np.array([np.mean([sndr_at(Qn(x), k) for k in range(3)]) for x in SN_SWEEP])
sndr_pvt = np.array([sndr_at(Qn(r["sigma_n"], r["vdd"])) for r in PVT["cmp"]])
# theory, with no fitted parameter: the 1-bit quantiser as a relay with a Gaussian input q = x2 + n has the gain
# k = sqrt(2/pi)/sigma_q and an error of variance 1 - 2/pi; the loop at that gain shapes both the error and k n by its
# NTF, and sigma_x2 follows from the same loop (solved self-consistently); the in-band integral covers the receiver's band
w_ = np.linspace(1e-6, np.pi, 20001); z_ = np.exp(-1j * w_); band_ = w_ <= 0.8 * np.pi / OSR   # FIR flat to 0.4 f_out
def df_sndr(sn_u, g=0.5, n_it=60):
    k, se2 = 2.0, 1 - 2 / np.pi
    for _ in range(n_it):
        Dz = (1 - z_) ** 2 + k * g * z_ * (g + 1 - z_)                # loop denominator at relay gain k
        hx = ((1 - z_) ** 2 / Dz - 1) / k                            # x2 per unit of (error + k n)
        sx2 = (se2 + k ** 2 * sn_u ** 2) * np.mean(np.abs(hx) ** 2) + amp_in ** 2 / 2 / k ** 2
        k = 0.5 * k + 0.5 * np.sqrt(2 / np.pi) / np.sqrt(sx2 + sn_u ** 2)
    Dz = (1 - z_) ** 2 + k * g * z_ * (g + 1 - z_)
    p_in = (se2 + k ** 2 * sn_u ** 2) * np.mean(np.where(band_, np.abs((1 - z_) ** 2 / Dz) ** 2, 0.0))
    return 10 * np.log10(amp_in ** 2 / 2 / p_in)
sn_th = np.logspace(-4, 0, 120)
sndr_th = np.array([df_sndr(x / VU(1.8)) for x in sn_th])
th_3db = crossing(sn_th, sndr_th, sndr_th[0] - 3)
# where the theory holds: the largest |theory - simulation| while the comparator noise stays below SN_DF; above it the
# quantiser input is noise-dominated and the linearised relay overestimates the SNDR
SN_DF = 0.3                                                                       # V
th_at = np.interp(np.log(SN_SWEEP), np.log(sn_th), sndr_th)
th_dmax = float(np.abs(th_at - sndr_sweep)[SN_SWEEP <= SN_DF].max()); th_dtop = float(th_at[-1] - sndr_sweep[-1])
# the offset identity, bit for bit: offset o  ==  offset-free loop started from x2[0] = o
u_id = u_sine[:20000]
ident = all(np.array_equal(bare_loop(u_id, offset=o), bare_loop(u_id, x2_0=o)) for o in (0.01, 0.3, -1.0))
# DC error against the offset; the range in which the loop absorbs it: |o| < x_lim - max|x2| (offset-free swing)
u_short = u_dc[:N_DSM // 4]
rd = dsm2(u_short, P_sys); dc_ref = decode(rd["D"])[50:].mean()
o_abs = (P_sys["xlim"] - np.abs(rd["X2"]).max()) * VU(1.8)
OS_DC = np.array([1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2, 3e-2, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.2, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0])
dc_err = np.array([max(abs(decode(dsm2(u_short, P_sys, offset=s * o / VU(1.8))["D"])[50:].mean() - dc_ref) for s in (-1, 1))
                   for o in OS_DC])
dc_3s = max(abs(decode(dsm2(u_short, P_sys, offset=s * 3 * os_max / VU(1.8))["D"])[50:].mean() - dc_ref) for s in (-1, 1))
SYS = dict(sndr_pvt=(sndr_pvt.min(), sndr_pvt.max()), sndr_3db=crossing(SN_SWEEP, sndr_sweep, sndr_sweep[0] - 3), dc_err=dc_3s,
           th_3db=th_3db, th_0=float(sndr_th[0]), o_abs=o_abs, o_fail=float(OS_DC[np.argmax(dc_err > 1e-3)]) if (dc_err > 1e-3).any() else None)
card("Study A, accuracy: comparator noise and offset",
     [("modulator SNDR at the 45 PVT conditions", f"<b>{SYS['sndr_pvt'][0]:.1f}–{SYS['sndr_pvt'][1]:.1f} dB</b>"),
      ("noise for −3 dB: simulation", f"σ<sub>n</sub> ≈ <b>{1e3 * SYS['sndr_3db']:.0f} mV</b>, {SYS['sndr_3db'] / sn_max:.0f}× the largest PVT value"),
      ("theory: the relay's describing function, no fitted parameter", f"SNDR {SYS['th_0']:.1f} dB without noise (simulation "
       f"{sndr_sweep[0]:.1f} dB); −3 dB at σ<sub>n</sub> ≈ {1e3 * th_3db:.0f} mV (simulation {1e3 * SYS['sndr_3db']:.0f} mV)"),
      ("theory − simulation", f"largest |difference| <b>{th_dmax:.1f} dB</b> for σ<sub>n</sub> ≤ {1e3 * SN_DF:.0f} mV; at "
       f"σ<sub>n</sub> = {1e3 * SN_SWEEP[-1]:.0f} mV the theory overestimates the SNDR by {th_dtop:.0f} dB (noise-dominated quantiser)"),
      ("offset = initial-state shift (no dither, noise, clipping)", f"bits identical for o = 0.01, 0.3, −1: <b>{ident}</b>"),
      ("DC error of the decoded reading with a 3σ PVT offset", f"{1e6 * dc_3s:.2f} ppm of full scale: absorbed by the loop"),
      ("integrator range: offset the loop absorbs, theory |o| &lt; x<sub>lim</sub> − max|x<sub>2</sub>|",
       f"{1e3 * o_abs:.0f} mV; simulation: DC error > 0.1 % from {1e3 * SYS['o_fail']:.0f} mV, so the theory's limit is "
       f"conservative by {SYS['o_fail'] / o_abs:.1f}×" if SYS["o_fail"] else f"{1e3 * o_abs:.0f} mV"),
      ("run time", f"{time.time() - t0:.0f} s")], tone="ok")

tcol, vmark = {-40.0: COL["ok"], 27.0: COL["aqua"], 125.0: COL["bad"]}, {1.62: "v", 1.8: "o", 1.98: "^"}
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(W2, 3.2))
ax = axs[0]
ax.axvspan(1e3 * min(r["sigma_n"] for r in PVT["cmp"]), 1e3 * sn_max, color=COL["faint"], alpha=0.3, lw=0, label="PVT range")
ax.semilogx(1e3 * SN_SWEEP, sndr_sweep, "-", color=COL["ink"], lw=1.5, label="simulation (tt, 27 °C, 1.8 V)")
ax.semilogx(1e3 * sn_th, sndr_th, "--", color=COL["key"], lw=1.2, label="theory: describing function")
for r, y in zip(PVT["cmp"], sndr_pvt):
    ax.plot(1e3 * r["sigma_n"], y, vmark[r["vdd"]], color=tcol[r["temp"]], ms=4, mec=COL["ink"], mew=0.3)
y3 = sndr_sweep[0] - 3                                                   # the -3 dB point of the simulation
ax.plot(1e3 * SYS["sndr_3db"], y3, "o", ms=6, mfc="none", mec=COL["ink"], mew=1.0)
ax.annotate(f"−3 dB at {1e3 * SYS['sndr_3db']:.0f} mV\n({SYS['sndr_3db'] / sn_max:.0f}× the PVT maximum)", (1e3 * SYS["sndr_3db"], y3),
            xytext=(-8, -16), textcoords="offset points", ha="right", va="top", fontsize=7.5, color=COL["ink"],
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", lw=0.6, color=COL["ink"]))
ax.annotate(f"45 PVT conditions: {SYS['sndr_pvt'][0]:.1f}–{SYS['sndr_pvt'][1]:.1f} dB", (1e3 * sn_max, SYS["sndr_pvt"][1]),
            xytext=(1e3 * sn_max * 2.0, sndr_sweep[0] + 2.4), ha="left", va="center", fontsize=7.5, color=COL["ink"],
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", lw=0.6, color=COL["ink"]))
leg = ax.legend(fontsize=6.5, loc="lower left")
mk = lambda **kw: Line2D([], [], ls="", ms=4, mec=COL["ink"], **kw)
pv, pl = [], []
for (t, c), (v, m) in zip(tcol.items(), vmark.items()):                     # columns: one temperature over one supply
    pv += [mk(marker="o", color=c, mew=0.3), mk(marker=m, color="white", mew=0.6)]
    pl += [f"{t:.0f} °C".replace("-", "−"), f"{v:.2f} V"]
ax.legend(pv, pl, fontsize=6.5, loc="lower left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 0.25), ncol=3, handlelength=1.0, columnspacing=0.9,
          title="PVT markers: colour = temperature, shape = supply", title_fontsize=6.5)
ax.add_artist(leg)
ax.set_ylim(max(0, sndr_sweep.min() - 18), sndr_sweep.max() + 5)
ax.set_xlabel(r"Comparator noise $\sigma_\mathrm{n}$ (mV)"); ax.set_ylabel("Modulator SNDR (dB)")
panel(ax, "a", "SNDR vs comparator noise")
ax = axs[1]
ax.axvspan(1e3 * min(r["sigma_os"] for r in PVT["cmp"]), 1e3 * os_max, color=COL["faint"], alpha=0.3, lw=0, label=r"PVT $\sigma_\mathrm{os}$")
ax.axvspan(1e3 * o_abs, 1e3 * OS_DC[-1], color=COL["bad"], alpha=0.10, lw=0, label="beyond the integrator range (theory)")
ax.loglog(1e3 * OS_DC, np.maximum(1e6 * dc_err, 1e-3), "o-", color=COL["ink"], ms=3.5, lw=1.4, label="simulation")
ax.axhline(1e3, color=COL["faint"], lw=0.8, ls=":")                    # 0.1 % of full scale: the reading counts as lost
ax.text(1.1, 1.6e3, "0.1 % FS: reading lost", fontsize=7.5, color=COL["faint"], va="bottom")
ax.plot(3e3 * os_max, max(1e6 * dc_3s, 1e-3), "D", ms=5, color=COL["ok"], mec=COL["ink"], mew=0.4)
ax.annotate(f"3× the largest PVT $\\sigma_\\mathrm{{os}}$:\n{1e6 * dc_3s:.2f} ppm", (3e3 * os_max, max(1e6 * dc_3s, 1e-3)), xytext=(0, -22),
            textcoords="offset points", ha="center", va="top", fontsize=7.5, color=COL["ok"],
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", lw=0.6, color=COL["ok"]))
if SYS["o_fail"]:
    ax.annotate(f"lost from {SYS['o_fail']:.1f} V", (1e3 * SYS["o_fail"], 1e6 * dc_err[np.argmax(dc_err > 1e-3)]), xytext=(-10, -6),
                textcoords="offset points", ha="right", va="top", fontsize=7.5, color=COL["bad"])
ax.set_ylim(1e-3 / 3, 3e8)
ax.set_xlabel("Comparator offset $|o|$ (mV)"); ax.set_ylabel("DC error of the reading (ppm FS)"); ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper left")
panel(ax, "b", "DC error vs comparator offset")
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```
