**Result.** In SKY130 at 10 MHz (Table XV), all gate-level checks of the six simulations pass. As written for one bit per clock, this work's SKY130 RTL of the S-DSM draws 43 µW, that of Trivium 223 µW and the proposal's full block 415 µW, the clock tree taking 30–32 % of each. In their low-power forms, the S-DSM draws 18.1 µW (2.4× less), Trivium 32.3 µW (6.9× less) and the proposal **64.3 µW (6.5× less)**; routed, with its extracted wires, the low-power proposal draws 73.4 µW (Subsection C). The ratio of the proposal to the S-DSM falls from 9.7× to **3.6×**, while the ratio to Trivium stays at 1.9–2.0×. By part (Table XVI), the clock tree draws 20.5 µW (32 %) of the low-power proposal, the Grain-128a state 14.2 µW (22 %), the MAC 11.6 µW (18 %) and the capture of the message bits for the MAC, which still runs at 10 MHz, 7.4 µW (12 %); the cipher control and counters, the dither bit counter, the dither LFSRs and the output multiplexers draw 9.7 µW together, and the gated key, nonce and counter registers draw less than 0.05 µW. Trivium's 223 µW in SKY130 is close to the 220 µW measured in 65 nm in [1], whereas the S-DSM's 43 µW is about 1.8× the 24 µW measured.

**Interpretation.** **The parallel update and clock gating remove most of the proposal's power, but not its distance from the S-DSM.** The reduction is largest where the state is large: Trivium and the proposal clock 300 and 586 flip-flops at 10 MHz when written for one bit per clock, and the low-power form clocks their state at 625 kHz and their idle registers not at all. The S-DSM gains only 2.4×, because its state is small: the output counter, the output multiplexers and the clock trunk that the low-power form adds or keeps at 10 MHz are a large part of what remains, and the clock tree's share rises from 32 to 48 %. As predicted, what remains of the proposal is what must run at 10 MHz (clock tree, message capture, counters: about 56 % of the block) and its state, 256 bits of Grain-128a and 64 of MAC against the S-DSM's 16 bits of LFSR state per register. The remaining factor of 3.6 is the cost of a 128-bit cipher with authentication over a 16-bit LFSR in the same flow; it is a ratio of two designs in the same flow and, to first order, does not depend on the process. The simulation without gate delays counts no glitches, so the gate-level values are lower bounds on the dynamic power in that respect; the deeper logic of the low-power forms makes this bound looser than for the forms written for one bit per clock.

#### Clock gating alone, on the block written for one bit per clock

**Goal.** Measure how much of the power of the block written for one bit per clock clock gating alone removes, with the gating inserted automatically by Yosys and no other change; the low-power form of Subsections A and D adds the parallel state update to it. Subsection C and Table XV show that most of the power is drawn by the flip-flops and the clock tree on every cycle, whether the flip-flops change or not. Many of the block's flip-flops hold their value for a whole frame: the 128-bit key, the 32-bit session nonce, the 31-bit chip nonce and the 32-bit frame counter change only when they are loaded or, for the counter, once per frame. The block of Subsections B and C clocks them on every cycle.

**Theory.** A flip-flop with an enable is built as a flip-flop whose input is a multiplexer that selects either the new value or its own output; its clock pin and the clock tree that drives it switch on every cycle. An integrated clock-gating (ICG) cell instead passes the clock to a group of flip-flops only in the cycles in which their enable is set; it contains a latch, so that the gated clock has no glitches. In the cycles in which the enable is off, the gated flip-flops and the branch of the clock tree behind the ICG cell draw no dynamic power, and the multiplexers are no longer needed. If $N_g$ of the $N$ flip-flops are gated and their enable is almost never set while a frame is encrypted, the prediction is that the flip-flop power and the clock-tree power fall roughly in the ratio $N_g/N$, less the power of the ICG cells, which still see every clock edge.

**Setup.**

* *Design:* the RTL of Subsection B, unchanged; Yosys inserts the clock gating during synthesis (`clockgate`): every group of at least four flip-flops that share a clock enable gets one `sky130_fd_sc_hd__dlclkp_1` ICG cell, and its flip-flops lose their enable. The rest of the synthesis script is that of Subsection B.
* *Verification:* the gated netlist is simulated with Icarus Verilog on both test jobs of the proposal from Subsection B (generator seeded with 2027), with the jobs' own checks, because the AIGER simulator of Subsection B handles a single clock only.
* *Implementation and power:* the gated and, for a like-for-like reference, the ungated netlist go through the complete flow of Subsection C: place and route, Magic DRC, OpenRCX extraction, timing at the three corners, LVS, gate-level simulation of the routed netlist on the 400-bit frame of Subsection C, and power with the extracted wires (tt, 25 °C, 1.8 V, 10 MHz). The clock-tree synthesis builds the tree through the ICG cells.
* *Recorded run:* the study requires two routings, about 6–9 minutes on two cores, so it is shown by default from its recorded run (`dev/rtl/clock_gating.json`, written by `dev/rtl/record_signoff.py` with the same code); setting `CLOCK_GATING_LIVE = True` in the next cell runs it in the session.
* *Metrics:* the number of ICG cells and gated flip-flops, the checks passed, the sign-off results of the gated block, its area and its power per group, against the ungated block.

**Result.** In the recorded run (Table XVII), Yosys inserts 4 clock-gating cells, one each for the key register (128 flip-flops), the session nonce (32), the chip nonce (31) and the frame counter (32): 223 of the 586 flip-flops are gated. The other 363 flip-flops, those of Grain-128a, its MAC and the two dither LFSRs, have no enable: they are updated in every cycle and keep the ungated clock. The gated netlist passes all 11 checks of both test jobs before layout and all 5 checks after routing. The gated block is clean as well: 0 routing DRC, 0 antenna and 0 Magic DRC violations, LVS match, setup slack +91.1 ns at ss and hold slack +0.20 ns at ff. Synthesis gives 17,505.5 µm² against 19,667.6 µm², 11 % less, because the 223 enable flip-flops become plain flip-flops. With the extracted wires, the power falls from 433 to **291 µW (33 % less)**: the flip-flops from 268 to 168 µW and the clock tree from 149 to 105 µW, while the logic rises from 17 to 18 µW. The prediction from the fraction of gated flip-flops, 223/586 = 38 % of the flip-flop and clock-tree power, or about 159 µW, compares with the 144 µW saved in these two groups, 91 % of it; the difference is the power of the four clock-gating cells and of the clock tree up to them, which still switch on every cycle.

**Interpretation.** **Clock gating removes a third of the block's power**, because more than a third of its flip-flops hold their value for the whole frame; it also saves area, and the timing slacks change by less than 0.2 ns. Clock gating alone leaves the 363 flip-flops of Grain-128a, its MAC and the dither LFSRs clocked at 10 MHz, because they change in every cycle; only the parallel state update of the low-power form, which lets them change once every 16 cycles, removes that part (Subsection D).

### E. A figure of merit across processes, and transmitted bits

**Goal.** Compare the security blocks of this work, simulated in SKY130, with the blocks measured in [1] in 65 nm and with other published security engines, fairly and without scaling any number from one process to another; and count the bits each design sends for the same information at the oversampling ratio at which this notebook's accuracy results hold, against the conventional design of [1] and against an information-equivalent conventional design.

**Theory: what the process changes, and what it does not.** Every power in Subsections C and D is a SKY130 number; the blocks of [1] are 65 nm numbers. The security blocks are digital, so the process acts on them through the dynamic power of the standard cells, $P = \alpha\,C\,V_{DD}^2\,f$:

| Parameter | SKY130, this work | 65 nm chip of [1] | Ratio, SKY130 / 65 nm |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Minimum gate length $L_{\min}$ | 150 nm (1.8 V devices) | 65 nm | 2.3 |
| Nominal supply $V_{\text{nom}}$ | 1.8 V | 1.2 V | $V^2$: 2.25 |
| $L_{\min} V_{\text{nom}}^2$ (gate capacitance ∝ $L_{\min}$, switching energy ∝ $C V^2$) | 486 nm·V² | 93.6 nm·V² | 5.2 |
| Clock $f$ | 10 MHz | 10 MHz | 1 |

A gate in SKY130 therefore switches about 5.2× the energy of a gate in the 65 nm process of [1], to first order: SKY130 is the older, larger and higher-voltage process, and it penalises every design built in it equally. What the process does not change is the ratio between two designs built in the same flow: $C$, $V_{DD}$ and $f$ are common to both and cancel. **The ratios of Table XV are therefore independent of the process to first order.**

**Theory: the figure of merit.** No power is scaled from one process to the other, and no modelled quantity enters the comparison. Each design keeps its own number, measured (published works) or simulated at gate level (this work's designed blocks), and the process enters only through a figure of merit built from published process facts,

$$\text{FOM} = \frac{E_{\text{bit}}}{L_{\min}\, V_{\text{nom}}^2\; S\; K}, \qquad E_{\text{bit}} = \frac{P}{f_{\text{bit}}},$$

in aJ/(nm·V²), lower is better, with three factors in the denominator, each chosen so that the comparison is fair:

* $L_{\min} V_{\text{nom}}^2$, the minimum gate length and the **nominal** supply of the process, which set the switching energy of its gates to first order. The nominal supply, not the operating supply, is used, so that a design operated below its nominal supply, such as a near-threshold engine, keeps the credit for that design choice, while the gate length and the nominal supply, which the designer of a block does not choose, are removed.
* $S$, the security level in bits: the smaller of the key length and $\log_2$ of the cost of the best published attack. The S-DSM has a 16-bit key, $S$ = 16; Trivium an 80-bit key, $S$ = 80; Grain-128a a 128-bit key and a fast correlation attack of $2^{113.8}$ data [18], $S$ = 113.8; AES-128 the biclique attack, $S$ = 126.1. The credit is linear in $S$, which is conservative: the attacker's work grows exponentially with $S$.
* $K$, the number of security properties provided, of four: confidentiality, authentication (integrity), freshness (replay protection), and a key that is not held in non-volatile memory, the rows of the comparison table of Section XIV. The S-DSM and Trivium provide confidentiality, $K$ = 1; the DTLS engine of [9] confidentiality, authentication and freshness, $K$ = 3; the proposal all four, $K$ = 4.

The FOM removes the first-order effect of the process and credits what the energy buys. It does not remove differences in what a measured block contains beyond its logic (test and output interfaces, key loading, a supply that feeds more than the block), and it credits security strength and properties, not the attacks of Section IX that a design withstands. The process-normalised energy per bit, $E_{\text{bit}}/(L_{\min} V_{\text{nom}}^2)$, without $S$ and $K$, is reported beside it. A design whose power is estimated rather than measured or simulated, such as the information-equivalent baseline below, receives no FOM.

*Setup.* $E_{\text{bit}}$ is the power over the keystream rate, one bit per 10 MHz clock in every design: [1]'s measured 24 µW (S-DSM) and 220 µW (Trivium) at 1.2 V; the DTLS engine's 0.89 nJ per byte [9]; this work's gate-level SKY130 powers of Table XV at 1.8 V.

*Share of the chip's power.* The security block's share of the chip's total power, with each block's own power and none scaled, $P_{\text{sec}}/(P_{\text{off}} + P_{\text{sec}})$, with $P_{\text{off}}$ = 321 + 271 + 250 + 510 = 1,352 µW (front end, TIA, S-to-D buffer and ΔΣ modulator, Fig. 4(a) of [1]). Subsection F also gives the overhead relative to the chip with security off, $P_{\text{sec}}/P_{\text{off}}$, the measure of [1].

*Bits sent for the same information.* No radio is designed in this work, so no radio energy is claimed. What the architecture sets, independently of any radio, is the number of bits the sensor must transmit for the same information, here per reading (Nyquist sample). Any energy consequence depends on a radio, which is not part of this work: only for a radio whose energy per transmitted bit is the same for every design would the transmission energies of two designs be in the ratio of their bits. Three kinds of design are compared:

* *Modulator-level* (the S-DSM and the proposal): every modulator bit is sent, OSR bits per reading, at OSR = 50, the ratio of every accuracy result of this notebook (Section VIII). The proposal adds the 32-bit counter, the 32-bit chip nonce and the 32-bit MAC tag sent in clear with every frame of 107,400 modulator clocks, $96\cdot\text{OSR}/107{,}400 \approx 0.045$ bits per reading.
* *The conventional design of [1]*: a decimating ADC with Trivium sends 16-bit words at SR/NR = 4.5 to 5 times the Nyquist rate (the two OSR-50 rows of Fig. 4(b) of [1]), 72 to 80 bits per reading.
* *An information-equivalent conventional design*: the receiver's third-order CIC decimator (Section V) is moved onto the sensor, and Grain-128a with its MAC encrypts and authenticates 16-bit words, the word length of [1], sent at the Nyquist rate, with the same frame fields. A shorter word matched to the sensor's resolution would rest on the SNDR of the behavioural model, which is not used in any comparison.

*Prediction.* The proposal sends 50 bits per reading, like the S-DSM, against 72–80 for [1]'s conventional design, 1.4–1.6× fewer, not the 2.7× of [1]'s OSR-30 comparison; the information-equivalent design sends about 16 and should send about 3× **fewer** bits than any modulator-level scheme, because a 1-bit modulator at OSR 50 sends 50 bits per Nyquist sample where one 16-bit word suffices.

**Setup.** A calculation on the gate-level results of Subsection D and on published values, plus one block in RTL: the CIC decimator (decimation by 50, three 19-bit integrators at 10 MHz and three combs at the output rate), simulated with Icarus Verilog on a 20,000-bit modulator-like stream and compared output for output with the model's CIC, then synthesised with Yosys on `sky130_fd_sc_hd`. Its power is not simulated: it is estimated from its area at the SKY130 gate-level power per GE of Grain-128a + MAC, also a datapath clocked at 10 MHz, and is therefore listed but not used in the FOM; its 31-tap compensation filter, which runs at the output rate (200 kS/s), is not included. Every design uses its own power, none scaled: the S-DSM and Trivium of [1] their measured powers (24 and 220 µW), this work's designs their SKY130 gate-level powers. The 32-bit delay line of Subsection A is not included. Fig. 58 plots the areas of Subsection B, the FOM and the bits sent per reading. Metrics, as the columns of Table XVIII: area (GE), source, process, power, energy per bit, $E_{\text{bit}}/(L_{\min} V_{\text{nom}}^2)$, S, K, the FOM and the bits sent per reading at OSR 50; the card adds the measured blocks of [1] against their RTL in this flow, the advantage over [1]'s conventional design, the decimator's check and area, and the bits per reading at the OSR 30 of [1]'s headline comparison.

> **Next cell.** 1. Reads the NAND2 input capacitance from the Liberty file and computes the FOM of every design from its own power. 2. Writes the CIC decimator of the information-equivalent baseline in Verilog, checks it against the model's CIC with Icarus Verilog and synthesises it. 3. Computes the bits sent per reading for the same information at OSR 50 for every design and both baselines. 4. Prints the cost table and the card. 5. Plots the area, the FOM and the transmitted bits of each design.


```python
#@title Fig.: area, power and energy
# Cost of each security block, without scaling any number: [1]'s two blocks keep their measured 65 nm, 1.2 V powers, this
# work's blocks their simulated SKY130 (150 nm, 1.8 V) gate-level powers. The processes and the functions enter only through a
# figure of merit built from published process facts and reported results, with no modelled quantity in it:
#   FOM = E_bit / (L_min V_nom^2 S K), in aJ/(nm V^2), lower is better;
#   E_bit = P / f_bit, the energy per encrypted bit as measured (published works) or simulated at gate level (this work);
#   L_min V_nom^2: minimum gate length and NOMINAL supply of the process (gate capacitance scales with L_min, switching energy
#            with C V^2); the nominal, not the operating, supply, so that a design run below its nominal supply keeps the credit;
#   S = security level in bits: the smaller of the key length and log2 of the cost of the best published attack
#            (S-DSM 16, Trivium 80, Grain-128a 113.8 [18], AES-128 126.1); linear credit is conservative;
#   K = security properties provided, of four: confidentiality, authentication (integrity), freshness (replay
#            protection), no key in non-volatile memory (the rows of the comparison table of Section XIV).
D = RTL["designs"]
ge = {k: SYN[k]["ge"] for k in D}                # low-power designs: the netlist with clock-gating cells
base_uw = sum(PAPER_FIG4A_UW[k] for k in ("fe", "tia", "s2d", "dsm"))
F_BIT = 10e6                                     # one keystream bit per 10 MHz clock in every design
PROC = {"65": dict(L=65, V=1.2), "sky130": dict(L=150, V=1.8)}       # L_min (nm), nominal V_DD (V)
SEC_BITS = {"sdsm": 16, "trivium": 80, "proposal": 113.8, "aes": 126.1}
SEC_PROPS = {"sdsm": 1, "trivium": 1, "proposal": 4}                 # of confidentiality, authentication, freshness, no NVM key
def n_gate(p_uw, proc):                          # E_bit / (L_min V_nom^2), aJ / (b nm V^2)
    return p_uw * 1e-6 / F_BIT * 1e18 / (PROC[proc]["L"] * PROC[proc]["V"] ** 2)
sec_of = lambda k: SEC_BITS[k.split("_")[0]]
props_of = lambda k: SEC_PROPS[k.split("_")[0]]
share = lambda p: 100 * p / (base_uw + p)        # security power / total chip power with security on

# Information-equivalent conventional baseline: the receiver's third-order CIC decimator (R = OSR = 50) moved onto the sensor
# in RTL, checked against the model's CIC and synthesised; then Grain-128a + MAC encrypts B-bit words at the Nyquist rate.
CIC_V = r"""// third-order CIC decimator by 50 for the 1-bit modulator output (0/1 -> -1/+1): three integrators at the modulator
// clock, three combs at the output rate, 19-bit registers (1 + 3 log2 50, rounded up); phase aligned with the receiver model
module cic3(input wire clk, input wire rst, input wire d, output reg [18:0] y, output reg out_valid);
  reg [18:0] i1, i2, i3, c1, c2, c3; reg [5:0] cnt;
  wire [18:0] x = d ? 19'd1 : {19{1'b1}};
  wire [18:0] d1 = i3 - c1, d2 = d1 - c2;
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (rst) begin i1 <= 0; i2 <= 0; i3 <= 0; c1 <= 0; c2 <= 0; c3 <= 0; cnt <= 47; y <= 0; out_valid <= 0; end
    else begin
      i1 <= i1 + x; i2 <= i2 + i1; i3 <= i3 + i2; out_valid <= 0;
      if (cnt == 49) begin cnt <= 0; c1 <= i3; c2 <= d1; c3 <= d2; y <= d2 - c3; out_valid <= 1; end
      else cnt <= cnt + 1;
    end
  end
endmodule
"""
t0 = time.time(); wd_b = WORK / "baseline"; wd_b.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
(wd_b / "cic3.v").write_text(CIC_V)
r_b = rng_for(5150); n_b = 50 * 400
D_b = (r_b.random(n_b) < 0.5 + 0.45 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * np.arange(n_b) / 2000)).astype(np.uint8)   # a busy bit stream
(wd_b / "d.mem").write_text("\n".join(map(str, D_b)) + "\n")
(wd_b / "tb.v").write_text(f"""module tb; reg clk = 0, rst = 1, d = 0; reg dm [0:{n_b - 1}]; integer c, fo; wire [18:0] y; wire ov;
  cic3 u(.clk(clk), .rst(rst), .d(d), .y(y), .out_valid(ov)); always #50 clk = ~clk;
  initial begin $readmemb("d.mem", dm); fo = $fopen("y.txt"); @(posedge clk); #1 rst = 0;
    for (c = 0; c < {n_b} + 3; c = c + 1) begin d = (c < {n_b}) ? dm[c] : 0; @(posedge clk); #1 if (ov) $fwrite(fo, "%0d\\n", $signed(y)); end
    $finish; end
endmodule
""")
subprocess.run([str(PNR_BIN / "iverilog"), "-g2012", "-o", "cic.vvp", "tb.v", "cic3.v"], cwd=wd_b, check=True, capture_output=True)
subprocess.run([str(PNR_BIN / "vvp"), "-n", "cic.vvp"], cwd=wd_b, check=True, capture_output=True)
y_hw = np.array([int(v) for v in (wd_b / "y.txt").read_text().split()])[1:]     # the first output precedes any input
y_ref = np.rint(cic(D_b) * 50 ** 3).astype(int)
cic_ok = len(y_hw) >= len(y_ref) and np.array_equal(y_hw[:len(y_ref)], y_ref)
S_CIC = R.synthesize(YOSYS, "cic3", [str(wd_b / "cic3.v")], str(LIBERTY), str(wd_b))
# its power: the SKY130 gate-level power per GE of Grain-128a + MAC (a datapath clocked at 10 MHz, like the integrators); an estimate
P130_CIC = P130["grain_auth2x"] / ge["grain_auth2x"] * S_CIC["ge"]
# the baseline sends 16-bit words, the word length of [1]: a shorter word would rest on the modelled SNDR, which is not used here

OSR_E = 50                                               # every accuracy result of this notebook is at OSR 50
frame_extra = lambda osr: 96 * (osr * NYQ) / N_DSM       # counter + chip nonce + tag (96 bits) per frame, per 20 samples
P_BASE = P130["grain_auth2x"] + P130_CIC                 # baseline security power, SKY130 (decimator estimated per GE)
# Bits the sensor must transmit per reading (Nyquist sample) for the same information: set by the architecture alone, no radio
# assumed (no radio is designed here). Modulator-level designs send every modulator bit (OSR per sample, plus the frame fields
# of the proposal); the conventional design of [1] sends 16-bit words at 4.5-5x the Nyquist rate (Fig. 4(b) of [1]); the
# information-equivalent design sends B-bit words at the Nyquist rate with the same frame fields.
BITS = {"sdsm": OSR_E, "proposal": OSR_E + frame_extra(OSR_E) / NYQ,
        "trivium": (16 * 4.5, 16 * 5.0),
        "base16": 16 + frame_extra(OSR_E) / NYQ}
BITS30 = dict(sdsm=30, proposal=30 + frame_extra(30) / NYQ, trivium=16 * 5.0)
for _k in ("sdsm_lp", "trivium_lp", "proposal_lp"):
    BITS[_k] = BITS[_k.replace("_lp", "")]
fmt_bits = lambda b: f"{b[0]:.0f} – {b[1]:.0f}" if isinstance(b, tuple) else f"{b:.2f}" if b % 1 else f"{b:.0f}"
EN = {"sdsm_meas": n_gate(PAPER_FIG4A_UW["sdsm"], "65"), "trivium_meas": n_gate(PAPER_FIG4A_UW["trivium"], "65"),
      **{k: n_gate(P130[k], "sky130") for k in ("sdsm", "trivium", "proposal", "sdsm_lp", "trivium_lp", "proposal_lp")},
      "proposal_lp_routed": n_gate(P_CORE, "sky130"), "base": n_gate(P_BASE, "sky130")}
FOM = {k: v / (sec_of(k) * props_of(k)) for k, v in EN.items() if k != "base"}
# the information-equivalent baseline has no FOM: its decimator power is an estimate, not a simulated or measured value
DTLS_EBIT_FJ = 0.89e-9 / 8 * 1e15                         # [9]: 0.89 nJ per byte encrypted, 65 nm (operated at 0.8 V)
FOM["dtls_meas"] = DTLS_EBIT_FJ * 1e3 / (PROC["65"]["L"] * PROC["65"]["V"] ** 2) / (SEC_BITS["aes"] * 3)   # AES-128; confidentiality, authentication, freshness

fmt_p = lambda p: f"{p:.1f}" if p < 100 else f"{p:.0f}"
COST = []
for name, k, p, proc, src in [("S-DSM [1]", "sdsm_meas", 24, "65", "measured [1]"),
                              ("Trivium (conventional, [1])", "trivium_meas", 220, "65", "measured [1]"),
                              ("S-DSM [1], as written, this flow", "sdsm", P130["sdsm"], "sky130", "simulated"),
                              ("Trivium, as written, this flow", "trivium", P130["trivium"], "sky130", "simulated"),
                              ("Proposal, 1 bit/clock (Subsection B)", "proposal", P130["proposal"], "sky130", "simulated"),
                              ("S-DSM [1], low power, this flow", "sdsm_lp", P130["sdsm_lp"], "sky130", "simulated"),
                              ("Trivium, low power, this flow", "trivium_lp", P130["trivium_lp"], "sky130", "simulated"),
                              ("Proposal, low power (full block)", "proposal_lp", P130["proposal_lp"], "sky130", "simulated")]:
    kk = k.replace("_meas", "")
    L, V = PROC[proc]["L"], PROC[proc]["V"]
    COST.append((f"<b>{name}</b>" if k == "proposal_lp" else name, f"{ge[kk]:,.0f}", src, f"{L} nm, {V} V", fmt_p(p),
                 f"{p / 10:.2f}", f"{EN[k]:,.0f}", f"{sec_of(k):g}", f"{props_of(k)}", f"<b>{FOM[k]:.1f}</b>" if k == "proposal_lp" else f"{FOM[k]:,.0f}",
                 fmt_bits(BITS[kk])))
for name, kk, bits in [("Decimate + Grain-128a/MAC, 16-bit words at Nyquist", "base16", 16)]:
    COST.append((name, f"{ge['grain_auth2x'] + S_CIC['ge']:,.0f}*", "simulated*", "150 nm, 1.8 V", f"{P_BASE:.0f}*",
                 f"{P_BASE / 10:.2f}*", "–", "113.8", "3", "– (estimated power)", fmt_bits(BITS[kk])))
table(["Design", "Area (GE)", "Source", "Process (L<sub>min</sub>, V<sub>DD</sub>)", "Power at 10 MHz (µW)", "Energy per bit (pJ/b)",
       "E<sub>bit</sub>/(L<sub>min</sub>V<sub>nom</sub><sup>2</sup>) (aJ/(nm·V²))", "S (bits)", "K", "FOM (aJ/(nm·V²))", f"Bits sent per reading, OSR {OSR_E}"], COST,
      caption="Table XVIII: cost of each security block, every number as measured or simulated in its own process, none scaled: "
              "[1]'s two blocks measured in 65 nm at 1.2 V; this work's blocks simulated at gate level in SKY130 "
              "(sky130_fd_sc_hd, tt, 25 °C, 1.8 V, the same flow for every design). Energy per bit: power over the 10 Mb/s "
              "keystream. L<sub>min</sub>, V<sub>nom</sub>: minimum gate length and nominal supply of the process. S: the smaller of "
              "the key length and log<sub>2</sub> of the cost of the best published attack. K: security properties provided, of four. "
              "FOM = E<sub>bit</sub>/(L<sub>min</sub> V<sub>nom</sub><sup>2</sup> S K), lower is better; no modelled quantity enters it. "
              "Bits sent per reading: transmitted bits per Nyquist sample for the same information, set by the architecture; no radio "
              "is assumed. *: the decimator's area is synthesised and its power "
              "estimated per GE; its 31-tap compensation filter is not included; the baseline's cipher is the one written for one "
              "bit per clock, which disadvantages it")
card("Cost, figure of merit, transmitted bits and the information-equivalent baseline",
     [("figure of merit (no number scaled, nothing modelled)", "FOM = E<sub>bit</sub> / (L<sub>min</sub> V<sub>nom</sub><sup>2</sup> S K): the "
       "energy per encrypted bit (measured for published works, gate-level simulated for this work) over the minimum gate length and "
       "nominal supply squared of its own process (65 nm, 1.2 V for [1]; 150 nm, 1.8 V for SKY130), per bit of security level S, per "
       "security property K provided (of confidentiality, authentication, freshness, no key in NVM); lower is better"),
      ("FOM, as measured in [1] and [9]", f"S-DSM {FOM['sdsm_meas']:,.0f} (S = 16, K = 1), Trivium {FOM['trivium_meas']:,.0f} (S = 80, K = 1), "
       f"DTLS engine [9] {FOM['dtls_meas']:,.0f} (S = 126.1, K = 3)"),
      ("FOM, this flow, 1 bit/clock", f"S-DSM {FOM['sdsm']:,.0f}, Trivium {FOM['trivium']:,.0f}, proposal {FOM['proposal']:,.0f} (S = 113.8, K = 4)"),
      ("FOM, this flow, low power", f"S-DSM {FOM['sdsm_lp']:,.0f}, Trivium {FOM['trivium_lp']:,.0f}, proposal <b>{FOM['proposal_lp']:.1f}</b> "
       f"({FOM['proposal_lp_routed']:.1f} routed, extracted)"),
      ("E<sub>bit</sub>/(L<sub>min</sub>V<sub>nom</sub><sup>2</sup>) alone (no security credit)", f"measured in [1]: S-DSM {EN['sdsm_meas']:,.0f}, Trivium {EN['trivium_meas']:,.0f}; "
       f"this flow, low power: S-DSM {EN['sdsm_lp']:,.0f}, Trivium {EN['trivium_lp']:,.0f}, proposal {EN['proposal_lp']:,.0f}; "
       f"proposal ÷ S-DSM {EN['proposal_lp'] / EN['sdsm_lp']:.1f}× in the same flow and form"),
      ("[1]'s blocks: measured against their RTL in this flow", f"{EN['sdsm_meas']:,.0f} against {EN['sdsm']:,.0f} for the S-DSM "
       f"({EN['sdsm_meas'] / EN['sdsm']:.1f}×), {EN['trivium_meas']:,.0f} against {EN['trivium']:,.0f} for Trivium "
       f"({EN['trivium_meas'] / EN['trivium']:.1f}×): the measured blocks draw more per unit of process than their logic"),
      ("proposal against the S-DSM by FOM", f"<b>{FOM['sdsm_meas'] / FOM['proposal_lp']:.0f}× lower</b> than [1]'s measured S-DSM; "
       f"{FOM['sdsm_lp'] / FOM['proposal_lp']:.1f}× lower than the S-DSM in the same flow and form"),
      (f"bits sent per reading for the same information, OSR {OSR_E} (no radio assumed)", f"S-DSM {fmt_bits(BITS['sdsm'])}, proposal "
       f"{fmt_bits(BITS['proposal'])} (with its counter, chip nonce and tag), decimate + Trivium of [1] {fmt_bits(BITS['trivium'])} "
       f"(16-bit words at 4.5–5× Nyquist): the proposal sends <b>{BITS['trivium'][0] / BITS['proposal']:.2f}–"
       f"{BITS['trivium'][1] / BITS['proposal']:.2f}× fewer bits</b> than the conventional design of [1]"),
      ("information-equivalent baseline (decimate on the sensor, Grain-128a + MAC, words at the Nyquist rate)",
       f"CIC decimator {S_CIC['ge']:,.0f} GE, {S_CIC['ffs']} flip-flops, {'bit-exact with the model' if cic_ok else '<b>MISMATCH</b>'} "
       f"on {len(y_ref)} outputs; 16-bit words at the Nyquist rate, the word length of [1]: <b>{fmt_bits(BITS['base16'])} bits per reading</b>, "
       f"i.e. the proposal sends <b>{BITS['proposal'] / BITS['base16']:.1f}× more</b>"),
      ("for reference: OSR 30, the setting of the 2.67× of [1]", f"bits per reading: proposal {fmt_bits(BITS30['proposal'])}, S-DSM "
       f"{BITS30['sdsm']}, decimate + Trivium {BITS30['trivium']:.0f}: {BITS30['trivium'] / BITS30['proposal']:.2f}× fewer"),
      ("run time", f"{time.time() - t0:.0f} s (decimator simulation and synthesis)")],
     note="No power is scaled from one process to the other. The FOM divides each design's own energy per bit by the switching-energy "
          "factor of its own process and by the security level it buys; it removes the first-order effect of gate length and "
          "supply, not differences in what a measured block contains beyond its logic, and it credits security strength, not the "
          "attacks of Section IX that a design withstands (S-DSM 4 of 15, proposal 15 of 15). No radio is designed in this work, so no radio energy is claimed: the bits per reading "
          "are a property of the architecture; with a radio whose energy per bit is the same for all designs and dominates, the "
          "energy ratio equals the bit ratio.", tone="ok" if cic_ok else "bad")

fig, (a1, a2, a3) = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(W2, 3.5), gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[0.95, 1.35, 1.0]))
PAIR = [("S-DSM\n[1]", "sdsm"), ("Trivium", "trivium"), ("Pro-\nposal", "proposal")]
xs = np.arange(len(PAIR))
a1.bar(xs - 0.19, [ge[k] for _, k in PAIR], width=0.36, color="white", edgecolor=COL["ink"], lw=0.7, label="1 bit/clock")
a1.bar(xs + 0.19, [ge[k + "_lp"] for _, k in PAIR], width=0.36, color=COL["ok"], edgecolor=COL["ink"], lw=0.7, label="Low power")
for i, (_, k) in enumerate(PAIR):
    a1.text(i + 0.19, ge[k + "_lp"] + 150, f"{ge[k + '_lp']:,.0f}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7.5)
a1.set_xticks(xs, [n for n, _ in PAIR]); a1.tick_params(axis="x", top=False, labelsize=7.5)
a1.set_ylabel("Area (GE, sky130_fd_sc_hd)"); a1.grid(axis="x", visible=False); a1.set_ylim(0, 1.22 * max(ge[k + "_lp"] for _, k in PAIR))
a1.legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper left", handlelength=1.3, borderpad=0.3, labelspacing=0.2)
panel(a1, "a", "synthesised area")
RANK = [("Proposal, low power", "proposal_lp", "lp"), ("Trivium, low power", "trivium_lp", "lp"), ("S-DSM, low power", "sdsm_lp", "lp"),
        ("Proposal, 1 bit/clock", "proposal", "wr"), ("S-DSM, as written", "sdsm", "wr"), ("Trivium, as written", "trivium", "wr"),
        ("S-DSM [1], measured", "sdsm_meas", "ms"), ("Trivium [1], measured", "trivium_meas", "ms"), ("DTLS engine [9], measured", "dtls_meas", "ms")]
RANK.sort(key=lambda r: FOM[r[1]])                                                     # best (lowest) at the top
STY = {"lp": dict(color=COL["ok"], label="this work's flow, low power (SKY130, simulated)"),
       "wr": dict(color="#9fc3ea", label="this work's flow, as written (SKY130, simulated)"),
       "ms": dict(color="#7a7f87", label="published, measured (65 nm)")}
seen = set()
for i, (lab, k, src) in enumerate(RANK):
    st = STY[src]
    a2.barh(i, FOM[k], color=st["color"], ec=COL["ink"], lw=1.4 if k == "proposal_lp" else 0.5, height=0.62,
            label=None if src in seen else st["label"]); seen.add(src)
    a2.text(FOM[k] * 1.08, i, f"{FOM[k]:.1f}" if FOM[k] < 100 else f"{FOM[k]:,.0f}", va="center", fontsize=7.5,
            fontweight="bold" if k == "proposal_lp" else None)
a2.set_yticks(range(len(RANK)), [r[0] for r in RANK]); a2.tick_params(axis="y", left=False, right=False, labelsize=7.5)
a2.set_xscale("log"); a2.set_xlim(0.5 * min(FOM[r[1]] for r in RANK), 3.0 * max(FOM[r[1]] for r in RANK)); a2.invert_yaxis()
a2.set_ylim(len(RANK) - 0.5, -2.3); a2.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
a2.set_xlabel("FOM = $E_\\mathrm{bit}/(L_\\mathrm{min} V_\\mathrm{nom}^2 S K)$ (aJ/(nm·V²)), log scale")
a2.legend(fontsize=6.6, loc="upper right", handlelength=1.0, borderpad=0.3, labelspacing=0.25)
a2.annotate("", xy=(0.04, 0.955), xytext=(0.30, 0.955), xycoords="axes fraction", arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=COL["ink"], lw=1.0))
a2.text(0.04, 0.905, "better (lower)", transform=a2.transAxes, ha="left", va="top", fontsize=7.5)
panel(a2, "b", "figure of merit")
rows_b = [("S-DSM [1]", BITS["sdsm"]), ("Proposal", BITS["proposal"]), ("Decimate + Trivium [1]", BITS["trivium"][1]),
          ("Decimate + Grain/MAC,\n16 bit at Nyquist", BITS["base16"])]
for i, (lab, b) in enumerate(rows_b):
    a3.barh(i, BITS["trivium"][0] if i == 2 else b, color=COL["ok"] if lab == "Proposal" else "#c9ced6", ec=COL["ink"], lw=0.5, height=0.55)
    a3.text(b + 1.5, i, f"{BITS['trivium'][0]:.0f}–{b:.0f}" if i == 2 else fmt_bits(b), va="center", fontsize=8)
a3.barh(2, BITS["trivium"][1] - BITS["trivium"][0], left=BITS["trivium"][0], color="white", hatch="////", ec=COL["ink"], lw=0.5,
        height=0.55, label="range of [1] (4.5–5× Nyquist)")
a3.axhline(2.5, color=COL["faint"], lw=0.6, ls=":")
a3.text(0.97 * 1.45 * BITS["trivium"][1], 0.5, "bits sent\nundecimated", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=7.5, color=COL["faint"])
a3.text(0.97 * 1.45 * BITS["trivium"][1], 3.0, "decimated on\nthe sensor", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=7.5, color=COL["faint"])
a3.set_yticks(range(len(rows_b)), [r[0] for r in rows_b]); a3.tick_params(axis="y", left=False, right=False, labelsize=7.5)
a3.set_ylim(len(rows_b) - 0.5, -1.2); a3.set_xlim(0, 1.45 * BITS["trivium"][1]); a3.set_xlabel("Bits per reading")
a3.grid(axis="y", visible=False); a3.legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper right", handlelength=1.0)
panel(a3, "c", "transmitted bits")
fig.tight_layout(w_pad=0.5); plt.show()

8.0× lower than the S-DSM in the same flow and form</td></tr><tr><td style="padding:2px 18px 2px 0;opacity:.8;vertical-align:top">bits sent per reading for the same information, OSR 50 (no radio assumed)</td><td style="padding:2px 0;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums">S-DSM 50, proposal 50.04 (with its counter, chip nonce and tag), decimate + Trivium of [1] 72 – 80 (16-bit words at 4.5–5× Nyquist): the proposal sends <b>1.44–1.60× fewer bits</b> than the conventional design of [1]</td></tr><tr><td style="padding:2px 18px 2px 0;opacity:.8;vertical-align:top">information-equivalent baseline (decimate on the sensor, Grain-128a + MAC, words at the Nyquist rate)</td><td style="padding:2px 0;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums">CIC decimator 1,889 GE, 140 flip-flops, bit-exact with the model on 400 outputs; 16-bit words at the Nyquist rate, the word length of [1]: <b>16.04 bits per reading</b>, i.e. the proposal sends <b>3.1× more</b></td></tr><tr><td style="padding:2px 18px 2px 0;opacity:.8;vertical-align:top">for reference: OSR 30, the setting of the 2.67× of [1]</td><td style="padding:2px 0;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums">bits per reading: proposal 30.03, S-DSM 30, decimate + Trivium 80: 2.66× fewer</td></tr><tr><td style="padding:2px 18px 2px 0;opacity:.8;vertical-align:top">run time</td><td style="padding:2px 0;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums">2 s (decimator simulation and synthesis)</td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:4px;opacity:.85">No power is scaled from one process to the other. The FOM divides each design's own energy per bit by the switching-energy factor of its own process and by the security level it buys; it removes the first-order effect of gate length and supply, not differences in what a measured block contains beyond its logic, and it credits security strength, not the attacks of Section IX that a design withstands (S-DSM 4 of 15, proposal 15 of 15). No radio is designed in this work, so no radio energy is claimed: the bits per reading are a property of the architecture; with a radio whose energy per bit is the same for all designs and dominates, the energy ratio equals the bit ratio.</div></div>

<p align="center" style="text-align:center"><b>Fig. 58.</b> Area, figure of merit and transmitted bits of the security blocks. (a) Synthesised area in GE, as written for one bit per clock (white) and in the low-power form (blue). (b) FOM = E<sub>bit</sub>/(L<sub>min</sub> V<sub>nom</sub><sup>2</sup> S K) in aJ/(nm·V²), log scale, lower is better (arrow), one bar per design, sorted from the lowest: this work's SKY130 gate-level blocks in the low-power form (blue; the proposal outlined) and as written (light blue), and the published blocks as measured in 65 nm ([1] and the DTLS engine [9], grey); no number scaled. (c) Bits sent per reading (Nyquist sample) for the same information at an oversampling ratio of 50, set by the architecture, no radio assumed; hatched: the range of [1]'s conventional design; lower group: designs that decimate on the sensor.</p>

**Result.** Fig. 58(a) shows the areas of Table XIV in both forms: the low-power forms are larger, the proposal most (9,869 against 5,240 GE), because the parallel update repeats the feedback logic of each step.

*Figure of merit* (Table XVIII, Fig. 58(b)). $L_{\min} V_{\text{nom}}^2$ is 486 nm·V² for SKY130 and 93.6 nm·V² for the 65 nm process of [1]. Normalised by it, the energy per bit is 25,641 aJ/(nm·V²) for [1]'s measured S-DSM and 235,043 for its measured Trivium; in this flow, 8,827 for the S-DSM as written and 3,724 in the low-power form, 45,885 and 6,646 for Trivium, and 85,391 and **13,230** for the proposal. The FOM, which divides these values by the security level and the number of security properties, is 1,603 for [1]'s measured S-DSM (S = 16, K = 1), 2,938 for its measured Trivium (S = 80, K = 1) and 3,142 for the DTLS engine of [9] (S = 126.1, K = 3); in this flow, 552, 574 and 188 for the S-DSM, Trivium and the proposal as written, and 233, 83 and **29.1** in the low-power form (33.2 for the proposal routed, with extracted wires). The information-equivalent baseline receives no FOM, because its decimator power is estimated. Without the credit for security, the low-power proposal takes 3.6× the normalised energy per bit of the S-DSM in the same flow and form, the ratio of their powers.

*Bits sent at OSR 50.* For the same information (Fig. 58(c)), the S-DSM sends 50 bits per reading and the proposal 50.04 with its frame fields, against 72–80 for the conventional design of [1]: **the proposal sends 1.44–1.60× fewer bits than the conventional design of [1] at OSR 50**, as predicted. The 2.66× of the same comparison at OSR 30 (30.03 against 80 bits, card), the setting of [1]'s headline 2.67×, does not apply at the oversampling ratio of this notebook's accuracy results.

*The information-equivalent baseline.* The CIC decimator in RTL reproduces the model's CIC output for output (400 outputs, card) and synthesises to 1,889 GE with 140 flip-flops. Sending 16-bit words, the word length of [1], at the Nyquist rate, the baseline sends **16.04 bits per reading, 3.1× fewer than the proposal**. As predicted, sending one word per Nyquist sample instead of 50 modulator bits is the decisive difference.

**Interpretation.** Two facts hold at once, and the FOM keeps them apart. By this figure of merit, the proposal provides the most security per unit of normalised energy of the designs compared: its FOM of 29.1 is 55× below that of [1]'s measured S-DSM, 108× below the DTLS engine of [9] and 8× below the S-DSM in the same flow and form, because it buys 113.8 bits of security and all four security properties for 3.6× the energy per bit. In absolute power, however, it is not as cheap as the S-DSM: in the same flow its gate-level simulated power is 3.6× the S-DSM's, a ratio that does not depend on the process, and part of the factor of 55 comes from [1]'s measured block, which takes 2.9× the normalised energy per bit of its own RTL in this flow for reasons the data of [1] do not give. In transmitted bits, the advantage of a modulator-level scheme exists only against the conventional design of [1], which sends 16-bit words at 4.5–5× the Nyquist rate; against a conventional design that decimates to the Nyquist rate before encrypting, **the proposal, like the S-DSM, sends about 3× more bits**. What the bit-level architecture keeps is the absence of a decimator and of a word-level datapath on the sensor, not the fewest bits per reading. No radio energy is claimed, since no radio is designed here.

### F. Power breakdown of the chip of [1], with each security block

**Goal.** Show the result in the form of Fig. 4(a) of [1], so that the proposal's security block can be compared at a glance with the two designs measured there.

**Setup.** The four blocks of the chip take the values measured in [1]: front end (DAC and amplifiers) 321 µW, TIA 271 µW, S-to-D buffer 250 µW and ΔΣ modulator 510 µW. The security block is the measured 24 µW (S-DSM) or 220 µW (Trivium), or, for the proposal, its low-power block at its own SKY130 gate-level power (64.3 µW at 1.8 V), not scaled to 65 nm. Because a SKY130 gate switches about 5.2× the energy of a 65 nm gate, this places the proposal pessimistically beside the measured slices. Overhead is the security power relative to the chip with security off (1,352 µW). Each ring starts at the top and runs clockwise; the security block is its last slice.

> **Next cell.** Draws the chip's power breakdown for each design as a ring chart, like Fig. 4(a) of [1].


```python
#@title Fig.: power breakdown
# Power breakdown as in Fig. 4(a) of [1]: the chip's four measured blocks and each design's security block
# (the proposal with its SKY130 power, unscaled); overhead = security power / chip power with security off
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
blocks = [("Front end (DAC, amplifiers)", PAPER_FIG4A_UW["fe"]), ("TIA", PAPER_FIG4A_UW["tia"]),
          ("S-to-D buffer", PAPER_FIG4A_UW["s2d"]), ("ΔΣ modulator", PAPER_FIG4A_UW["dsm"])]
# categorical slots 2-5 of the figure palette (slot 1, blue, is the security block); this ring order, including the
# closing security-to-front-end pair, keeps adjacent wedges apart for colour-blind readers
shades = ["#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100", "#e87ba4"]
# the low-power block with its own SKY130 power (150 nm, 1.8 V), not scaled to the 65 nm chip: a pessimistic placement
p_prop = P130["proposal_lp"]
designs = [("Original S-DSM [1]", "LFSRs", PAPER_FIG4A_UW["sdsm"], None),
           ("Trivium [1]", "Trivium", PAPER_FIG4A_UW["trivium"], None),
           ("Proposal, low power (SKY130)", "Proposal (SKY130)", p_prop, None)]
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(W2, 2.45), gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[1, 1, 1, 1.15]))   # rings + legend column
lax = axs[3]; axs = axs[:3]
for ax, (title, sec, p, band), lab in zip(axs, designs, "abc"):
    vals = [v for _, v in blocks] + [p]
    w, _ = ax.pie(vals, colors=shades + [COL["ok"]], startangle=90, counterclock=False, radius=1.0,
                  wedgeprops=dict(width=0.42, edgecolor="white", linewidth=1.6))
    total = sum(vals)
    ax.text(0, 0.10, f"{total:,.0f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=11.5, fontweight="bold")
    ax.text(0, -0.17, "µW total", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8.5, color=COL["faint"])
    # label the security slice outside, with a leader line from the middle of the ring
    ang = np.deg2rad((w[-1].theta1 + w[-1].theta2) / 2)
    x0, y0 = 0.79 * np.cos(ang), 0.79 * np.sin(ang)
    side = 1 if np.cos(ang) >= 0 else -1
    ax.annotate(f"{sec}\n{p:.0f} µW" + (f" ({band[0]:.0f}–{band[1]:.0f})" if band else ""),
                xy=(x0, y0), xytext=(0.62 * side, 1.08), ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8, color=COL["ink"],
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=COL["ok"], lw=0.8, shrinkA=0, shrinkB=1))
    ov = f"{100 * p / base_uw:.1f} %" + (f"  ({100 * band[0] / base_uw:.1f}–{100 * band[1] / base_uw:.1f} %)" if band else "")
    ax.text(0, -1.08, f"overhead {ov}", ha="center", va="top", fontsize=8.5)
    ax.text(0, -1.36, f"({lab}) {title}", ha="center", va="top", fontsize=9)
    ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.set_xlim(-1.3, 1.3); ax.set_ylim(-1.62, 1.55); ax.axis("off")
handles = [Patch(fc=c, ec=COL["ink"], lw=0.5, label=f"{n}, {v:.0f} µW") for (n, v), c in zip(blocks, shades)]
handles.append(Patch(fc=COL["ok"], ec=COL["ok"], label="Security block"))
lax.axis("off"); lax.legend(handles=handles, loc="center left", ncol=1, fontsize=7.5, frameon=False, handlelength=1.2,
                            labelspacing=0.6, borderaxespad=0.0)
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.0, right=1.0, top=0.99, bottom=0.01, wspace=0.02); plt.show()

### G. Complete system power: the proposal against [1] under the same conditions

**Goal.** Bring the results of Subsections D to F together for the complete chip, so that the power of the proposal is compared with the chip of [1] block by block, with every number's source stated and both fair comparisons given: with the unscaled numbers (measured for [1], simulated for the proposal) on [1]'s chip, and against [1]'s design treated exactly as the proposal is.

**Theory.** The chip's power is the sum of its blocks, $P_{\text{chip}} = P_{\text{FE}} + P_{\text{TIA}} + P_{\text{S2D}} + P_{\Delta\Sigma} + P_{\text{sec}}$, and its current at the 1.2 V supply of [1] is $I = P_{\text{chip}}/1.2\ \text{V}$. The proposal leaves the four analog blocks unchanged (Section IV), so the only term that differs between the designs is $P_{\text{sec}}$, and the comparison reduces to the security block. This work does not simulate the power of the analog blocks: the front end, the TIA, the buffer and the modulator's integrators are behavioural in the model (Section V), and only the modulator's comparator is simulated at transistor level, at about 2 µW (Section VIII). Their powers are therefore the values measured on the chip of [1], and are marked as such; the radio is left out. No power is scaled from one process to the other. Two comparisons are fair, and they answer different questions. *With the numbers as obtained, unscaled:* the proposal's SKY130 block (gate-level simulation) on the chip of [1], beside the S-DSM's 24 µW as measured; since a SKY130 gate switches about 5.2× the energy of a 65 nm gate (Subsection E), this places the proposal pessimistically. *Under strictly equal treatment:* the proposal against [1]'s design re-implemented in the same flow with the same low-power techniques, whose ratio does not depend on the process; and the FOM of Subsection E, which compares designs across processes. The prediction from Subsection D is that the ratio under equal treatment stays above one, because the proposal holds 256 bits of cipher state and 64 bits of MAC state where [1] holds 16 bits of LFSR state, and because the per-clock interface (the output bit selection and the capture of one message bit per clock for the MAC) remains at 10 MHz.

**Setup.** Analog blocks: Fig. 4(a) of [1], the values of Subsection E; the radio is not included, since no radio is designed or simulated in this work. Security blocks: [1]'s measured S-DSM (24 µW) and Trivium (220 µW) in 65 nm at 1.2 V; this work's SKY130 gate-level powers at 1.8 V (Table XV) of the S-DSM, Trivium and the proposal, as written and in the low-power form, and of the routed low-power proposal; none scaled. Metrics: each block's power and current, the chip's total power and current with each security block, the security block's share of the chip's power, and the energy for the same information at OSR 50.

> **Next cell.** 1. Collects the measured powers of the four analog blocks and the radio of [1] and the security block of every design: [1]'s measured values and this work's gate-level SKY130 powers, none scaled. 2. Tabulates each block's power and current at 1.2 V and the chip's totals. 3. Prints the card with the comparisons against [1]. No new simulation.


```python
#@title Complete system power: the proposal against [1]
# Complete system power, the proposal against [1] under the same conditions. The four analog blocks are the
# values measured on the chip of [1] (this work does not simulate their power; the analog front end and the modulator are
# unchanged by the proposal). The security block of each design is this work's gate-level SKY130 power, in both forms,
# scaled to the 65 nm, 1.2 V chip of [1] by first principles (CV²f, the same factor for every design); [1]'s two measured
# blocks are given beside them. Currents are at the 1.2 V supply of [1].
VDD65 = 1.2                                              # supply of [1]
# Every security block with its own number, none scaled: [1]'s measured 65 nm blocks, and this work's SKY130 gate-level blocks.
SEC = [("S-DSM [1], measured (65 nm, 1.2 V)", PAPER_FIG4A_UW["sdsm"], "measured [1]"),
       ("Trivium [1], measured (65 nm, 1.2 V)", PAPER_FIG4A_UW["trivium"], "measured [1]"),
       ("S-DSM [1] as written, this flow (SKY130, 1.8 V)", P130["sdsm"], "simulated"),
       ("S-DSM [1], low power, this flow (SKY130, 1.8 V)", P130["sdsm_lp"], "simulated"),
       ("Trivium, low power, this flow (SKY130, 1.8 V)", P130["trivium_lp"], "simulated"),
       ("Proposal, 1 bit/clock, this flow (SKY130, 1.8 V)", P130["proposal"], "simulated"),
       ("Proposal, low power, this flow (SKY130, 1.8 V)", P130["proposal_lp"], "simulated"),
       ("Proposal, low power, routed and extracted (SKY130, 1.8 V)", P_CORE, "simulated")]
rows = [(n, "measured [1]", f"{v:,.0f}", f"{v / VDD65:,.0f}", "–") for n, v in
        [("Front end (DAC and amplifiers)", PAPER_FIG4A_UW["fe"]), ("TIA", PAPER_FIG4A_UW["tia"]),
         ("S-to-D buffer", PAPER_FIG4A_UW["s2d"]), ("ΔΣ modulator", PAPER_FIG4A_UW["dsm"])]]
rows.append(("<b>Analog chip without security</b>", "measured [1]", f"<b>{base_uw:,.0f}</b>", f"<b>{base_uw / VDD65:,.0f}</b>", "–"))
for n, v, src in SEC:
    tot = base_uw + v
    rows.append((("<b>" + n + "</b>") if n.startswith("Proposal, low power, this flow") else n, src, f"{v:,.1f}" if v < 100 else f"{v:,.0f}",
                 f"{v / VDD65:,.1f}" if v < 100 else f"{v / VDD65:,.0f}", f"{tot:,.0f} µW, {tot / VDD65:,.0f} µA; {share(v):.1f} %"))
table(["Block", "Source", "Power (µW)", "Current at 1.2 V (µA)", "Chip total with this security block; security share"], rows,
      caption="Table XIX: complete chip power of the sensor of [1] with each security block. Analog blocks: measured in "
              "[1] (65 nm, 1.2 V; unchanged by the proposal, not simulated here). Security blocks: [1]'s measured values and this "
              "work's SKY130 gate-level powers, each in its own process and none scaled, so the chip totals with a SKY130 block mix "
              "two processes and place this work's blocks pessimistically. The radio is not included: no radio is designed or "
              "simulated in this work", align=["left", "left", "right", "right", "left"])
tot = lambda v: f"{base_uw + v:,.0f} µW, {(base_uw + v) / VDD65:,.0f} µA"
card("Complete system power: the proposal against [1]",
     [("security block, actual numbers (none scaled)", f"S-DSM [1] {PAPER_FIG4A_UW['sdsm']:.0f} µW measured in 65 nm; low-power proposal "
       f"<b>{P130['proposal_lp']:.1f} µW</b> simulated in SKY130 ({P_CORE:.1f} µW routed) "
       f"(L<sub>min</sub> V<sub>nom</sub><sup>2</sup> {PROC['sky130']['L'] * PROC['sky130']['V'] ** 2 / (PROC['65']['L'] * PROC['65']['V'] ** 2):.1f}× that of the 65 nm process of [1])"),
      ("chip of [1] with the proposal's SKY130 block (pessimistic)", f"{tot(P130['proposal_lp'])}; security {share(P130['proposal_lp']):.1f} % "
       f"of the chip, against {tot(24)} and {share(24):.1f} % with the S-DSM as measured"),
      ("same flow, same techniques (process cancels)", f"proposal ÷ S-DSM <b>{P130['proposal_lp'] / P130['sdsm_lp']:.1f}×</b> in power; "
       f"proposal ÷ Trivium {P130['proposal_lp'] / P130['trivium_lp']:.1f}×; before the low-power forms {P130['proposal'] / P130['sdsm']:.1f}× and "
       f"{P130['proposal'] / P130['trivium']:.1f}×"),
      ("figure of merit (E<sub>bit</sub> / (L<sub>min</sub> V<sub>nom</sub><sup>2</sup> S K), aJ/(nm·V²), lower is better)", f"S-DSM [1] measured "
       f"{FOM['sdsm_meas']:,.0f}, Trivium [1] measured {FOM['trivium_meas']:,.0f}; low-power proposal <b>{FOM['proposal_lp']:.1f}</b>; "
       f"S-DSM low power in this flow {FOM['sdsm_lp']:,.0f}"),
      (f"bits sent per reading for the same information, OSR {OSR_E}", f"S-DSM {fmt_bits(BITS['sdsm'])}, proposal {fmt_bits(BITS['proposal'])}, "
       f"decimate + Trivium of [1] {fmt_bits(BITS['trivium'])}: set by the architecture; no radio is designed here")],
     note="The analog powers are [1]'s measurements, not results of this work; only the security blocks are simulated here, and no "
          "radio is designed, so none is included. "
          "No power is scaled between processes; the process enters only through the figure of merit of Subsection E.")
```
