**Result.** In Table XIX, the four analog blocks measured in [1] draw 1,352 µW (1,127 µA at 1.2 V); the security block is the only term that differs between the designs. *With actual numbers*, the low-power proposal draws **64.3 µW in SKY130** in gate-level simulation on its placement (73.4 µW with the wiring extracted after routing), against the S-DSM's 24 µW measured in 65 nm in [1]: placed unscaled on the chip of [1], it raises the chip's power to 1,416 µW (1,180 µA) instead of 1,376 µW (1,147 µA), and the security share from 1.7 % to 4.5 % (5.1 % routed), against 14.0 % for the measured Trivium. *Under strictly equal treatment*, in the same flow and form, the proposal draws **3.6×** the S-DSM and 2.0× Trivium, against 9.7× and 1.9× before the low-power forms. By the FOM, the low-power proposal reaches 29.1 aJ/(nm·V²), against 1,603 for [1]'s measured S-DSM and 233 for the S-DSM in the same flow and form. For the same information at OSR 50, the S-DSM sends 50 bits per reading, the proposal 50.04 and the conventional design of [1] 72–80.

**Interpretation.** **Even with its SKY130 power, unscaled and in a process whose gates switch 5.2× the energy of those of [1], the proposal's security block, placed unscaled on the chip of [1], would take 4.5 % of that chip's power**, for a key that is not held in non-volatile memory, a 128-bit cipher in place of a 16-bit LFSR, and an authenticated, replay-protected link. Its power in the same flow is 3.6× that of the S-DSM. That factor is not a matter of process, since both designs are compared in the same flow and the ratio does not depend on it: it is the price of 256 bits of cipher state and 64 bits of MAC state against 16 bits of LFSR state per register, and of the message capture and output selection that must run at the 10 MHz modulator clock. Reducing it further would require changing what is computed, for example a shorter MAC, rather than how it is implemented. Per unit of security, the FOM shows the opposite order: the proposal buys far more security per gate switching than the S-DSM. Both modulator-level designs send fewer bits than the conventional design of [1] at OSR 50 (no radio is designed in this work, so no radio power or energy is included).

**Result.** The rings total 1,376 µW with the LFSRs of the S-DSM, 1,572 µW with Trivium and 1,416 µW with the low-power proposal at its own SKY130 power. The overhead, the security block's power relative to the chip of [1] with security off (its measured 65 nm power, with the proposal's unscaled SKY130 gate-level power), is 1.8 % with the LFSRs of the S-DSM, 16.3 % with Trivium and 4.8 % with the proposal; as a share of the chip's total these are 1.7, 14.0 and 4.5 %.

**Interpretation.** The analog front end and the modulator draw almost all of the chip's power in every design. In its low-power form, and even unscaled from SKY130, the proposal's security slice is a few times that of the S-DSM and far below that of an on-chip Trivium; Subsection G gives the chip block by block and the ratio under strictly equal treatment.

#### Summary of Section X

1. **The RTL passes every functional check.** All eight Verilog top-level modules, five written for one bit per clock and three in low-power form, pass every check against the published test vectors, at RTL and after synthesis, from random initial flip-flop states (178/178, Table XIV).
2. **Area.** The proposal's keystream block is 9,869 GE on `sky130_fd_sc_hd` in its low-power form (5,240 GE written for one bit per clock), against 869 GE (450) for the S-DSM and 2,931 GE (2,376) for Trivium (Table XIV). This is the block that runs during every frame; the key generator, the hash and the PUF array are costed in Section XI.
3. **The block is placed and routed in SKY130; 16 antenna violations are not closed.** The low-power block is placed and routed with OpenROAD, is DRC and LVS clean, meets timing at three corners with extracted wires, and its routed netlist passes its functional checks; 16 antenna violations remain (Fig. 56, Subsection C).
4. **Same conditions for every design.** The parallel update (radix 16) and clock gating, applied to every design, reduce the proposal's power in SKY130 from 415 to 64.3 µW (73.4 µW routed), the S-DSM's from 43 to 18.1 µW and Trivium's from 223 to 32.3 µW; the proposal falls from 9.7× to 3.6× the S-DSM (Table XV). What remains is its 10 MHz interface and clock tree (about 56 %) and its 320 bits of cipher and MAC state (Table XVI).
5. **Across processes, by a figure of merit; no number scaled.** FOM = E<sub>bit</sub>/(L<sub>min</sub> V<sub>nom</sub><sup>2</sup> S K): the energy per bit, measured or gate-level simulated, over L<sub>min</sub>V<sub>nom</sub><sup>2</sup> of the design's own process, per bit of security level S, per security property K provided; no scaled or estimated quantity enters it. The low-power proposal reaches **29.1 aJ/(nm·V²)** (33.2 routed), against 1,603 for [1]'s measured S-DSM, 2,938 for its measured Trivium and 3,142 for the DTLS engine of [9], and 233 for the S-DSM in the same flow and form (Table XVIII, Fig. 58(b)). Placed unscaled on the chip of [1], its SKY130 power takes 4.5 % of the chip's total against 1.7 % for the S-DSM and 14.0 % for Trivium (Table XIX).
6. **Transmitted bits at OSR 50; no radio energy claimed.** For the same information, the proposal sends 50.04 bits per reading against 72–80 for the conventional design of [1], **1.44–1.60× fewer** (2.66× at the OSR 30 of [1]'s headline). **An information-equivalent conventional design**, decimating on the sensor and encrypting 16-bit words at the Nyquist rate with Grain-128a + MAC, **sends 16.04, 3.1× fewer than the proposal** (Table XVIII). No radio is designed in this work, so these are bit counts, not energies.

*Limits.* Timing and power are computed at the typical corner only (Subsection C states the parasitics used), with zero-delay activity, which counts no glitches; the power of the compared designs is computed on their placements, the low-power proposal also on its routing; 16 antenna violations of the low-power block are not closed; the FOM normalises the process to first order only (L<sub>min</sub>V<sub>nom</sub><sup>2</sup>), credits security linearly in bits and by a count of properties, and cannot remove what [1]'s measured blocks contain beyond their logic (2.9× and 5.1× the normalised energy per bit of their RTL in this flow); the information-equivalent baseline's decimator power is estimated per GE, without its compensation filter; the PUF array, the key decoder and the hash are costed in Section XI; the 32-bit delay line, the downlink receiver (which receives the session nonce and the helper data), the PUF array's periphery (word-line drivers, read-out and power switching) and the decoder's and hash's power are not costed anywhere in this notebook. The decoder and the hash run once per power-up (Section XI), so their energy, not their power, is what matters, and it is not computed.

**Next.** The key generator, the PUF array and its BCH decoder, is not costed in this section; its size depends on how reliable the key must be and at which corners. Section XI sizes it from a specification, and generates, verifies, synthesises and lays out its decoder with the flow of this section, then completes the area with the hash and the helper data.

# **XI. From specification to hardware: a key-generator compiler**
---
**Question.** Given a reliability and secrecy specification for the key, which SRAM-PUF array and which error-correcting code meet it at every process corner and temperature, and what does the resulting key-reconstruction hardware cost?

**Why it matters.** The proposal stores no key: it regenerates a 128-bit key from the SRAM-PUF at every power-up. Its security therefore depends on that key being reproduced correctly on every chip, and its cost includes the decoder that reproduces it, which Section X did not include.

**What it takes from earlier sections.** The fuzzy extractor of the model (Section V: a BCH code over GF(2<sup>10</sup>) whose syndromes are the helper data); the SRAM cell's corner models, anchored to each corner's SPICE Monte Carlo, and the two-temperature enrolment (Section VII-F); the cell's bias and its drawn layout (Section VII-D); the findings of Sections VII-E, VII-F and VIII-F that the code sized by hand at the typical corner cannot meet both the reliability target and the secrecy limit with 600 cells, and fails at three of the five corners; and the synthesis and place-and-route flow of Section X.

**Why a compiler is needed.** The proposal's central claim is a key that is regenerated correctly at every power-up, with a failure probability below 10<sup>−6</sup> over the specified temperatures, at every process corner. **Sizing the key generator by hand cannot establish that claim**, for four reasons, each shown by the results of this notebook:

* *The hand design fails at some corners.* Section VII-E sizes the code at the typical corner from the simulated error rates: with 600 cells and a 25 °C enrolment, reliability over the population needs t = 39 at the 99th percentile (t ≥ 46 over the interval of the 85 °C error rate) but the bounded secrecy budget (192 bits at the 95 % lower bound of the min-entropy) allows at most t = 35, so both cannot be met; the system simulations use t = 45 as a working setting (94–137 secret bits). Section VIII-F shows that, with the error rates of the PVT run, this code is reliable at tt and ss but fails at the three other corners: at sf, where the cell is noisier, and at the fast-nMOS corners ff and fs above room temperature, where cells reverse their preferred state. The code must be checked against every corner, temperature and enrolment procedure, which is a search, not a single calculation.
* *Whether a solution exists at all is a search result.* With a 25 °C enrolment, the errors at the fast-nMOS corners are reproducible flips; a stronger code absorbs them only by publishing more helper data than the cells contain secrecy. Showing that no code within a stated design space meets the specification, and that a two-temperature enrolment does, requires a systematic search of that space.
* *The hardware cost cannot be read from the code parameters.* The trade-off between more cells (an inner repetition code) and a smaller decoder (a smaller t) changes with the corner and the enrolment. Only synthesis of the candidates shows which design is smallest, and whether the decoder or the cell array dominates the area.
* *A reliability figure must describe hardware, not a formula.* The decoder that will be built has to reconstruct the key bit for bit as the model does, including when it must report failure.

A compiler, a program that turns a specification into a generated decoder, verified in RTL simulation, synthesised and laid out, answers all four, and it does so again whenever the specification, the process or the cell changes. It is also the part of this work that is a *code-to-chip* flow in the literal sense: its input is a specification, its output a layout. It works in five steps, and a sixth completes the cost:

1. **Specification:** the key-failure probability per power-up, the temperature range, the process corners, the enrolment procedure and the number of secret bits.
2. **Design-space search:** for each repetition factor of a concatenated code, the smallest array and BCH strength that meet the specification at every corner and temperature.
3. **Verilog generation, synthesis and selection:** the most promising candidates are written as Verilog, synthesised on `sky130_fd_sc_hd`, and the smallest total area (decoder plus PUF array) is selected.
4. **Verification:** the generated hardware is simulated against the model's fuzzy extractor, bit for bit.
5. **Place and route:** the selected design is carried to a layout with the flow of Section X.
6. **Complete area:** the hash that turns the corrected fingerprint into the key is written and synthesised, and the area of every part of the proposal's digital security is collected, with the parts that are not designed listed.

**Live and recorded.** Steps 1–4 and the placement, clock tree, global routing and timing of step 5 run live in the present session. Step 3 synthesises only the two most promising candidates of each specification, ranked by an area estimate; the others keep the estimate. The detailed routing of step 5 (with its routing-DRC and antenna counts) and the Magic DRC of the routed layout are shown by default from a recorded run of the same flow on the same design (`dev/rtl/compiled_unit_routed.json`: 0 routing DRC and 0 Magic DRC violations, 2 antenna violations, 424 s on two cores); setting `ROUTE_COMPILED = True` in the step-5 cell runs them live.

**Roadmap.** Subsection A sets the specification and the search (steps 1 and 2), Subsection B the generation, synthesis and selection (step 3); one code cell runs both, and their results follow it. Subsection C verifies the generated hardware (step 4), Subsection D places and routes it (step 5), Subsection E completes the area (step 6) and compares the decoder with published ones, and a summary closes the section. The compiler itself is the module `keygen.py` written by the first cell. It is independent of the notebook and can be reused with other cell models, targets or codes.

> **Next cell.** Writes the compiler to `keygen.py`: 1. the design-space search; 2. the Verilog generator; 3. the Icarus test bench.


```python
%%writefile keygen.py
"""keygen.py - a compiler for the proposal's PUF key-reconstruction hardware: from a specification to verified Verilog.

    cfg = design_keygen(spec, cell_err)   # design-space search: repetition factor r, BCH length n and strength t
    files = emit_verilog(cfg, outdir)     # synthesisable Verilog: repetition voter + serial BCH(n, t) decoder
    out = simulate(cfg, outdir, tests, iverilog, vvp)   # Icarus simulation of the generated RTL on given test streams

The fuzzy extractor is the model's (Section V): the syndrome construction over GF(2^10) with the primitive polynomial
x^10 + x^3 + 1, the t odd syndromes of the fingerprint as helper data, Berlekamp-Massey and a Chien search. The compiler
adds an optional inner repetition code (concatenated construction): the cells form n groups of r; the enrolled value of a
group is its first cell, the helper data holds the other cells xor the first, and reconstruction takes the majority. The
BCH code then corrects the n group values. The hardware decodes with the inversionless Berlekamp-Massey algorithm, whose
error locator is a non-zero multiple of the model's, so the corrected bits and the success flag are identical.
"""
import math, os, subprocess
import numpy as np

M, PRIM = 10, 0x409                      # GF(2^10), x^10 + x^3 + 1 (as the model)
GF_N = (1 << M) - 1
EXP = [0] * (2 * GF_N); LOG = [0] * (GF_N + 1)
_x = 1
for _i in range(GF_N):
    EXP[_i] = _x; LOG[_x] = _i
    _x <<= 1
    if _x & (1 << M):
        _x ^= PRIM
for _i in range(GF_N, 2 * GF_N):
    EXP[_i] = EXP[_i - GF_N]


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 1. design-space search
def _dist(p):
    """Poisson-binomial distribution of the number of errors among independent events with probabilities p."""
    d = np.zeros(len(p) + 1); d[0] = 1.0
    for q in p:
        d[1:] = d[1:] * (1 - q) + d[:-1] * q
        d[0] *= 1 - q
    return d


def group_err(p, r):
    """Probability that the majority of each group of r consecutive cells is wrong (r odd); p: per-cell error probabilities."""
    if r == 1:
        return np.asarray(p, float)
    g = np.asarray(p, float)[: len(p) // r * r].reshape(-1, r)
    d = np.zeros((g.shape[0], r + 1)); d[:, 0] = 1.0
    for c in range(r):
        q = g[:, c:c + 1]
        d[:, 1:] = d[:, 1:] * (1 - q) + d[:, :-1] * q
        d[:, 0] *= 1 - q[:, 0]
    return d[:, (r + 1) // 2:].sum(axis=1)


def secret_bits(n, r, t, bias):
    """Fingerprint bits that stay secret: min-entropy of n groups of r cells, less the (r-1) repetition and m = 10 BCH
    helper bits per group and per unit of t (for r = 1 this is the model's puf_residual)."""
    h = -math.log2(max(bias, 1 - bias))
    return int(math.floor(n * (r * h - (r - 1)) - M * t))


def evaluate(n, r, cell_err, corners, temps, t_max):
    """Worst-case (over corners and temperatures) probability of more than t group errors, for t = 0..t_max."""
    worst = np.zeros(t_max + 1)
    for c in corners:
        for T in temps:
            d = _dist(group_err(cell_err(c, n * r, T), r))
            tail = np.cumsum(d[::-1])[::-1][1: t_max + 2]          # P(more than t), summed exactly
            worst = np.maximum(worst, tail)
    return worst


def design_keygen(spec, cell_err, log=None):
    """The smallest configuration (fewest PUF cells; then the smallest t) meeting spec at every corner and temperature.
    spec: p_fail, temps (list, deg C), corners, secret (bits), bias, r (tuple of odd repetition factors), n_step, and keep:
    the fraction of the array that the enrolment keeps (1 for a single 25 C enrolment; the worst corner's fraction for a
    masked enrolment), which sets the physical array size.
    cell_err(corner, N, T): per-cell error probabilities of N enrolled (kept) cells at temperature T.
    Returns dict(choice=..., per_r={r: best or None})."""
    per_r = {}
    for r in spec.get("r", (1, 3, 5, 7)):
        h = r * -math.log2(max(spec["bias"], 1 - spec["bias"])) - (r - 1)
        if h <= 0:
            per_r[r] = None; continue
        n = max(16, int(math.ceil((spec["secret"] + M) / h)))
        best, step = None, spec.get("n_step", 32)
        while n <= GF_N and best is None:
            t_max = min(spec.get("t_max", 120), n // M - 1)
            w = evaluate(n, r, cell_err, spec["corners"], spec["temps"], t_max)
            ok_t = [t for t in range(1, t_max + 1) if w[t] <= spec["p_fail"] and secret_bits(n, r, t, spec["bias"]) >= spec["secret"]]
            if ok_t:
                best = dict(r=r, n=n, t=ok_t[0], p_fail=float(w[ok_t[0]]), secret=secret_bits(n, r, ok_t[0], spec["bias"]))
            else:
                n += step
        if best and step > 4:                                # refine downwards in steps of 4
            for n2 in range(best["n"] - 4, best["n"] - step, -4):
                t_max = min(spec.get("t_max", 120), n2 // M - 1)
                w = evaluate(n2, r, cell_err, spec["corners"], spec["temps"], t_max)
                ok_t = [t for t in range(1, t_max + 1) if w[t] <= spec["p_fail"] and secret_bits(n2, r, t, spec["bias"]) >= spec["secret"]]
                if not ok_t:
                    break
                best = dict(r=r, n=n2, t=ok_t[0], p_fail=float(w[ok_t[0]]), secret=secret_bits(n2, r, ok_t[0], spec["bias"]))
        if best:
            best["cells"] = int(math.ceil(best["n"] * r / spec.get("keep", 1.0)))
        per_r[r] = best
        if log:
            log(f"r = {r}: " + (f"n = {best['n']}, t = {best['t']}, {best['cells']} cells" if best else "infeasible"))
    feas = [b for b in per_r.values() if b]
    choice = min(feas, key=lambda b: (b["cells"], b["t"])) if feas else None
    return dict(choice=choice, per_r=per_r, spec=spec)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 2. Verilog generation
def latency(cfg):
    """Clock cycles of one reconstruction (load, syndromes, Berlekamp-Massey, two Chien passes, output)."""
    n, t, r = cfg["n"], cfg["t"], cfg["r"]
    return n * r + M * t + t * n + t + 2 * t * (2 * (t + 1)) + 2 * n * (t + 1) + n + 8


def _w(x):
    return max(1, int(x).bit_length())


def emit_verilog(cfg, outdir):
    """Write the reconstruction unit for cfg = dict(r, n, t): returns the list of files (top module 'keygen_rec')."""
    os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
    n, t, r = cfg["n"], cfg["t"], cfg["r"]
    a_inv = EXP[GF_N - 1]
    W_POS, W_T, W_R = _w(n), _w(2 * t + 1), _w(max(r, 1))
    bch = f"""// BCH({n}, t = {t}) reconstruction over GF(2^{M}), x^10 + x^3 + 1: generated by keygen.py. Serial: odd syndromes of the
// received word xor the helper data, the even ones by squaring, inversionless Berlekamp-Massey, then two Chien passes
// (count the roots; if they match the locator degree, correct). Bit-compatible with the model's reconstruct().
module bch_rec (
    input  wire clk, input wire rst, input wire start,
    input  wire din, input wire din_valid,        // received word, position 0 first
    input  wire hin, input wire hin_valid,        // helper data: syndromes S1, S3, ..., MSB first
    output reg  dout, output reg dout_valid,      // corrected word, position 0 first
    output reg  done, output reg ok);
  localparam N = {n}, T = {t}, M = {M};
  localparam [M-1:0] ALPHA = 10'd2, ALPHA2 = 10'd4, ALPHA_INV = 10'd{a_inv};
  function [M-1:0] gmul(input [M-1:0] a, input [M-1:0] b);
    integer q; reg [M-1:0] p, x;
    begin
      p = 0; x = a;
      for (q = 0; q < M; q = q + 1) begin
        if (b[q]) p = p ^ x;
        x = x[M-1] ? ((x << 1) ^ 10'h009) : (x << 1);
      end
      gmul = p;
    end
  endfunction
  localparam S_IDLE = 4'd0, S_LOADW = 4'd1, S_LOADH = 4'd2, S_SYN = 4'd3, S_EVEN = 4'd4, S_DISC = 4'd5, S_UPD = 4'd6,
             S_CH1 = 4'd7, S_CH2 = 4'd8, S_OUT = 4'd9, S_DONE = 4'd10;
  reg [3:0] st;
  reg [N-1:0] w;                                  // the word, rotated one position per clock
  reg [M-1:0] S [1:2*T];                          // syndromes
  reg [M-1:0] L [0:T];                            // error locator
  reg [M-1:0] B [0:T];                            // correction polynomial
  reg [M-1:0] acc, pw, as_, gam, del, v, beta, hsh;
  reg [{W_POS}:0] pos, cnt;
  reg [{W_T}:0] j, i, rr, k;
  reg cond;
  integer z;
  wire [M-1:0] m1 = (st == S_SYN) ? gmul(pw, as_) : (st == S_DISC) ? gmul(L[i], ((rr + 1 >= i) && (rr + 1 - i >= 1) && (rr + 1 - i <= 2*T)) ? S[rr + 1 - i] : {{M{{1'b0}}}})
                    : (st == S_UPD) ? gmul(gam, L[i]) : gmul(v, beta);
  wire [M-1:0] m2 = gmul(del, (i == 0) ? {{M{{1'b0}}}} : B[i - 1]);
  wire [M-1:0] sq = gmul(S[j], S[j]);
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (rst) begin
      st <= S_IDLE; done <= 0; ok <= 0; dout <= 0; dout_valid <= 0;
    end else begin
      dout_valid <= 0;
      case (st)
        S_IDLE: if (start) begin
          st <= S_LOADW; pos <= 0; j <= 0; hsh <= 0; done <= 0; ok <= 0;
        end
        S_LOADW: if (din_valid) begin
          w <= {{din, w[N-1:1]}}; pos <= pos + 1;
          if (pos == N - 1) begin st <= S_LOADH; pos <= 0; end
        end
        S_LOADH: if (hin_valid) begin
          hsh <= {{hsh[M-2:0], hin}}; pos <= pos + 1;
          if (pos == M - 1) begin
            S[2*j + 1] <= {{hsh[M-2:0], hin}}; pos <= 0; j <= j + 1;
            if (j == T - 1) begin st <= S_SYN; j <= 0; acc <= 0; pw <= 1; as_ <= ALPHA; end
          end
        end
        S_SYN: begin                              // S[2j+1] ^= sum_pos w[pos] alpha^(pos (2j+1))
          if (w[0]) acc <= acc ^ pw;
          pw <= m1; w <= {{w[0], w[N-1:1]}}; pos <= pos + 1;
          if (pos == N - 1) begin
            S[2*j + 1] <= S[2*j + 1] ^ acc ^ (w[0] ? pw : {{M{{1'b0}}}});
            pos <= 0; acc <= 0; pw <= 1; as_ <= gmul(as_, ALPHA2); j <= j + 1;
            if (j == T - 1) begin st <= S_EVEN; j <= 1; end
          end
        end
        S_EVEN: begin                             // S[2j] = S[j]^2
          S[2*j] <= sq; j <= j + 1;
          if (j == T) begin
            st <= S_DISC; rr <= 0; i <= 0; del <= 0; k <= 0; gam <= 1;
            for (z = 0; z <= T; z = z + 1) begin L[z] <= (z == 0); B[z] <= (z == 0); end
          end
        end
        S_DISC: begin                             // discrepancy: sum_i L[i] S[rr+1-i]
          del <= del ^ m1; i <= i + 1;
          if (i == T) begin st <= S_UPD; i <= T; cond <= 0; end
        end
        S_UPD: begin                              // L = gam L - del x B; B = cond ? L : x B (i from T down to 0)
          if (i == T) cond <= (del != 0) && (2 * k <= rr);
          L[i] <= m1 ^ m2;
          if (((i == T) ? ((del != 0) && (2 * k <= rr)) : cond)) B[i] <= L[i]; else B[i] <= (i == 0) ? {{M{{1'b0}}}} : B[i - 1];
          if (i == 0) begin
            if (cond || ((T == 0) && (del != 0) && (2 * k <= rr))) begin k <= rr + 1 - k; gam <= del; end
            if (rr == 2*T - 1) begin st <= S_CH1; pos <= 0; i <= T; cnt <= 0; beta <= 1; v <= L[T]; end
            else begin st <= S_DISC; rr <= rr + 1; i <= 0; del <= 0; end
          end else i <= i - 1;
        end
        S_CH1, S_CH2: begin                       // Horner: v = L(beta), beta = alpha^-pos
          if (i != 0) begin
            v <= m1 ^ L[i - 1]; i <= i - 1;
          end else begin
            if (st == S_CH1) cnt <= cnt + (v == 0);
            else w <= {{w[0] ^ (v == 0), w[N-1:1]}};
            beta <= gmul(beta, ALPHA_INV); i <= T; v <= L[T]; pos <= pos + 1;
            if (pos == N - 1) begin
              pos <= 0; beta <= 1;
              if (st == S_CH2) st <= S_OUT;
              else if ((k <= T) && (cnt + (v == 0) == k)) begin st <= S_CH2; ok <= 1; end
              else st <= S_OUT;
            end
          end
        end
        S_OUT: begin
          dout <= w[0]; dout_valid <= 1; w <= {{w[0], w[N-1:1]}}; pos <= pos + 1;
          if (pos == N - 1) st <= S_DONE;
        end
        S_DONE: begin done <= 1; st <= S_IDLE; end
        default: st <= S_IDLE;
      endcase
    end
  end
endmodule
"""
    if r > 1:
        vote = f"""
// Repetition voter (r = {r}): the cells arrive with their helper bit (0 for the first cell of a group); the majority of
// cell xor helper over each group is the group's value.
module rep_vote (input wire clk, input wire rst, input wire cin, input wire rin, input wire cin_valid,
                 output reg gout, output reg gout_valid);
  localparam R = {r};
  reg [{W_R}:0] c, ones;
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (rst) begin c <= 0; ones <= 0; gout_valid <= 0; end
    else begin
      gout_valid <= 0;
      if (cin_valid) begin
        if (c == R - 1) begin
          gout <= (ones + (cin ^ rin)) > (R / 2); gout_valid <= 1; c <= 0; ones <= 0;
        end else begin c <= c + 1; ones <= ones + (cin ^ rin); end
      end
    end
  end
endmodule
"""
        top = """
module keygen_rec (input wire clk, input wire rst, input wire start, input wire cin, input wire rin, input wire cmask,
                   input wire cin_valid, input wire hin, input wire hin_valid, output wire dout, output wire dout_valid,
                   output wire done, output wire ok);
  wire g, gv;                                   // cmask = 0: a cell discarded at enrolment, skipped
  rep_vote u_vote (.clk(clk), .rst(rst), .cin(cin), .rin(rin), .cin_valid(cin_valid & cmask), .gout(g), .gout_valid(gv));
  bch_rec u_bch (.clk(clk), .rst(rst), .start(start), .din(g), .din_valid(gv), .hin(hin), .hin_valid(hin_valid),
                 .dout(dout), .dout_valid(dout_valid), .done(done), .ok(ok));
endmodule
"""
    else:
        vote = ""
        top = """
module keygen_rec (input wire clk, input wire rst, input wire start, input wire cin, input wire rin, input wire cmask,
                   input wire cin_valid, input wire hin, input wire hin_valid, output wire dout, output wire dout_valid,
                   output wire done, output wire ok);
  bch_rec u_bch (.clk(clk), .rst(rst), .start(start), .din(cin), .din_valid(cin_valid & cmask), .hin(hin), .hin_valid(hin_valid),
                 .dout(dout), .dout_valid(dout_valid), .done(done), .ok(ok));
endmodule
"""
    path = os.path.join(outdir, "keygen_rec.v")
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        f.write(bch + vote + top)
    return [path]


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 3. simulation
def _tb(cfg, ntests, nc):
    n, t, r = cfg["n"], cfg["t"], cfg["r"]
    nh = M * t
    return f"""`timescale 1ns/1ps
module tb;
  reg clk = 0, rst = 1, start = 0, cin = 0, rin = 0, cmask = 1, cin_valid = 0, hin = 0, hin_valid = 0;
  wire dout, dout_valid, done, ok;
  keygen_rec dut (.clk(clk), .rst(rst), .start(start), .cin(cin), .rin(rin), .cmask(cmask), .cin_valid(cin_valid), .hin(hin),
                  .hin_valid(hin_valid), .dout(dout), .dout_valid(dout_valid), .done(done), .ok(ok));
  always #50 clk = ~clk;
  reg [{nc - 1}:0] C [0:{ntests - 1}];
  reg [{nc - 1}:0] RH [0:{ntests - 1}];
  reg [{nc - 1}:0] MK [0:{ntests - 1}];
  reg [{nh - 1}:0] H [0:{ntests - 1}];
  integer k, q, fo, cyc;
  initial begin
    $readmemb("cells.mem", C); $readmemb("rhelp.mem", RH); $readmemb("mask.mem", MK); $readmemb("bhelp.mem", H);
    fo = $fopen("out.txt", "w");
    repeat (3) @(posedge clk); rst = 0;
    for (k = 0; k < {ntests}; k = k + 1) begin
      @(negedge clk) start = 1; @(negedge clk) start = 0;
      for (q = 0; q < {nc}; q = q + 1) begin
        @(negedge clk) begin cin = C[k][q]; rin = RH[k][q]; cmask = MK[k][q]; cin_valid = 1; end
      end
      @(negedge clk) cin_valid = 0;
      repeat (3) @(negedge clk);
      for (q = 0; q < {nh}; q = q + 1) begin
        @(negedge clk) begin hin = H[k][{nh - 1} - q]; hin_valid = 1; end
      end
      @(negedge clk) hin_valid = 0;
      cyc = 0;
      while (!done) begin @(posedge clk); cyc = cyc + 1; if (dout_valid) $fwrite(fo, "%b", dout); end
      $fwrite(fo, " %0d %0d\\n", ok, cyc);
    end
    $fclose(fo); $finish;
  end
endmodule
"""


def simulate(cfg, outdir, tests, iverilog, vvp, timeout=1800):
    """tests: list of dict(cells=0/1 array of the array's read cells, mask=0/1 array (1: kept at enrolment; default all 1),
    rhelp=0/1 array (0 at each group's first kept cell), bhelp=0/1 array of 10t BCH helper bits); all tests use arrays of
    the same length. Returns a list of dict(bits=n corrected group values, ok, cycles)."""
    files = emit_verilog(cfg, outdir)
    nc = len(tests[0]["cells"])
    with open(os.path.join(outdir, "tb.v"), "w") as f:
        f.write(_tb(cfg, len(tests), nc))
    for name, key in (("cells.mem", "cells"), ("rhelp.mem", "rhelp"), ("mask.mem", "mask"), ("bhelp.mem", "bhelp")):
        with open(os.path.join(outdir, name), "w") as f:
            for tst in tests:
                b = np.asarray(tst.get(key, np.ones(nc, np.uint8)), np.uint8)
                f.write("".join("1" if x else "0" for x in (b[::-1] if key != "bhelp" else b)) + "\n")
    subprocess.run([iverilog, "-g2012", "-o", "sim.vvp", "tb.v"] + [os.path.abspath(p) for p in files], cwd=outdir,
                   check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
    subprocess.run([vvp, "-n", "sim.vvp"], cwd=outdir, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
    out = []
    for line in open(os.path.join(outdir, "out.txt")):
        bits, ok, cyc = line.split()
        out.append(dict(bits=np.array([int(c) for c in bits], np.uint8), ok=bool(int(ok)), cycles=int(cyc)))
    return out
```

    Overwriting keygen.py


### A. Steps 1 and 2: specification and design-space search

**Goal.** For each of three specifications, find for every repetition factor the smallest PUF array and the weakest BCH code that keep the key-failure probability below the target at every corner and temperature while leaving at least 192 secret bits at the 95 % lower bound of the min-entropy, the bounded budget of the hand design (Section VII-E).

**Theory.** *The code.* The compiler uses a concatenated code. The $N = n\,r$ enrolled cells form $n$ groups of $r$ cells ($r$ odd). The inner code is a repetition code: a group's enrolled value is its first cell, the helper data hold the other $r - 1$ cells XOR the first, and reconstruction takes the majority of the group. The outer code is a BCH code of length $n$ over GF($2^m$), $m$ = 10 (so $n$ ≤ 1023), that corrects up to $t$ wrong group values; its helper data are $t$ syndromes of $m$ bits each. For $r$ = 1 this is the model's fuzzy extractor.

*Cell errors.* Cell $i$ of a chip has a mismatch $\delta_i$, in units of the mismatch spread of the cell model (Section VIII-F), and an enrolled value $w_i$ (one power-up at 25 °C). At temperature $T$ it powers up to the other value with probability

$$p_i(T) = \Phi\big(-\delta_i / s(T)\big)\ \text{if}\ w_i = 1,\qquad p_i(T) = \Phi\big(\delta_i / s(T)\big)\ \text{if}\ w_i = 0,$$

where $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function and $s(T)$ the effective noise-to-mismatch ratio of the corner, anchored to its SPICE Monte Carlo (Section VII-F): one fit for the single 25 °C enrolment, another for the cells kept by the two-temperature enrolment.

*Key failure.* A group is wrong when more than $r/2$ of its cells are wrong; its probability $q_g$ follows exactly from the $p_i$ of its cells. The key fails when more than $t$ groups are wrong:

$$P_{\text{fail}}(n, r, t) = \max_{\text{corner},\ T}\ \Pr\Big[\sum_g E_g > t\Big],$$

with $E_g$ independent Bernoulli($q_g$) events, summed exactly (Poisson-binomial distribution). $s(T)$ is interpolated linearly between the simulated temperatures (−40, 25 and 85 °C), and the failure probability grows with $s$, so the worst case over 0–85 °C lies at 0, 25 or 85 °C, the three temperatures evaluated.

*Secrecy.* With $b$ the probability that a cell powers up to 1, each cell carries a min-entropy $h = -\log_2 \max(b, 1-b)$, taken at its 95 % lower bound from the 1,024-cell post-layout Monte Carlo (Section VII-E), and the helper data publish $r - 1$ bits per group and $m\,t$ bits in all. The secret bits left are

$$H = \big\lfloor n\,\big(r\,h - (r - 1)\big) - m\,t \big\rfloor \ \ge 192 ,$$

the 128 bits of the key plus $2\log_2(1/\varepsilon)$ = 64 bits for a key within statistical distance $\varepsilon = 2^{-32}$ of uniform after the hash (leftover-hash lemma), the same budget as for the hand design.

*Search.* For each $r \in \{1, 3, 5, 7\}$, $n$ starts at the smallest value that could hold 192 secret bits and grows in steps of 32 until some $t$ meets both conditions, then is refined downwards in steps of 4; the smallest such $t$ is kept. The physical array is $\lceil n r / \kappa \rceil$ cells, where $\kappa$ is the fraction of cells the enrolment keeps (1 for a single 25 °C enrolment; the worst corner's fraction for the two-temperature enrolment).

*Intuition and prediction.* For small cell error probabilities, a majority of $r$ cells fails far less often than one cell, so a larger $r$ allows a much smaller $t$, at the cost of $r$ times more cells and $r - 1$ published bits per group. Reproducible flips are different: at the fast-nMOS corner fs they make 27.8 % of the bits wrong at 85 °C (Section VII-F), so many that a majority of up to seven cells still errs often, and a BCH code that corrects the remaining wrong groups publishes more helper data than the cells hold secret. The prediction, from Section VIII-F, is that with a 25 °C enrolment no code meets the target at every corner, and that the two-temperature enrolment, which discards the flipping cells, does, with a weaker code.

*Assumptions.* As in Section VIII-F, part 2, the reproducible flips are represented by a larger random noise $s(T)$ that reproduces the simulated error rate of each corner (SPICE Monte Carlo), but not the fact that the same cells are wrong at every hot power-up. The cells err independently; the per-cell probabilities are those of one simulated chip per corner (the model's chip seed) with one enrolment read; the PUF corners cover process and temperature, not supply voltage.

**Setup.** Behavioural level: exact probabilities from the cell models anchored to the transistor-level Monte Carlo of Section VII-F (no further sampling). The three specifications differ only in the corners and the enrolment:

| Specification | Corners | Enrolment |
|---|---|---|
| A | tt | one read at 25 °C |
| B | tt, ss, ff, sf, fs | one read at 25 °C |
| C | tt, ss, ff, sf, fs | at 25 and 85 °C, keeping the cells that are stable and equal at both (Section VII-F) |

Common to all: key failure below 10<sup>−6</sup> per power-up from 0 to 85 °C, at least 192 secret bits at the 95 % lower bound of the min-entropy, $r \in \{1, 3, 5, 7\}$, $n$ ≤ 1023, and the cell bias $b$ of the post-layout Monte Carlo (Section VII-D).

### B. Step 3: Verilog generation, synthesis and selection

**Goal.** Turn the feasible designs of step 2 into hardware and select, for each specification, the one with the smallest total area, decoder plus PUF array.

**Setup.**

* *Generated hardware (RTL).* For a configuration $(r, n, t)$ the compiler writes synthesisable Verilog: a serial repetition voter (`rep_vote`) and a serial BCH($n$, $t$) reconstruction unit (`bch_rec`) over GF(2<sup>10</sup>) with the primitive polynomial $x^{10} + x^3 + 1$ of the model. The decoder is serial, one operation per clock, with a combinational shift-and-add multiplier over GF(2<sup>10</sup>). It loads the $n$ group values and the $10t$ helper bits; computes the $t$ odd syndromes of the received word, one pass of $n$ clocks each, and adds the helper data to them; obtains the even syndromes by squaring; runs $2t$ iterations of the inversionless Berlekamp-Massey algorithm, each with a discrepancy and an update over the $t + 1$ coefficients; and evaluates the error locator by Horner's rule at every position in two Chien-search passes. The first pass counts the roots; the second corrects the word only if the count equals the degree of the locator, and otherwise the unit reports failure (`ok` = 0). The voter adds, over each group of $r$ cells, the cell XOR its helper bit and outputs the majority. The top level (`keygen_rec`) adds a mask input that skips the cells discarded at enrolment.
* *Ranking estimate.* Synthesis is the slow step, so an estimate ranks the feasible designs first: $A_{\text{est}} = 50\ \mu\text{m}^2 \times F_{\text{est}} + N_{\text{cells}}\,A_{\text{cell}}$, with $F_{\text{est}} = n + 20\,t + 20\,(t + 1) + 50$ the decoder's storage in flip-flops (the word, $2t$ syndromes and two locator polynomials of $t + 1$ coefficients, 10 bits each, plus 50 for control). The 50 µm² per flip-flop, including its share of the logic, is an assumption read from the synthesised designs; $A_{\text{cell}}$ is the area of the SRAM cell drawn in Section VII-D.
* *Synthesis and selection.* The two candidates with the smallest estimate in each specification are synthesised with Yosys onto `sky130_fd_sc_hd` (as in Section X-B). The selected design is the smallest *synthesised* total area; the others keep their estimate.
* *Latency:* the cycle count of one reconstruction from the compiler's formula, $n r + 10t + t n + t + 4t(t + 1) + 2n(t + 1) + n + 8$ (loading of the cells and the helper data, syndromes, Berlekamp-Massey, two Chien passes, output), at 10 MHz.
* *Metrics:* for each specification and $r$: groups $n$, $t$, PUF cells, secret bits, $P_{\text{fail}}$, decoder area (GE) and flip-flops, total area, latency.

> **Next cell.** Runs steps 1 to 3 for the three specifications: 1. builds each corner's per-cell error model; 2. searches the design space for every repetition factor r; 3. ranks the feasible designs by the area estimate; 4. generates and synthesises the two most promising of each specification; 5. selects the smallest synthesised total area; 6. prints the table and the card and draws the design space with the selected designs marked. Run time: about 40 s on two cores, mostly synthesis.


```python
#@title Fig.: key-generator compiler
# Steps 1 to 3 of the compiler: three specifications, the design-space search with the corner models of Section
# VII-F, and the generation and synthesis of the most promising designs; the smallest total area (decoder + PUF array) wins
import importlib, keygen as KG, puf_layout as pl
importlib.reload(KG)
t0 = time.time()
_ce = {}
def cell_err_for(enrol):
    """Per-cell error probabilities of N enrolled (kept) cells at temperature T, from each corner's anchored cell model."""
    def f(corner, N, T):
        if (corner, N, enrol) not in _ce:
            q = PUF_SYS[corner]; s = q["s%d" % enrol]
            puf = SRAMPUF(DEFAULTS["chip_seed"], N, s(25), float(ndtr(q["mu"])), 0.0)
            _ce[corner, N, enrol] = (puf, puf.read(25, rng_for(DEFAULTS["chip_seed"] * 7919 + 1)), s)
        puf, w, s = _ce[corner, N, enrol]
        return np.where(w == 1, ndtr(-puf.mismatch / s(T)), ndtr(puf.mismatch / s(T)))
    return f
ALL, KEEP = list(PUF_SYS), min(q["keep"] for q in PUF_SYS.values())
# Secrecy: the bounded budget of Section VII-E, the same as for the hand design: at least SECRET_REQ = 192 secret bits
# (128 + 2 log2(1/eps), eps = 2^-32, leftover-hash lemma) at the 95 % lower bound of the min-entropy per cell, given to the
# search as the equivalent bias max(P(1), 1 - P(1)) = 2^-h
BASE = dict(p_fail=1e-6, secret=SECRET_REQ, bias=2.0 ** -H_TT[0], temps=[0, 25, 85], r=(1, 3, 5, 7))   # s(T) is piecewise linear in T,
SPECS = {"A": ("typical corner, 25 °C enrolment", dict(BASE, corners=["tt"]), 1),                # so the worst case over 0-85 °C
         "B": ("all five corners, 25 °C enrolment", dict(BASE, corners=ALL), 1),                   # lies at 0, 25 or 85 °C
         "C": ("all five corners, enrolment at 25 and 85 °C", dict(BASE, corners=ALL, keep=KEEP), 2)}
CELL_UM2 = (lambda z: z["width_um"] * z["height_um"])(pl.cell_report(ps.CELL))       # the SRAM cell drawn in Section VII-D
# Synthesis is the slow step, so an estimate ranks the candidates first and only the two most promising of each specification
# are synthesised. The estimate counts the decoder's storage (the word, 2t syndromes and two locator polynomials of t + 1
# coefficients, 10 bits each) at about 50 µm² per flip-flop including its share of the logic, as the synthesised designs show.
EST_UM2_PER_FF = 50
est_ffs = lambda b: b["n"] + 20 * b["t"] + 20 * (b["t"] + 1) + 50
DSE, SYN = {}, {}
for key, (label, spec, enrol) in SPECS.items():
    DSE[key] = KG.design_keygen(spec, cell_err_for(enrol))
    feas = [b for b in DSE[key]["per_r"].values() if b]
    for b in feas:
        b.update(arr_um2=b["cells"] * CELL_UM2, cycles=KG.latency(b), est_um2=EST_UM2_PER_FF * est_ffs(b) + b["cells"] * CELL_UM2)
    for b in sorted(feas, key=lambda b: b["est_um2"])[:2]:                  # the two most promising: emit the Verilog, synthesise
        tag = (b["r"], b["n"], b["t"])
        if tag not in SYN:
            wd = WORK / "keygen" / ("r%d_n%d_t%d" % tag)
            SYN[tag] = R.synthesize(YOSYS, "keygen_rec", KG.emit_verilog(b, str(wd)), str(LIBERTY), str(wd),
                                    netlist=str(wd / "keygen_rec_netlist.v"))
        s = SYN[tag]
        b.update(dec_ge=s["ge"], dec_um2=s["area_um2"], ffs=s["ffs"], total_um2=s["area_um2"] + b["arr_um2"])
    synth = [b for b in feas if "total_um2" in b]
    DSE[key]["best"] = min(synth, key=lambda b: b["total_um2"]) if synth else None

rows_d = []
for key, (label, spec, enrol) in SPECS.items():
    for r, b in DSE[key]["per_r"].items():
        sel = b is not None and b is DSE[key]["best"]
        f = (lambda x: f"<b>{x}</b>") if sel else str
        syn = b is not None and "total_um2" in b
        rows_d.append((f"{key}. {label}" if r == spec["r"][0] else "", r) + (
            (f(b["n"]), f(b["t"]), f(b["cells"]), b["secret"], f"{b['p_fail']:.1e}",
             f"{b['dec_ge']:,.0f} / {b['ffs']:,}" if syn else "not synthesised",
             f(f"{b['total_um2'] / 1e3:.1f}") if syn else f"≈ {b['est_um2'] / 1e3:.0f} (estimate)", f"{b['cycles'] / 10e6 * 1e3:.1f}")
            if b else ("–", "–", "infeasible", "–", "–", "–", "–", "–")))
table(["Specification", "r", "Groups n", "t", "PUF cells", "Secret bits (95 % lower bound)", "P(key fails)", "Decoder (GE / FF)",
       "Total area (10<sup>3</sup> µm²)", "Latency (ms)"], rows_d,
      caption="Table XX: the compiler's design-space search for three specifications (key failure below 10<sup>−6</sup> from 0 to "
              f"85 °C, at least {SECRET_REQ} secret bits at the 95 % lower bound of the min-entropy): for each repetition factor r, the smallest array that meets the specification, "
              "its decoder synthesised on sky130_fd_sc_hd (the two most promising candidates of each specification, ranked by an "
              "estimate), and the total area with the SRAM cell of Section VII-D; bold: the design selected (smallest total area). PUF cells: the physical array, including the cells that a masked enrolment "
              "discards. Latency: one reconstruction at 10 MHz")
card("Key-generator compiler: design-space search and synthesis",
     [(f"{key}. {SPECS[key][0]}", (f"<b>r = {d['best']['r']}, {d['best']['n']} groups, t = {d['best']['t']}</b>: {d['best']['cells']} PUF cells, "
       f"decoder {d['best']['dec_ge']:,.0f} GE, {d['best']['cycles'] / 10e6 * 1e3:.1f} ms per reconstruction" if d["best"] else
       "<b>no design</b> with r ≤ 7 and n ≤ 1023 meets it")) for key, d in DSE.items()]
     + [("designs synthesised", f"{len(SYN)} (Yosys onto sky130_fd_sc_hd), {time.time() - t0:.0f} s in all")],
     tone="ok" if DSE["C"]["best"] else "bad")

fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(W2, 3.0))
rs = BASE["r"]; xs = np.arange(len(rs)); wdt = 0.26
STAR = dict(marker="*", ms=10, mfc=COL["yellow"], mec=COL["ink"], mew=0.6, ls="none")
for k, (key, c) in enumerate(zip(SPECS, (COL["ink"], COL["bad"], COL["ok"]))):
    v = [DSE[key]["per_r"][r]["cells"] if DSE[key]["per_r"][r] else 0 for r in rs]
    axs[0].bar(xs + (k - 1) * wdt, v, wdt, color=c, ec=COL["ink"], lw=0.4, label=key)
    for x, b in zip(xs, (DSE[key]["per_r"][r] for r in rs)):
        if not b:
            axs[0].text(x + (k - 1) * wdt, 20, "×", ha="center", va="bottom", color=c, fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
        elif b is DSE[key]["best"]:                                     # the design the compiler selects
            axs[0].plot(x + (k - 1) * wdt, b["cells"] + 70, **STAR)
axs[0].plot([], [], label="selected", **STAR)
axs[0].set_xticks(xs, [f"$r$ = {r}" for r in rs]); axs[0].set_ylabel("PUF cells")
axs[0].set_ylim(0, 1.12 * max(b["cells"] for d in DSE.values() for b in d["per_r"].values() if b))
axs[0].legend(fontsize=7.5, loc="upper left", title="specification", title_fontsize=7.5)
axs[0].grid(axis="x", visible=False); panel(axs[0], "a", "array size (×: no design)")
for k, (key, c) in enumerate(zip(("A", "C"), (COL["ink"], COL["ok"]))):
    for x, r in zip(xs, rs):
        b = DSE[key]["per_r"][r]
        if not b:
            continue
        syn = "dec_um2" in b
        dec = (b["dec_um2"] if syn else b["est_um2"] - b["arr_um2"]) / 1e3
        xb = x + (k - 0.5) * 0.36
        axs[1].bar(xb, dec, 0.34, color=c, ec=COL["ink"], lw=0.4, alpha=1 if syn else 0.4)
        axs[1].bar(xb, b["arr_um2"] / 1e3, 0.34, bottom=dec, color="white", ec=c, hatch="////", lw=0.6)
        if b is DSE[key]["best"]:
            axs[1].plot(xb, dec + b["arr_um2"] / 1e3 + 4, **STAR)
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
axs[1].legend(handles=[h for key, c in (("A", COL["ink"]), ("C", COL["ok"])) for h in
                       (Patch(fc=c, ec=COL["ink"], lw=0.4, label=f"{key}: decoder"),
                        Patch(fc="white", ec=c, hatch="////", lw=0.6, label=f"{key}: PUF array"))],
              fontsize=7, ncol=2, loc="upper right")
axs[1].set_xticks(xs, [f"$r$ = {r}" for r in rs]); axs[1].set_ylabel("Area (10$^3$ µm²)")
axs[1].set_ylim(0, 1.12 * axs[1].get_ylim()[1])
axs[1].grid(axis="x", visible=False); panel(axs[1], "b", "total area (faded decoder: estimate)")
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

<p align="center" style="text-align:center"><b>Fig. 60.</b> Key-generator compiler: design space. (a) PUF cells required for each repetition factor r, one bar per specification of Table XX (×: no design meets it). (b) Total area of the best design for each r, specifications A and C: decoder (solid where synthesised, faded where estimated) and PUF array (hatched). Stars: selected designs.</p>

**Result, step 2 (search; Table XX, Fig. 60(a)).**

* *Specification A* (tt, 25 °C enrolment) is feasible at every $r$. The smallest array is 611 cells at $r$ = 1 ($n$ = 611, $t$ = 36, 194 secret bits at the lower bound, $P_{\text{fail}}$ = 8.4 × 10<sup>−7</sup>); with repetition, 1,092 cells at $r$ = 3 ($t$ = 7), 2,075 at $r$ = 5 ($t$ = 3) and 3,990 at $r$ = 7 ($t$ = 1).
* *Specification B* (five corners, 25 °C enrolment) **is infeasible**: no design with $r$ ≤ 7 and $n$ ≤ 1023 meets it. The search reports the worst case over the corners and therefore does not identify the failing corner; the error rates of Section VII-F point to fs (27.8 % at 85 °C, of which 25.6 % are reproducible flips).
* *Specification C* (five corners, two-temperature enrolment) is feasible at every $r$: 636 cells at $r$ = 1 ($n$ = 443, $t$ = 21), 1,395 at $r$ = 3 ($n$ = 324, $t$ = 4), 2,690 at $r$ = 5 ($t$ = 1) and 5,723 at $r$ = 7 ($t$ = 1).

This is the predicted outcome. B fails, as Section VIII-F anticipated, and C needs a weaker code than A for $r$ ≤ 5 ($t$ = 21, 4 and 1 against 36, 7 and 3), although it covers five corners instead of one. C needs more physical cells than A at the same $r$, because its enrolment discards the cells that change between 25 and 85 °C. Compared with a criterion of 128 secret bits at the point estimate of the min-entropy, the bounded budget enlarges the arrays (C at $r$ = 3: 1,395 cells instead of 741; A at $r$ = 1: 611 instead of 441): each group of $r$ cells keeps only $r h - (r - 1)$ secret bits, which is small for $h$ close to its lower bound, so the repetition factor costs more cells than before.

**Result, step 3 (synthesis and selection; Table XX, Fig. 60(b)).** Four designs were synthesised: for A, $r$ = 3 (9,980 GE, 807 flip-flops, 50.7 × 10<sup>3</sup> µm² in total) and $r$ = 5 (8,567 GE, 696 flip-flops, 57.4 × 10<sup>3</sup> µm²); for C, $r$ = 3 (8,984 GE, 707 flip-flops, 50.7 × 10<sup>3</sup> µm²) and $r$ = 5 (7,467 GE, 572 flip-flops, 60.7 × 10<sup>3</sup> µm²). The selected designs, starred in Fig. 60, are $r$ = 3, 364 groups, $t$ = 7 for A (1,092 cells, 1.0 ms per reconstruction) and $r$ = 3, 324 groups, $t$ = 4 for C (1,395 cells, 0.6 ms). The candidates that were not synthesised (faded in Fig. 60(b)) are all estimated above the selected totals: about 113 and 82 × 10<sup>3</sup> µm² for A at $r$ = 1 and 7, and about 75 and 104 × 10<sup>3</sup> µm² for C at $r$ = 1 and 7, so the selection does not depend on the estimate's ranking.

**Interpretation.** The search turns the qualitative finding of Section VIII-F into the result of an exhaustive search, under the cell models, over the design space considered: with a 25 °C enrolment no concatenated code up to $r$ = 7 and $n$ = 1023 reaches 10<sup>−6</sup> at all five corners with 192 secret bits at the lower bound, and **the two-temperature enrolment is what makes a specification over all corners achievable**. The decoder is a large part of the hardware (Fig. 60(b)): the selected decoders (8,984–9,980 GE) are 2.9–3.3× the Grain-128a + MAC core of Section X written for one bit per clock (3,068 GE, without the counter, nonce and key registers of the complete block). The estimates without repetition ($r$ = 1, with $t$ = 36 and 21) indicate that the inner repetition code, by lowering $t$, keeps the decoders that small, while repetition beyond $r$ = 3 costs more in cells than it saves in decoder. Step 4 must now show that the generated decoder does exactly what the model assumes.

### C. Step 4: RTL verification of the generated decoder

**Goal.** Show that the generated Verilog reconstructs exactly what the model's fuzzy extractor reconstructs, including when the read has more errors than the code can correct, so that the failure probabilities of step 2 apply to the generated decoder and not only to the model's decoder; and measure how often a read beyond the code's capacity is miscorrected while the decoder reports success.

**Theory.** *Equivalence.* The hardware's inversionless Berlekamp-Massey algorithm produces an error locator that is a non-zero multiple of the model's; it has the same roots, and both decoders accept a read exactly when the locator's degree is at most $t$ and equals the number of its roots among the $n$ positions of the shortened code. The corrected bits and the success flag must therefore be identical in every test, whatever the number of errors.

*Miscorrection beyond t.* A read with more than $t$ errors cannot be corrected, but the decoder may still find a locator of degree $L \le t$ with all $L$ roots inside the shortened code and flag success with a wrong word. For a pattern far beyond $t$, the syndrome behaves like a random element of the $2^{mt}$ possible ones ($m$ = 10 for codes over GF(2¹⁰)), and the decoder accepts it when it equals the syndrome of one of the $\sum_{j \le t}\binom{n}{j}$ correctable patterns:

$$P_{\text{mis}} \approx \frac{\sum_{j=0}^{t}\binom{n}{j}}{2^{mt}}.$$

*Prediction.* About 16 % for $t$ = 1 and $n$ = 162 (every single-error syndrome points to one of 1,023 positions, 162 of which are in the code), about 4 × 10⁻⁴ for $t$ = 4 and $n$ = 324, about 10⁻⁷ for $t$ = 7 and $n$ = 364, and negligible for $t$ = 45 and $n$ = 600. A miscorrection does not change the key-failure probability of step 2, which counts every read beyond $t$ as a failure; it only means that the success flag does not detect the failure, so that the wrong key is first detected by the receiver, as a MAC failure of the first frame.

**Setup.**

* *Level:* RTL, the generated `keygen_rec` simulated with Icarus Verilog. A generated test bench (100 ns clock) reads all tests from memory files; for each test it pulses `start`, streams the physical cells with their repetition helper bits and mask bits, then the $10t$ BCH helper bits, and records the corrected word, the success flag `ok` and the number of clock cycles from the end of the helper-data input to `done`.
* *Designs:* the selected designs of specifications C and A.
* *RTL tests:* per design, 12 directed tests and 60 random ones, from generators seeded with 2027 and 77. Each draws a random enrolment mask (the fraction kept by the specification's enrolment), a random enrolled word and its helper data, and a read in which $k$ groups are corrupted (the majority of their cells flipped): in the directed tests $k$ cycles through 0, 1, about $t/2$, $t$, $t + 1$ and $t + 3$; in the random ones $k$ is uniform in 0 to $t + 4$. Other groups receive single-cell errors below the majority, which the vote must absorb.
* *Reference:* the function `reconstruct` of the model (Section V) on the same group values.
* *Random error patterns:* 4,000 per BCH code, at the level of the code word, on the model's decoder (which the RTL matches decision for decision; simulating thousands of reads in Icarus would cost minutes): a random enrolled word and an error pattern of weight $w$ at random positions, with $w$ from 0 to $t$ and up to six weights beyond $t$ ($t + 1$, $t + 2$, $t + 3$, $t + 5$, $2t + 1$ and $2t + 5$; five for $t$ = 1, where $2t + 1 = t + 2$), equally many each. Three codes: the BCH codes of the selected designs of C and A, and the BCH code of the hand design of Section VII-E.
* *Metrics:* reconstructions identical bit for bit and in the success flag; cases beyond the code's capacity; for the random patterns, the reads with weight ≤ $t$ that are corrected, and those beyond $t$ that are flagged as failures or miscorrected with the success flag set, against the prediction; clock cycles.

> **Next cell.** 1. Generates the Verilog of the selected designs of specifications C and A. 2. Builds 12 directed and 60 random test reads for each, with the fuzzy extractor of the model as reference. 3. Simulates them with Icarus Verilog. 4. Compares the corrected bits and the success flag. 5. Runs 4,000 random error patterns against each of three BCH codes on the model's decoder and counts corrections, flagged failures and miscorrections. 6. Prints the generated interface, the table and the card.


```python
#@title Key-generator compiler: verification
# Step 4: the generated Verilog of two selected designs, simulated with Icarus against the model's fuzzy extractor
# (reconstruct of Section V) on the same cell streams: 12 directed tests (k = 0, 1, t/2, t, t+1, t+3 corrupted
# groups) and N_RTL random ones per design; then a Monte Carlo of random error patterns at the BCH level, on the model's
# decoder (which the RTL matches decision for decision), that counts miscorrections beyond t flagged as success
N_RTL, N_MC = 60, 4000                   # random RTL tests per design; random error patterns per BCH code
def kg_tests(cfg, keep, ks, seed=2027):
    """Random enrolments and reads; for each k in ks, k groups corrupted (majority of their cells flipped), plus single-cell
    errors in other groups, which the majority must absorb. Returns the streams and the model's expectation."""
    r, n, t = cfg["r"], cfg["n"], cfg["t"]; rg = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    nk = n * r; nphys = int(np.ceil(nk / keep)); tests, expect = [], []
    for kk in ks:
        mask = np.zeros(nphys, np.uint8); mask[rg.choice(nphys, nk, replace=False)] = 1
        wk = rg.integers(0, 2, nk).astype(np.uint8); g = wk[0::r].copy(); rh = wk ^ np.repeat(g, r)
        h = bch_syndrome(g, t); rd = wk.copy()
        bad = rg.choice(n, min(kk, n), replace=False)
        for gi in range(n):
            cells_g = gi * r + rg.permutation(r)
            rd[cells_g[: (r + 1) // 2 if gi in bad else (r - 1) // 2 * int(rg.random() < 0.5)]] ^= 1
        cells = rg.integers(0, 2, nphys).astype(np.uint8); cells[mask == 1] = rd
        rhp = np.zeros(nphys, np.uint8); rhp[mask == 1] = rh
        gv = ((rd ^ rh).reshape(n, r).sum(axis=1) > r // 2).astype(np.uint8)
        res = reconstruct(gv, h, t)
        tests.append(dict(cells=cells, mask=mask, rhelp=rhp, bhelp=syn_to_bits(h)))
        expect.append((res["w"].astype(np.uint8), bool(res["ok"]), bool(np.array_equal(res["w"], g))))
    return tests, expect
t0, VER = time.time(), {}
for key in ("C", "A"):
    cfg = DSE[key]["best"]; t = cfg["t"]
    keep = SPECS[key][1].get("keep", 1.0)
    ks = [[0, 1, max(1, t // 2), t, t + 1, t + 3][j % 6] for j in range(12)] + list(np.random.default_rng(77).integers(0, t + 5, N_RTL))
    tests, expect = kg_tests(cfg, keep, ks)
    out = KG.simulate(cfg, str(WORK / "keygen" / f"verify_{key}"), tests, str(PNR_BIN / "iverilog"), str(PNR_BIN / "vvp"))
    same = [np.array_equal(o["bits"], e[0]) and o["ok"] == e[1] for o, e in zip(out, expect)]
    VER[key] = dict(match=sum(same[:12]), n=12, fails=sum(not e[1] for e in expect[:12]), cycles=max(o["cycles"] for o in out),
                    rmatch=sum(same[12:]), rn=len(same) - 12, rbeyond=sum(k > t for k in ks[12:]),
                    rmis=sum(o["ok"] and not e[2] for o, e in zip(out[12:], expect[12:])))
t_rtl = time.time() - t0

# Monte Carlo at the BCH level: a random enrolled word, a random error pattern of weight w at uniformly random positions
def bch_mc(n, t, weights, n_mc, seed):
    rg = np.random.default_rng(seed); res = {w: [0, 0, 0] for w in weights}      # [correct, failure flagged, miscorrected]
    for j in range(n_mc):
        w = weights[j % len(weights)]
        g = rg.integers(0, 2, n).astype(np.uint8); h = bch_syndrome(g, t); rd = g.copy()
        rd[rg.choice(n, w, replace=False)] ^= 1
        o = reconstruct(rd, h, t)
        res[w][0 if (o["ok"] and np.array_equal(o["w"], g)) else 1 if not o["ok"] else 2] += 1
    return res
from math import comb, log2
def p_mis_theory(n, t, m=10):          # a random syndrome beyond t: decodable patterns of the shortened code / all syndromes
    return sum(comb(n, j) for j in range(t + 1)) / 2.0 ** (m * t)
t1 = time.time()
MC_CODES = [(f"C (r = {DSE['C']['best']['r']})", DSE["C"]["best"]["n"], DSE["C"]["best"]["t"]),
            (f"A (r = {DSE['A']['best']['r']})", DSE["A"]["best"]["n"], DSE["A"]["best"]["t"]),
            ("hand design (Section VII-E)", PUF_BITS, DEFAULTS["bch_t"])]
MC = {}
for lab, n, t in MC_CODES:
    wts = list(range(0, t + 1)) + [t + 1, t + 2, t + 3, t + 5, 2 * t + 1, 2 * t + 5]
    wts = sorted(set(w for w in wts if w <= n))
    MC[lab] = (n, t, bch_mc(n, t, wts, N_MC, 4040 + n + t))
t_mc = time.time() - t1

src = open(WORK / "keygen" / "verify_C" / "keygen_rec.v").read().splitlines()
print(f"keygen_rec.v generated for specification C ({len(src)} lines of Verilog); its interface:")
print("\n".join(l for l in src if l.startswith("module") or l.lstrip().startswith(("input", "output")))[:900])
rows_mc = []
for lab, (n, t, res) in MC.items():
    le = [w for w in res if w <= t]; be = [w for w in res if w > t]
    ok_le = sum(res[w][0] for w in le); n_le = sum(sum(res[w]) for w in le)
    n_be = sum(sum(res[w]) for w in be); mis = sum(res[w][2] for w in be); det = sum(res[w][1] for w in be)
    rows_mc.append((lab, n, t, f"{ok_le:,}/{n_le:,}", f"{det:,}/{n_be:,}", f"<b>{mis:,}/{n_be:,}</b> ({100 * mis / n_be:.2g} %)" if mis else f"0/{n_be:,}",
                    f"{p_mis_theory(n, t):.1e}" if p_mis_theory(n, t) > 1e-30 else f"2<sup>{log2(p_mis_theory(n, t)):.0f}</sup>"))
table(["Code", "Length n", "t", "Weight ≤ t: corrected", "Weight > t: failure flagged", "Weight > t: miscorrected, success flagged",
       "Theory, random syndrome"], rows_mc,
      caption=f"Table XXI: random error patterns against the BCH decoder ({N_MC:,} per code, weights 0 to t and up to six weights beyond t, "
              "equally many each; model decoder, which the generated RTL matches decision for decision). Theory: the fraction of "
              "syndromes that the shortened code decodes, Σ<sub>j≤t</sub> C(n, j) / 2<sup>10t</sup>")
card("Generated key-reconstruction hardware: verification against the model",
     [(f"specification {key}: r = {DSE[key]['best']['r']}, n = {DSE[key]['best']['n']}, t = {DSE[key]['best']['t']}",
       f"directed: <b>{v['match']}/{v['n']}</b> identical to the model, bit for bit and in the success flag ({v['fails']} beyond the "
       f"code's capacity, correctly reported as failures); random: <b>{v['rmatch']}/{v['rn']}</b> identical ({v['rbeyond']} with more "
       f"than t corrupted groups, {v['rmis']} of them miscorrected with the success flag set, as in the model); "
       f"longest {v['cycles']:,} clock cycles after the helper data")
      for key, v in VER.items()]
     + [("random error patterns, model decoder (table above)", "; ".join(f"{r[0]}: {r[5]} miscorrected beyond t" for r in rows_mc).replace("<b>", "").replace("</b>", "")),
        ("run time", f"Icarus Verilog {t_rtl:.0f} s ({2 * (12 + N_RTL)} tests), Monte Carlo {t_mc:.0f} s")],
     tone="ok" if all(v["match"] == v["n"] and v["rmatch"] == v["rn"] for v in VER.values()) else "bad")
```

**Result.** The generated `keygen_rec.v` for specification C has 141 lines of Verilog; its interface is printed above. For specification C ($r$ = 3, $n$ = 324, $t$ = 4), **12/12 directed and 60/60 random reconstructions are identical to the model, bit for bit and in the success flag**; 4 of the directed tests are beyond the code's capacity and are correctly reported as failures, and 23 of the random ones have more than $t$ corrupted groups, none of them miscorrected with the success flag set; the longest reconstruction takes 4,946 clock cycles after the helper data. For specification A ($r$ = 3, $n$ = 364, $t$ = 7), 12/12 directed and 60/60 random reconstructions are identical; 20 random reads exceed $t$, again with no miscorrection; the longest takes 8,969 cycles. This is the predicted exact agreement. The cycle counts also confirm the latency formula of Subsection B: without its loading terms ($n r + 10t$), the formula gives 4,952 and 8,975 cycles, within 6 cycles of the simulated 4,946 and 8,969. The latencies of Table XX (0.6 and 1.0 ms at 10 MHz) include the loading of the cells and the helper data; the test bench excludes it, and with a masked enrolment the physical array (1,395 cells for C) is streamed instead of the $n r$ kept cells.

The random error patterns (Table XXI) confirm the prediction for miscorrection. Every pattern of weight up to $t$ is corrected (2,000/2,000 for C, 2,288/2,288 for A, 3,542/3,542 for the hand design). Beyond $t$, every read is flagged as a failure: none of 2,000 for C (4.2 × 10⁻⁴ predicted per read, about one expected), none of 1,712 for A (1.4 × 10⁻⁷ predicted) and none of 458 for the hand design ($t$ = 45, $n$ = 600) is miscorrected with the success flag set.

**Interpretation.** The generated RTL makes the same decisions as the model, including the decision to report failure, on 144 simulated reads of the two designs; the key-failure probabilities of step 2 therefore apply to the generated decoder, under the cell models. With $t$ = 4 and 7, a read beyond the code's capacity is almost always flagged, so the success flag is a useful failure detector for both selected designs (a retry of the power-up read on a failed flag would be sound); for a code with $t$ = 1 and $n$ = 162, a random syndrome is decoded with a probability of 163/1024, about 1/6, so the flag would not be. A wrong key that escapes the flag is still detected by the receiver, when the first frame's MAC fails. Step 5 carries the selected design of specification C to a layout.

### D. Step 5: place and route

**Goal.** Carry the selected design of specification C from its synthesised netlist to a layout, with the same flow and sign-off checks as the keystream block of Section X-C, so that the specification ends in GDS.

**Setup.** The flow, parameters and corner are those of Section X-C, steps 1–5 (target core utilisation 25 %, placement density 0.35, 100 ns clock, routing on met1–met5, antenna margin 20 %, tt, 25 °C, 1.8 V). In both modes the timing is computed after global routing, with parasitics estimated from the global routes. No gate-level simulation or power analysis is run for this unit. What runs live and what is recorded:

| Part of the flow | Default (`ROUTE_COMPILED = False`) | `ROUTE_COMPILED = True` |
|---|---|---|
| Netlist preparation, floorplan, placement, clock tree, global routing (OpenROAD) | live | live |
| Timing at 10 MHz | live, with global-routing parasitics | live |
| GDS (KLayout) | live, placed design | live, routed design |
| Detailed routing (TritonRoute), routing DRC, antenna check | recorded | live |
| Magic DRC of the routed GDS | recorded | live |

The recorded values come from `dev/rtl/compiled_unit_routed.json`, a run of the same flow on the same design ($r$ = 3, $n$ = 324, $t$ = 4) that took 424 s (about 7 min) on two cores (`dev/rtl/record_compiled_unit.py`), with an antenna margin of 60 % and the input ports buffered at their pins, the settings that the cell also uses; the default margin of 20 % and the margin of 60 % without buffering each left 2 antenna violations as well. The cell checks that the recorded design is the one this session selected, and says so on the card if it is not. Metrics: die size and instances, setup and hold slack, routing DRC and antenna violations, Magic DRC violations.

> **Next cell.** 1. Prepares the selected design of specification C and runs OpenROAD live: floorplan, placement, clock tree, global routing and timing (about 10 s). 2. With `ROUTE_COMPILED = False` (default), takes the detailed routing, its routing-DRC and antenna counts and the Magic DRC from the recorded run of the same flow (`dev/rtl/compiled_unit_routed.json`); with `True`, runs them live (415 s on two cores in the recorded run). 3. Writes the GDS of the placed (or routed) unit with KLayout and prints the card, saying which values are recorded.


```python
#@title Fig.: compiled key-reconstruction unit
# Step 5 for the selected design of specification C: from the synthesised netlist to a placed (by default) or routed and
# DRC-checked layout (the flow of Section X), so that the specification ends in GDS. Placement, clock tree, global
# routing and timing run live in seconds; the detailed routing of this ~14,000-instance design takes about 7 minutes on Colab's
# two cores, so by default its sign-off is shown from the recorded run of the same flow (dev/rtl/compiled_unit_routed.json)
ROUTE_COMPILED = False                  #@param {type:"boolean"}
KG_ROUTED = json.loads('{"seconds": 362.9, "area_um2": 40157.0, "utilization": 30.0, "slack_setup_ns": 89.93130761294383, "slack_hold_ns": 0.39853194095078837, "instances": 18492, "die_um": [379.39, 379.39], "route_drc": 0, "antenna_violations": 2, "diodes": 4, "fillers": 13464, "clock_buffers": null, "magic_drc": 0, "design": "r3_n324_t4", "antenna_margin": 60, "buffer_inputs": true, "total_seconds": 424, "cores": 2, "command": "taskset -c 0,1 python dev/rtl/record_compiled_unit.py r3_n324_t4 (or ROUTE_COMPILED = True in the cell)"}')
t0 = time.time()
cfg = DSE["C"]["best"]; tag = "r%d_n%d_t%d" % (cfg["r"], cfg["n"], cfg["t"]); wd = WORK / "keygen" / tag
net_k = PR.prep(YOSYS, wd / "keygen_rec_netlist.v", LIBERTY, "keygen_rec", str(wd / "pnr"))
run_k = PR.place_and_route(str(OPENROAD), PDK_ROOT, net_k, "keygen_rec", str(wd / "pnr"), route=ROUTE_COMPILED,
                           antenna_margin=KG_ROUTED.get("antenna_margin", 20),   # the settings of the recorded run
                           buffer_inputs=KG_ROUTED.get("buffer_inputs", False))
GDS_K = PR.to_gds(PDK_ROOT, run_k["def"], str(wd / "pnr" / "keygen.gds"))
if ROUTE_COMPILED:
    drc_k = sl.drc(sl.tool_config(str(PDK_ROOT), magic=str(MAGIC), netgen=str(NETGEN), workdir=str(wd / "pnr")), GDS_K, "keygen_rec")
    sign = dict(route_drc=run_k["route_drc"], antenna_violations=run_k["antenna_violations"], magic_drc=drc_k["count"], src="this run")
else:
    same = KG_ROUTED["design"] == tag
    sign = dict(KG_ROUTED, src=(f"recorded run of the same design, {KG_ROUTED['total_seconds'] / 60:.0f} min on two cores; "
                                "<code>ROUTE_COMPILED = True</code> re-runs it" if same else
                                f"recorded run of {KG_ROUTED['design']} (this session selected {tag}): set <code>ROUTE_COMPILED = True</code>"))
ok_k = sign["magic_drc"] == 0 and sign["route_drc"] == 0 and sign["antenna_violations"] == 0
card("Compiled key-reconstruction unit (specification C) in SKY130: " + ("placed, routed and checked" if ROUTE_COMPILED else
     "placed and globally routed live; detailed routing and DRC recorded"),
     [("design", f"r = {cfg['r']}, {cfg['n']} groups, t = {cfg['t']}: {SYN[cfg['r'], cfg['n'], cfg['t']]['ge']:,.0f} GE, "
                 f"{SYN[cfg['r'], cfg['n'], cfg['t']]['ffs']:,} flip-flops"),
      ("die / standard cells", f"{run_k['die_um'][0]:.0f} × {run_k['die_um'][1]:.0f} µm, {run_k['instances']:,} instances"),
      ("timing at 10 MHz (tt, 25 °C, 1.8 V; global-routing parasitics)", f"setup slack <b>{run_k['slack_setup_ns']:+.1f} ns</b>, "
       f"hold slack <b>{run_k['slack_hold_ns']:+.2f} ns</b>"),
      (f"detailed routing ({sign['src']})", f"<b>{sign['route_drc']} DRC violations</b>, <b>{sign['antenna_violations']} antenna violations</b>"),
      ("DRC of the routed GDS (Magic, full SKY130 deck)", f"<b>{sign['magic_drc']} violations</b>"),
      ("GDS of this session (KLayout)", f"{'routed' if ROUTE_COMPILED else 'placed'} design, <code>{str(GDS_K).rsplit('/', 1)[-1]}</code> (<code>GDS_K</code>); "
                                        "<code>kl_window({'unit': kl_view(GDS_K)})</code> opens it in the layout viewer"),
      ("run time", f"{time.time() - t0:.0f} s")], tone="ok" if ok_k else "bad")

# drawn like the keystream block's placement: standard cells and power stripes only (no signal routing), with a scale bar
V_K = kl_view(GDS_K); kl_size(V_K, 760, 760)
V_K.set_config("grid-show-ruler", "false")                                     # the figure draws its own 50 µm bar
for name, _, it in kl_layers(V_K):
    it.current().visible = name in {"nwell.drawing", "diff.drawing", "tap.drawing", "poly.drawing", "met4.drawing"}
img = plt.imread(io.BytesIO(kl_png(V_K)), format="png"); vb = V_K.box()          # vb: the visible box, in µm
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(W1, W1 + 0.15))
ax.imshow(img); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([]); ax.grid(False)
px_um, hgt = img.shape[1] / vb.width(), img.shape[0]
x0, y0 = 0.06 * img.shape[1], 0.95 * hgt
ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((x0 - 0.02 * hgt, y0 - 0.085 * hgt), 50 * px_um + 0.04 * hgt, 0.11 * hgt, color="white", alpha=0.9, lw=0))
ax.plot([x0, x0 + 50 * px_um], [y0, y0], color=COL["ink"], lw=2.5, solid_capstyle="butt")
ax.text(x0 + 25 * px_um, y0 - 0.02 * hgt, "50 µm", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8.5, color=COL["ink"])
ax.set_title(("Routed" if ROUTE_COMPILED else "Placement") + f", {run_k['die_um'][0]:.0f} × {run_k['die_um'][1]:.0f} µm", fontsize=10)
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```
